definition_zh: 分配；配置；分摊；拨款；名额
definition_en: the act of deciding how resources, tasks or money are shared out
core_image: 一张大饼被切成若干份，每份旁边都写着用途
scene: 项目组把有限的经费摊在桌上，按优先次序分给三个小组。 The committee agreed on an allocation of funds to three research teams.
sceneCN: 项目组把有限经费摊在桌上，按优先次序分给三个小组；句中的 allocation 指「把资源按用途分给各方的行为」（第 1 个义项：把资源分开并派给不同对象）。图中可辨识物件：摊开的预算表、三只信封、计算器、白板。

pos.zh: 分配；配置；分摊；拨款；名额

senses.title: The act of sharing out resources
senses.titleCN: 把资源分给各方的行为
senses.definition: the act of dividing something among several users or purposes
senses.definitionCN: 把某物在多个使用者或用途之间分开的行为
senses.example: The committee agreed on an allocation of funds to three research teams.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会同意把经费分配给三个研究团队。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to place something somewhere, so allocation is literally placing each part where it goes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为把某物放到某处，因此 allocation 字面上就是把每一份放到它该去的地方。

senses.title: Resource allocation in economics
senses.definition: the way an economy decides which goods and services get produced and who gets them
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体决定生产哪些商品与服务、由谁获得的方式
senses.example: Efficient resource allocation is the central question of the course.
senses.exampleCN: 有效的资源配置是这门课的核心问题。
senses.why: Economics studies who gets what, and placing each part is exactly what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 经济学研究谁得到什么，而「把每一份放好」正是这个词所描述的。

senses.title: A budget line or grant
senses.definition: a sum of money set aside for a particular department or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某部门或某用途专门留出的款项
senses.example: The library's allocation rose by five per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆的拨款增加了百分之五。
senses.why: A grant is money placed at a destination, so the word shifts from the act to the sum assigned.
senses.whyCN: 拨款就是把钱放到某个去处，因此词义从动作转到被指派的款额。

senses.title: Assigning duties to people
senses.definition: the assignment of jobs or responsibilities to particular people
senses.definitionCN: 把工作或责任分给具体的人
senses.example: A clear allocation of duties prevented two people editing the same page.
senses.exampleCN: 明确分派职责，避免了两人重复编辑同一页。
senses.why: Tasks are placed on people's desks, which extends the placing image from things to duties.
senses.whyCN: 任务被放到各人的桌上，这把「安放」的意象从物品扩展到职责。

senses.title: A share of limited places
senses.definition: the distribution of limited places such as seats or school positions
senses.definitionCN: 座位、学位等有限名额的分发
senses.example: The allocation of school places followed a new formula.
senses.exampleCN: 学位名额按新公式分配。
senses.why: When places are scarce, sharing them out becomes a visible decision with rules.
senses.whyCN: 当名额稀缺，如何分发就成了一件有规则、看得见的决定。

senses.title: Memory allocation in computing
senses.definition: the process by which a program reserves memory for data
senses.definitionCN: 程序为数据预留内存的过程
senses.example: A memory allocation error crashed the program.
senses.exampleCN: 一次内存分配错误让程序崩溃。
senses.why: Computing reused the word because memory, like money, is a finite store that must be handed out.
senses.whyCN: 计算机沿用这个词，因为内存和钱一样是有限存量，必须逐一派给。

senses.title: Cost allocation in accounting
senses.definition: the assignment of shared costs to the activities or products that caused them
senses.definitionCN: 把共同成本分给造成这些成本的业务或产品
senses.example: Cost allocation put half the warehouse bill on the online orders.
senses.exampleCN: 成本分摊把一半仓储费算到了网络订单上。
senses.why: Accounting places each cost on a product, which is the same gesture applied to figures.
senses.whyCN: 会计把每笔成本放到某个产品上，是同一动作用在数字上。

senses.title: Rationing in times of shortage
senses.definition: the controlled distribution of scarce goods to users, often by quota
senses.definitionCN: 按配额把稀缺物资受控地分给使用者
senses.example: Wartime allocation of sugar limited each household to a small weekly amount.
senses.exampleCN: 战时的食糖配给把每户每周限制在少量。
senses.why: Rationing is sharing out under pressure, so the word takes on the tone of scarcity.
senses.whyCN: 配给就是压力下的分发，因此这个词带上稀缺的意味。

intro.en: Allocation comes from Medieval Latin allocatio, from allocare 'to place, assign', built on ad- 'to' and locus 'place'. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: allocation 来自中世纪拉丁 allocatio，源自动词 allocare「安放、指派」，由 ad-「向」与 locus「地方」构成，十六世纪进入英语。

items.en: Locus meant 'place, position'. It gives local, locate, locality and dislocate.
items.cn: locus 意为「地方、位置」，衍生 local、locate、locality 与 dislocate。

items.en: Locare meant 'to place, set, station', turning the noun of place into a verb of putting.
items.cn: locare 意为「放置、安顿、驻扎」，把表示地方的名词变成「放」的动词。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus locare gave allocare, 'to place something to someone, assign'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 locare 构成 allocare，意为「把某物放到某人处、指派」。

items.en: Allocatio, 'an assigning', was used in accounts and administration before English borrowed it.
items.cn: allocatio「指派、分派」在英语借入之前已用于账目与行政。

items.en: English adopted the word in the 1500s for the setting aside of money or goods for a purpose.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收这个词，指为某用途留出钱或货。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether English took the noun directly from Latin or through French allocation is not settled, and the earliest date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语是直接从拉丁语借入，还是经法语 allocation 传入，尚无定论；最早年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same place root that are easily confused with allocation; group two holds near terms for sharing out.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「地方」词根、易与 allocation 混淆的词；第二组是表示分发的近义词。

entries.definition: A position or site, from the same place root; it names where something is, not how it is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 位置或地点，同出「地方」词根；指某物在哪，不指如何分。

entries.definition: A share or a small plot assigned to someone, built on lot rather than locus; it is close in meaning but not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 分给某人的一份或一小块地，由 lot 而非 locus 构成；意思接近但不同源。

entries.definition: To move something out of its proper place, as a joint; it keeps the place image but reverses the fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移出原位，如关节脱位；保留「地方」意象但把安放反过来。

entries.definition: A formal speech, from loqui 'to speak'; the shared opening is misleading.
entries.definitionCN: 正式讲话，来自 loqui「说话」；相同的开头容易误导。

entries.definition: The general word for spreading things among people or places; it does not imply a decision about shares.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西分给人或地方的通用词；不含「决定份额」之意。

entries.definition: The division of something in fixed proportions, often by rule; it stresses the ratio rather than the placing.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定比例分，常依规则；强调比例而非安放。

entries.definition: The giving of a task or a person to a role; it is the usual word when duties rather than funds are involved.
entries.definitionCN: 把任务或人派到某角色；涉及职责而非资金时更常用。

entries.definition: Controlled distribution of scarce goods by quota; it is the emergency form of allocation.
entries.definitionCN: 按配额受控地分发稀缺物资；是 allocation 的紧急形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the place root, the fixed phrases and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「地方」词根、固定搭配与真实词族。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus locus 'place': to allocate is to put each part in its place.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 locus「地方」：分配就是把每一份放到它的位置。

normal.en: The family runs allocate, allocation, allocative, allocator, reallocation and misallocation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 allocate、allocation、allocative、allocator、reallocation 与 misallocation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: resource allocation, budget allocation, seat allocation, cost allocation.
normal.cn: 固定说法：资源配置、预算分配、名额分配、成本分摊。

normal.en: The same root appears in local, locate, locality and dislocate.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 local、locate、locality 与 dislocate 中。

normal.en: A budget line is money placed at a destination, so the act and the sum share one word.
normal.cn: 预算中的一项就是把钱放到某个去处，动作与款额因此共用一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut into shares, each labelled with a name.
abstract.cn: 想象一块饼切成若干份，每份都写着名字。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf of identical boxes, each carried to a different desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一排放着相同盒子，每只被搬到不同的桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a limited row of chairs and a list deciding who sits where.
abstract.cn: 想象一排有限的椅子，一份名单决定谁坐哪里。

examples.en: The allocation of water between farms and towns is decided each spring.
examples.cn: 农场与城镇之间的水量分配每年春天决定。

examples.en: A fair allocation of seats gave every department two places.
examples.cn: 公平的名额分配让每个部门得到两个位置。

examples.en: Poor allocation of staff left the busiest ward short-handed.
examples.cn: 人员配置不当让最忙的病区人手不足。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「al（向）+ location（位置）」——把东西一件件放到各自的位置，就是分配

root: 中世纪拉丁 allocatio，来自 allocare「安放、指派」= ad-（向）+ locare「放置」，而 locare 出自 locus「地方」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture, placing each part where it belongs: sharing resources, the economic question, a budget line, duties, limited places, computer memory, shared costs and finally wartime rations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个动作——把每一份放到该去的地方：分配资源、经济问题、预算拨款、职责、有限名额、计算机内存、共同成本，最后是战时配给。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a large cake cut into labelled shares, one for each purpose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张大饼切成标好用途的若干份。

branches.en: ACT AND SUM: sharing out and the budget line it produces are one gesture seen as process and result.
branches.cn: 动作与款额：分发行为与由此产生的预算项，是同一动作的过程与结果。

branches.en: TWO ECONOMIES: resources and shared costs are both placed on someone's account.
branches.cn: 两种经济：资源与共同成本，都被记到某方的账上。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PLACES: duties go to desks and places go to applicants, both by a decision.
branches.cn: 人与位置：职责分到桌上，名额分到申请人，都靠一个决定。

branches.en: MACHINE MEMORY: the computer hands out its finite store as money is handed out.
branches.cn: 机器内存：计算机像分钱一样分发有限的存储。

branches.en: SCARCITY: when goods run short, sharing becomes rationing.
branches.cn: 稀缺：物资一紧张，分发就变成配给。

intro.en: Allocation is a Latin verb of placing with a prefix that points it at someone, plus a noun ending.
intro.cn: allocation 是由「放置」的拉丁动词加指向某人的前缀，再加名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin locus and locare give allocate, location, local and dislocate; ad- directs the placing toward a recipient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 locus 与 locare 衍生 allocate、location、local 与 dislocate；ad- 把「放」指向接受者。

items.structure: Latin prefix (assimilating to al- before l)
items.example: The prefix points the placing at a recipient.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「放置」指向接受者。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a spot.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「地点」的意思。

items.example: The verb turns place into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「地方」变成动作。

items.example: The board allocated funds to two labs.
items.exampleCN: 董事会把经费分给两个实验室。

items.meaning: the act or result of assigning
items.example: The allocation was announced in June.
items.exampleCN: 分配方案在六月公布。

items.example: Allocative efficiency matters in health care.
items.exampleCN: 配置效率在医疗中很重要。

items.example: Reallocation moved two posts to the new site.
items.exampleCN: 重新分配把两个岗位挪到新址。

items.meaning: a bad or wrong sharing out
items.example: Misallocation wasted half the budget.
items.exampleCN: 配置失当浪费了一半预算。

definition_zh: 受孕；构想；构思；概念；观念；理解方式；（艺术）构思；开端
definition_en: the act of forming an idea or plan; the way someone understands something; the beginning of something; biological conception
core_image: 一粒种子落进土里，同时另一颗念头在心里落定，两者都叫“开始成形”
scene: 他对「公平」的理解与同事完全不同。 His conception of fairness is nothing like his colleague's, so the same proposal reads as two different things.
sceneCN: 这里 conception 是「（对某事的）理解方式、观念」（第 3 个义项：某人理解某事物的方式）；句意：他对公平的理解与同事完全不同，所以同一份方案被两人读成两件事。图中可辨识物件：两副不同的眼镜、同一份方案、种子与花盆、天平、对话气泡。

pos.zh: 受孕；构想；概念；观念；理解方式

senses.title: Biological conception
senses.definition: the moment when an egg is fertilised and a pregnancy begins
senses.definitionCN: 卵子受精、妊娠开始的时刻
senses.example: The drug can prevent conception.
senses.exampleCN: 该药可阻止受孕。
senses.why: Medicine uses the word for a physical beginning. The Latin image of 'taking in' fits: the egg takes in the sperm, and a new process starts. This sense is concrete and dated, unlike the mental ones.
senses.whyCN: 医学用该词指物理开端。拉丁“摄入”意象正合：卵摄入精子，新过程开始。此义具体、可定日期，不同于心智诸义。

senses.title: Forming a plan
senses.definition: the act of forming an idea or plan in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在心中形成想法或计划的行为
senses.example: The conception of the reform took years.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革的构想用了数年。
senses.why: Here the word names the act, not the idea produced. A conception is an event in someone's mind; a concept is the content that can be shared afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 此处该词命名动作，而非产出的观念。conception 是某人心中发生的事件；concept 是此后可共享的内容。

senses.title: A way of understanding
senses.definition: the particular way a person or group understands something
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体理解某事物的特定方式
senses.example: Different cultures have different conceptions of time.
senses.exampleCN: 不同文化有不同的时间观。
senses.why: This is the dominant modern sense: conception is perspectival. Two people can share the word 'justice' and still have incompatible conceptions of it, which is why the noun is often paired with 'of'.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代主导义：conception 是视角性的。两人可共享“正义”一词，却对其有不相容的观念，故该名词常与 of 连用。

senses.title: A conception of liberty
senses.definition: a systematic view of what a value means and requires
senses.definitionCN: 关于某价值意味着什么、要求什么的系统看法
senses.example: Berlin contrasted two conceptions of liberty.
senses.exampleCN: 伯林对比了两种自由观。
senses.why: Political theory uses the noun for rival interpretations of a shared value. The debate is not whether liberty is good but what counts as liberty, and each conception draws a different boundary.
senses.whyCN: 政治理论用该名词指对共享价值的不同解释。争论不是自由好不好，而是什么算自由；每种观念画出不同边界。

senses.title: The Immaculate Conception
senses.definition: the doctrine that Mary was conceived without original sin
senses.definitionCN: 玛利亚无原罪而成胎的教义
senses.example: The Immaculate Conception is a Marian doctrine.
senses.exampleCN: 无原罪成胎是关于玛利亚的教义。
senses.why: Theology fixes a capitalised phrase. Note the common confusion with the virgin birth: the Immaculate Conception concerns Mary's own conception, not the conception of Jesus.
senses.whyCN: 神学固定这一大写短语。注意常与童贞受孕混淆：无原罪成胎讲的是玛利亚自身的受孕，而非耶稣的受孕。

senses.title: Concept formation
senses.definition: the mental process by which a child or learner forms categories
senses.definitionCN: 儿童或学习者形成范畴的心智过程
senses.example: Piaget studied the child's conception of number.
senses.exampleCN: 皮亚杰研究儿童的数字概念形成。
senses.why: Psychology uses the noun for a developmental achievement. The child moves from particulars to a category, and the timing of that move is what experiments try to measure.
senses.whyCN: 心理学用该名词指发展成就。儿童从个别走向范畴，实验试图测量这一转变的时点。

senses.title: Artistic conception
senses.definition: the original idea and design of a work before or during its making
senses.definitionCN: 作品在制作前或制作中的原初想法与设计
senses.example: The painting's conception is bolder than its execution.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画的构思比执行更大胆。
senses.why: Art criticism separates conception from execution: what was imagined versus what was made. A work can have a strong conception and a weak finish, or the reverse.
senses.whyCN: 艺术批评区分构思与执行：想象之物与制成之物。作品可构思强而完成弱，或反之。

senses.title: The beginning of something
senses.definition: the point at which an enterprise or process is first conceived
senses.definitionCN: 事业或过程最初被构想的时点
senses.example: The conception of the project dates to 2019.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目肇始于二〇一九年。
senses.why: This sense extends 'conception' from a mind to a project's origin. The plan is treated as an entity with a birth, and the word gives it a biography.
senses.whyCN: 此义把 conception 从心智扩展到项目的起源。计划被当作有出生的实体，该词给它一部传记。

senses.title: A world conception
senses.definition: an organized set of beliefs about reality and value
senses.definitionCN: 关于实在与价值的组织化信念集合
senses.example: Marx's conception of history shaped the century.
senses.exampleCN: 马克思的历史观塑造了那个世纪。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the noun for a comprehensive outlook. A world conception is more than one idea; it is a system in which the ideas support one another.
senses.whyCN: 哲学用该名词指综合视野。世界观不止一个观念；它是一个观念相互支撑的系统。

intro.en: Conception is from Latin conceptio, the action noun of concipere 'to take in, receive, conceive', com- 'together' plus capere 'take'. The base is the same as concept and conceptual, but the suffix -ion names the act or process, while concept names the thing conceived. English uses conception for both biological fertilisation and mental formation, because Latin conceptio covered both: a taking in of seed or of an idea.
intro.cn: conception 出自拉丁 conceptio，即 concipere“摄入、接受、构想”的动作名词，由 com-“一起”加 capere“拿”构成。词基与 concept、conceptual 相同，但 -ion 后缀命名动作或过程，concept 则命名被构想之物。英语用 conception 兼指生物学受精与心智形成，因为拉丁 conceptio 两者都覆盖：摄入种子或摄入观念。

items.en: capere 'to take' and concipere 'to take in' are the base; the same root gives concept and capture.
items.cn: capere“拿”与 concipere“摄入”是词基；同根给出 concept 与 capture。

items.en: conceptio is the action noun: a taking in, a conceiving, whether of seed or of an idea.
items.cn: conceptio 是动作名词：摄入、构想，无论种子还是观念。

items.en: The word covered both biological and mental conception from the start, a double life English inherits.
items.cn: 该词从一开始就兼指生物受孕与心智构想，英语继承了这双重身份。

items.en: English conception enters in the 14C in theology and medicine, then spreads to philosophy.
items.cn: 英语 conception 于十四世纪进入神学与医学，后扩展到哲学。

items.en: The sense 'a way of understanding' becomes central in philosophical writing about ideas.
items.cn: 十七世纪“理解方式”义在论观念的哲学写作中成为核心。

items.en: Psychology, art criticism, and political theory each keep a specialised sense of the noun.
items.cn: 现代心理学、艺术批评与政治理论各保留该名词一个专门义。

note.en: The first group is the conceive family, where conception and concept divide act from product; the second is words for ideas, which differ in whether they name the act, the content, or a mistaken content.
note.cn: 第一组是 conceive 词族，conception 与 concept 在此分工为动作与产品；第二组是“观念”类词，差别在于指动作、内容还是错误内容。

entries.definition: to form an idea; to become pregnant.
entries.definitionCN: 构想；受孕。

entries.definition: the idea that results from conceiving; a general category.
entries.definitionCN: 构想产生的观念；一般范畴。

entries.definition: a wrong or mistaken conception.
entries.definitionCN: 误解；错误观念。

entries.definition: a thought or notion, often less systematic than a conception.
entries.definitionCN: 想法或念头，常不如 conception 系统。

entries.definition: a vague or general idea, often informal or slightly dismissive.
entries.definitionCN: 模糊或一般的想法，常口语或略含轻蔑。

entries.definition: a particular reading or explanation of something. It stresses reading a text or event.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物的特定读法或解释。强调解读文本或事件。

normalIntro.en: Real links: concipere 'take in', conceptio as action noun, and the double life of biological and mental conception.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：concipere“摄入”、conceptio 动作名词，以及生物与心智受孕的双重身份。

normal.en: Concipere is 'take in'. Conception is the taking-in; concept is what has been taken in.
normal.cn: concipere 是“摄入”。conception 是摄入动作；concept 是被摄入之物。

normal.en: The same word covers seed and idea because Latin conceptio did: both are beginnings that take hold.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖种子与观念，因为拉丁 conceptio 如此：两者都是落定的开端。

normal.en: Conception of X is how you understand X; a concept of X is the content you can share. Perspective versus package.
normal.cn: conception of X 是你如何理解 X；concept of X 是可共享的内容。视角对包裹。

normal.en: The Immaculate Conception is about Mary's own conception, not Jesus's virgin birth; the two doctrines are often confused.
normal.cn: 无原罪成胎讲玛利亚自身的受孕，不是耶稣的童贞降生；两种教义常被混淆。

normal.en: 'The conception of the project' gives a plan a birth date; the metaphor turns an idea into a biography.
normal.cn: the conception of the project 给计划一个出生日；隐喻把观念变成传记。

abstract.en: Conception is the act that makes a concept possible; without the act, there is no content to share.
abstract.cn: conception 是使概念成为可能的动作；没有动作，就没有可共享的内容。

abstract.en: Rival conceptions of one value cannot be settled by definition alone, because each conception is a whole way of seeing.
abstract.cn: 对同一价值的不同观念不能只靠定义解决，因为每种观念都是一整套看的方式。

abstract.en: Every beginning is a conception in retrospect: the origin is assigned after the fact, not given with it.
abstract.cn: 每个开端都是回溯中的构想：起源是事后指派的，而非与生俱来的。

examples.en: The conception of the new library began with a public meeting.
examples.cn: 新图书馆的构想始于一次公开会议。

examples.en: Children's conceptions of distance differ from adults'.
examples.cn: 儿童对距离的概念与成人不同。

examples.en: The study covers the period from conception to birth.
examples.cn: 该研究涵盖从受孕到出生这一时期。

dict_mnemonic.text: “康塞普申”——心里“接住”一个念头，或身体接住一粒种子 → conception 构想/受孕

root: 拉丁 conceptio（concipere“摄入、构想”的动作名词 = com-“一起”+ capere“拿”）；与 concept、conceptual 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of conception: fertilisation, plan-forming, a way of understanding, a political view of a value, a Marian doctrine, concept formation, artistic design, a project's origin, and a world view. The thread is a beginning that takes hold, in body or mind.
sensesIntro.cn: conception 的九个义项：受孕、构想计划、理解方式、价值之政治观、玛利亚教义、概念形成、艺术构思、项目肇始、世界观。共同线索是身体或心智中落定的开端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed falling into soil and an idea settling in a mind, both beginning to take form.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒种子落入土中，一个念头落入心中，两者都开始成形。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE CHILD: fertilisation and concept formation are beginnings that develop.
branches.cn: 身体与儿童：受精与概念形成都是会发展的开端。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE WORK: planning, artistic design, and a project's origin are conceptions in time.
branches.cn: 动作与作品：计划、艺术构思与项目肇始都是时间中的构想。

branches.en: THE OUTLOOK: political conceptions and world views are organized perspectives.
branches.cn: 视野：政治观念与世界观都是组织化的视角。

branches.en: THE DOCTRINE: the Immaculate Conception fixes a theological sense and a common confusion.
branches.cn: 教义：无原罪成胎固定一个神学义与一种常见混淆。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: conception is perspectival where concept is shareable content.
branches.cn: 对照：conception 是视角性的，concept 是可共享内容。

intro.en: Conception is conceive + -ion, from Latin conceptio. Conceive is concipere, com- plus capere 'take'. The family includes concept, conceptual, conceptional, and misconception; the same capere root gives capture and captive.
intro.cn: conception 是 conceive 加 -ion，出自拉丁 conceptio。conceive 是 concipere（com- 加 capere“拿”）。词族含 concept、conceptual、conceptional、misconception；同一 capere 词根给出 capture 与 captive。

latinIntro.en: Latin concipere 'take in, conceive' gives conceptio 'a conceiving'. English keeps -ion for the act and uses concept for the product. The -ual adjective conceptual belongs to concept, while conceptional belongs to conception, a useful division.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 concipere“摄入、构想”给出 conceptio“构想”。英语保留 -ion 指动作，用 concept 指产品。-ual 形容词 conceptual 属于 concept，而 conceptional 属于 conception，这是有用的分工。

definition_zh: 明确的；清楚的；直言的；露骨的；显式的
definition_en: stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing to be inferred or guessed
core_image: 折起的纸被完全摊平，每一道折痕都露出来
scene: 监考老师指着黑板上的规则说： The instructions are explicit: no phones in the exam room.
sceneCN: 这里 explicit 是「明确写明的」（第 1 个义项：完全说清、不留暗示）；句意：规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。图中可辨识物件：黑板、规则清单、手机收纳盒、监考老师。

pos.zh: 明确的；清楚的；直言的；露骨的

senses.title: Fully stated: nothing left implied
senses.titleCN: 明确写出：不留任何暗示
senses.definition: expressed in clear and complete words, with nothing left for the reader to infer
senses.definitionCN: 用清楚完整的话表达，不给读者留下需要推断的空白
senses.example: The instructions are explicit: no phones in the exam room.
senses.exampleCN: 规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。
senses.why: Latin explicare is ex 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. Explicit is the sheet unfolded: every line that could have stayed hidden is now open to view.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 explicare 是 ex「出」+ plicare「折叠」。explicit 就是被展开的那张纸：原本可以藏住的每一行，现在都摊在外面。

senses.title: Precise and unambiguous
senses.titleCN: 确切无歧义：不给第二种读法
senses.definition: so clearly worded that it can be understood in only one way
senses.definitionCN: 措辞清楚到只有一种理解方式
senses.example: The doctor gave an explicit warning about mixing the drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 医生对混用这些药物发出了明确警告。
senses.why: A folded page hides parts of the text. An explicit wording lays the whole sentence flat, so there is no fold left in which a second meaning could hide.
senses.whyCN: 折起的页面会遮住部分文字。明确的措辞把整句话摊平，于是没有一道折痕还能藏住第二种意思。

senses.title: Open about something usually hidden
senses.titleCN: 直言不讳：把通常藏着的话说出来
senses.definition: willing to state something openly that people often leave unsaid
senses.definitionCN: 愿意公开说出人们通常避而不谈的事
senses.example: She was explicit about her reasons for leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 她直言不讳地说明了自己离开的原因。
senses.why: The verb can be reflexive: a person unfolds his own motives instead of leaving them folded inside. Openness is the human version of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也可以指向人自身：一个人把自己的动机展开，而不是折起来藏在里面。坦率就是同一意象在人的身上的版本。

senses.title: Sexually explicit content
senses.titleCN: 露骨性内容：不加遮掩地呈现
senses.definition: showing sexual acts or nudity in an open, detailed way
senses.definitionCN: 以公开、详细的方式呈现性行为或裸体
senses.example: The film is rated for explicit content.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影因含露骨内容而被分级。
senses.why: The modern phrase uses 'explicit' for what is shown rather than implied. Nothing is folded away or concealed, and that is exactly why the label warns.
senses.whyCN: 现代短语用 explicit 指“直接呈现而非暗示”的内容。没有什么被折起或遮住，这正是这个标签要警告的地方。

senses.title: Explicit language: open swearing
senses.titleCN: 粗口直出：不加消音的歌词或言语
senses.definition: containing swear words or crude language that is not edited out
senses.definitionCN: 含有未消音、未删改的粗话或脏话
senses.example: The album carries an explicit lyrics warning.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑带有“含粗口歌词”的警示。
senses.why: A clean version folds the offensive word away; an explicit version leaves it unfolded in the open. The same contrast between hidden and displayed.
senses.whyCN: 干净版把冒犯性的词折起来藏掉；explicit 版则让它展开在外。仍是“藏”与“露”的同一组对立。

senses.title: Explicit formula: fully specified
senses.titleCN: 显式公式：每一项都写出来
senses.definition: in mathematics and logic, stated in full form rather than left in shorthand or implication
senses.definitionCN: 数学与逻辑中，以完整形式写出，而不是用简写或隐含
senses.example: The paper gives an explicit formula for the solution.
senses.exampleCN: 论文给出了解的显式公式。
senses.why: A formula in shorthand is folded up; an explicit formula multiplies it out so that every term stands visible. This is the algebraic version of unfolding.
senses.whyCN: 简写公式是折起来的；显式公式把它乘开，让每一项都立在外面。这是“展开”的代数版本。

senses.title: Explicit consent: permission in plain terms
senses.titleCN: 明确同意：法律与医疗上的明示许可
senses.definition: clear, recorded permission given for a specific act, especially in law or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 对某一具体行为给出的清楚、有记录的许可，尤用于法律或医疗
senses.example: The study required explicit consent from every participant.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究要求每位参与者明确同意。
senses.why: Consent that is merely implied can be disputed later. Explicit consent is written out and signed, so the permission cannot be folded back into silence.
senses.whyCN: 仅仅隐含的同意日后可能有争议。explicit consent 被写出来并签署，许可就无法再折回沉默里。

senses.title: Explicit memory: consciously available
senses.titleCN: 外显记忆：能清楚说出来的记忆
senses.definition: in psychology, a memory that a person can consciously recall and state
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指人能有意识地回忆并说出的记忆
senses.example: Explicit memory lets you recall your first day at school.
senses.exampleCN: 外显记忆让你能回想起上学第一天。
senses.why: What is explicit is laid out where the mind can look at it. Explicit memory is knowledge a person can unfold and describe, unlike a skill that stays folded into the body.
senses.whyCN: explicit 的东西被铺在心灵能看见的地方。外显记忆是人能展开并描述的知识，不同于折进身体里的技能。

senses.title: The old manuscript explicit: here the book ends
senses.titleCN: 古抄本收尾语：书到此展开完毕
senses.definition: historical, noun: the closing word or note of a medieval manuscript, marking the end of the text
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，名词：中世纪抄本末尾的收尾词或题记，标记正文结束
senses.example: The scribe wrote explicit at the foot of the last page.
senses.exampleCN: 抄写员在最后一页末尾写下了 explicit。
senses.why: Medieval scribes ended with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded/read out'. The word that marked a completed reading became the label for the end itself.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪抄写员用 explicitus est liber 收尾，意为“书已展开／读完了”。标记“读完”的词，最后变成了“结尾”本身的标签。

intro.en: Explicit comes from Latin explicare 'to unfold, unravel, explain', ex- 'out' + plicare 'to fold'. The English adjective, meaning 'clear, not ambiguous', is first recorded in the 1610s through French explicite.
intro.cn: explicit 来自拉丁语 explicare“展开、解开、解释”，由 ex-“出”+ plicare“折叠”构成。英语形容词“清楚、不含糊”于 1610 年代经法语 explicite 进入英语。

items.en: Explicare meant 'to unfold, unroll; disentangle; explain'. The image is physical: a folded thing is opened until its parts can be seen.
items.cn: explicare 意为“展开、铺开；解开；解释”。意象是物理的：把折起的东西打开，直到各部分都能看见。

items.en: Plicare 'to fold' goes back to PIE *plek- 'to plait, weave, fold'. The same root gives plait, plexus, complex, and the two Latin directions in- and ex-.
items.cn: plicare“折叠”可追溯到原始印欧语 *plek-“编织、折叠”。同一词根生出 plait、plexus、complex，以及拉丁语里 in- 与 ex- 两个方向。

items.en: Explicitus, a variant past participle of explicare, meant 'unobstructed, clear'. What is unfolded is also unblocked: nothing is left in the way of understanding.
items.cn: explicitus 是 explicare 的异体过去分词，意为“无阻碍的、清楚的”。被展开的东西也畅通无阻：理解的道路上没有东西挡着。

items.en: English takes the adjective from French explicite with the sense 'clear, plain, not ambiguous'. It is the opposite of implicit, which is folded in.
items.cn: 英语从法语 explicite 借入形容词，义为“清楚的、明白的、不含糊的”。它是 implicit 的反面，后者是“折进去的”。

items.en: Scribes closed a manuscript with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded / read out'. From that formula, explicit became the word written at the end of a text.
items.cn: 抄写员用 explicitus est liber“书已展开／读完了”来结束抄本。从这个固定语开始，explicit 成了写在文本末尾的那个词。

items.en: Modern English keeps the 'nothing hidden' core: explicit instructions, explicit consent, sexually explicit, explicit memory. Its mirror is implicit, in- 'in' + plicare 'fold'.
items.cn: 现代英语保留“没有隐藏”的内核：explicit instructions、explicit consent、sexually explicit、explicit memory。它的镜像是 implicit，即 in-“内”+ plicare“折”。

note.en: The first group is close in spelling or word parts; the second is close in meaning. Form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或构词成分上接近；第二组在词义上接近。先看词形，再看意义。

entries.definition: implied but not stated. In- 'in' + plicare 'fold' means folded in, the mirror image of explicit's unfolded.
entries.definitionCN: 隐含而未明说的。in-“内”+ plicare“折”意为折进去，正是 explicit“展开”的镜像。

entries.definition: to explain a text or idea in detail. It is the verb; explicit is the adjective for what has been fully laid out.
entries.definitionCN: 详细解释文本或观点。它是动词；explicit 是形容词，形容已被完全铺开的内容。

entries.definition: to use something for profit, or a bold deed. It comes from Latin explicitum 'something unfolded or settled', but its meaning moved to 'turn to account'.
entries.definitionCN: 利用；开发；也可指功绩。它来自拉丁语 explicitum“被展开或了结之事”，但词义转向“加以利用”。

entries.definition: easy to understand or see. Clear can describe a style or a view; explicit stresses that the content is actually stated, not merely easy.
entries.definitionCN: 易懂的；清晰的。clear 可形容文风或视野；explicit 强调内容确实被说出来，而不只是容易懂。

entries.definition: fixed, certain, and not likely to change. Definite stresses certainty; explicit stresses complete expression.
entries.definitionCN: 确定的；不会改变的。definite 强调确定性；explicit 强调表达完整。

entries.definition: having only one possible meaning. It focuses on the absence of ambiguity; explicit focuses on the presence of full statement.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一种可能含义的。它聚焦于“没有歧义”；explicit 聚焦于“把话完整说出来”。

entries.definition: stated openly and specifically, especially in a contract or law. Express is formal and legal; explicit is broader and also covers sexual content.
entries.definitionCN: 明示的，尤用于合同或法律。express 正式且偏法律；explicit 范围更广，也可指露骨内容。

normalIntro.en: Real parts, real phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词成分、真实短语和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ex- 'out' + plicare 'fold' = unfold. Explicit is the sheet opened flat, with every fold laid out.
normal.cn: ex-“出”+ plicare“折”= 展开。explicit 就是被摊平的那张纸，每一道折痕都铺开。

normal.en: The same plicare gives implicit 'folded in', implicate, explicate, complexity and plait.
normal.cn: 同一个 plicare 生出 implicit“折进去”、implicate、explicate、complexity 和 plait。

normal.en: Medieval scribes ended with explicitus est liber, 'the book is unfolded / read out'; from this the word explicit came to mark the end of a text.
normal.cn: 中世纪抄写员用 explicitus est liber“书已展开／读完了”收尾；由此 explicit 成了标记文本结尾的词。

normal.en: To make something explicit is the everyday phrase for bringing an unstated rule or feeling into the open.
normal.cn: make something explicit 是日常短语，意为把没说出口的规则或感受摆到明面上。

normal.en: Do not confuse explicit with exhibit: exhibit has habere 'hold' and means hold out; explicit has plicare 'fold' and means unfold.
normal.cn: 不要把 explicit 和 exhibit 混淆：exhibit 的词根是 habere“握”，意为举出去；explicit 的词根是 plicare“折”，意为展开。

abstract.en: A letter folded small: implicit keeps it closed, explicit opens it flat and reads every line aloud.
abstract.cn: 一封折得很小的信：implicit 让它保持合着，explicit 把它摊平，并逐行读出来。

abstract.en: A rule everyone follows but nobody says is implicit; writing it on the door makes it explicit.
abstract.cn: 一条人人都遵守却没人说出口的规则是 implicit；把它写在门上，就变成 explicit。

abstract.en: Every fold has an inside and an outside. Implicit is the inside; explicit is the outside turned toward the reader.
abstract.cn: 每道折痕都有里面和外面。implicit 是里面；explicit 是翻向读者的外面。

examples.en: The instructions were explicit: no phones in the exam room.
examples.cn: 规则写得很明确：考场内不许用手机。

examples.en: She was explicit about her reasons for leaving.
examples.cn: 她直言不讳地说明了自己离开的原因。

examples.en: The film is rated for explicit content.
examples.cn: 这部电影因含露骨内容而被分级。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一克斯普利说」——把折起的话全铺开、普利落落地说明白 → explicit 明确的

root: 源自拉丁语 explicitus「无阻碍的、清楚的」，是 explicare「展开、解开、解释」的异体过去分词，由 ex「出」+ plicare「折叠」构成。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of explicit share one gesture: a folded surface is opened until nothing is hidden — a rule, a warning, a motive, a sexual scene, a swear word, a formula, a consent form, a memory, or the end of a manuscript.
sensesIntro.cn: explicit 的九个义项共享同一个动作：把折起的表面打开，直到没有东西被遮住——规则、警告、动机、性场景、脏话、公式、同意书、记忆，或一部抄本的结尾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded sheet is opened flat so that every line can be read.
core.cn: 核心意象：折起的纸被完全摊平，每一行都能读到。

branches.en: THE OPEN PAGE: a fully stated instruction or warning leaves no second reading.
branches.cn: 摊开的页面：完整写出的指示或警告，不留下第二种读法。

branches.en: OPENNESS ABOUT THE HIDDEN: a motive, a sexual scene, or a swear word is brought out instead of folded away.
branches.cn: 对隐藏之事的坦白：动机、性场景或脏话被摆出来，而不是折起来藏掉。

branches.en: THE FULLY SPECIFIED: an explicit formula writes out every term, and explicit memory can be recalled and stated.
branches.cn: 完整写明：显式公式写出每一项，外显记忆能被回忆并说出。

branches.en: THE SIGNED PERMISSION: explicit consent cannot be folded back into silence.
branches.cn: 签署的许可：明确同意无法再折回沉默里。

branches.en: THE OLD COLOPHON: explicitus est liber marked the book as unfolded and finished.
branches.cn: 古老的收尾语：explicitus est liber 标记书已展开、已读完。

intro.en: Explicit is the adjective from Latin explicare: ex- 'out' plus the plic- stem 'fold'. English builds adverbs, nouns, verbs and negatives on this stem, and the same root runs through implicit, complex and plait.
intro.cn: explicit 是拉丁语 explicare 的形容词：ex-“出”加 plic- 词干“折”。英语在这个词干上构成副词、名词、动词和否定形式；同一词根也贯穿 implicit、complex 和 plait。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' has the compound explicare 'to unfold, explain' and its participle explicitus; the opposite compound implicare 'to fold in' gives implicit and implicate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plicare“折叠”有复合形式 explicare“展开、解释”及其分词 explicitus；反方向的复合形式 implicare“折进去”生出 implicit 和 implicate。

items.meaningCN: 展开的；清楚的；明确写出的（ex- 出 + plicare 折）
items.example: The rule is explicit.
items.exampleCN: 规则很明确。

items.meaning: in a clear, fully stated way
items.meaningCN: 明确地；直截了当地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She explicitly denied the claim.
items.exampleCN: 她明确否认了这一说法。

items.meaningCN: 明确性；直白程度（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The explicitness of the warning left no doubt.
items.exampleCN: 警告的明确程度让人毫无怀疑。

items.meaning: to unfold the meaning of a text or idea
items.meaningCN: 解释；阐发（把折叠的含义展开）
items.example: The essay explicates the poem line by line.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章逐行阐释这首诗。

items.meaningCN: 解释；阐释（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Her explication of the theory was clear.
items.exampleCN: 她对这个理论的阐释很清楚。

items.example: The error is explicable.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误是可以解释的。

items.meaningCN: 无法解释的（in- 表否定 + 可解释的）
items.example: The lights failed for inexplicable reasons.
items.exampleCN: 灯以无法解释的原因熄灭了。

items.meaning: folded in; suggested but not stated
items.meaningCN: 折进去的；隐含的（与 explicit 的“展开”相对）
items.example: There was an implicit threat in his tone.
items.exampleCN: 他的语气里有一种隐含的威胁。

items.meaning: to fold someone into a matter; to involve
items.meaningCN: 牵连；使卷入（把某人折进事件里）
items.example: The letter implicated two officials.
items.exampleCN: 这封信牵连了两名官员。

items.meaning: to turn something to use; a bold act
items.meaningCN: 利用；开发；功绩（由“展开、了结之事”转为“加以利用”）
items.example: The company exploited a gap in the market.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司利用了市场空白。

items.meaningCN: 复杂的（com- 共同 + plectere 编织，同属 *plek- 词根）
items.example: The problem is more complex than it looks.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题比看上去更复杂。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 展开的；无阻碍的；清楚的

definition_zh: 越来越多的（后接可数名词复数，强调数量逐年或逐期上升）
definition_en: a growing quantity of countable people or things, with the count rising over time
core_image: 招生办公室的登记册一年比一年厚，后来的名字排到了走廊
scene: 招生办公室的登记册一年比一年厚，来自小镇的申请者多到排上了走廊。 An increasing number of applicants come from small towns each year.
sceneCN: 这里指申请者人数逐年上升（第 1 个义项：人数上升）；句意为每年有越来越多的申请者来自小镇。图中可辨识物件：逐年变厚的登记册、走廊上排队的人、贴满名字的名单。

pos.zh: （固定搭配）越来越多的（后接可数名词复数）

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语「生长」动词进入英语，义为「增加」
由现在分词加副词尾构成，义为「越来越」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「不断增加的」
由拉丁语「数」一词进入英语，义为「数目」
同出拉丁语「数」一词，义为「众多的」

senses.title: More people over time
senses.definition: to have a rising count of people in a stated group
senses.definitionCN: 指某一群体中的人数在上升
senses.example: An increasing number of people work from home at least one day a week.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的人每周至少有一天在家工作。
senses.why: Number is for things that can be counted one by one, and people are the clearest case.
senses.whyCN: number 用于能一个个数清的东西，人是最清楚的例子。

senses.title: More cases or events
senses.definition: to have more recorded instances of something occurring
senses.definitionCN: 指被记录的某事发生次数变多
senses.example: An increasing number of accidents has been reported at this crossing since the road was widened.
senses.exampleCN: 自从道路拓宽以来，这个路口报告的事故越来越多。
senses.why: Events are countable too, so the phrase suits records and reports as naturally as crowds.
senses.whyCN: 事件同样可数，所以这个短语用于记录与报告，和用于人群一样自然。

senses.title: More participants
senses.definition: to have a growing count of people taking part in an activity
senses.definitionCN: 指参加某项活动的人数不断增加
senses.example: An increasing number of volunteers join the clean-up every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 每年春天有越来越多的志愿者加入清理活动。
senses.why: Participation is counted at the door, which makes the rise visible and easy to report.
senses.whyCN: 参与是在门口数的，所以上升看得见，也容易报告。

senses.title: More publications or studies
senses.definition: to have a rising count of papers, reports or books on a topic
senses.definitionCN: 指关于某一题目的论文、报告或书籍数量上升
senses.example: An increasing number of studies link sleep quality to memory.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的研究把睡眠质量与记忆联系起来。
senses.why: Academic prose uses the phrase to describe a trend without claiming that the trend is good.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作使用这个短语来陈述趋势，而不主张这一趋势是好的。

senses.title: A year-on-year trend
senses.definition: to show a steady rise from one period to the next
senses.definitionCN: 指从一个时期到下一个时期持续上升
senses.example: An increasing number of tourists arrive by train rather than by car.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的游客坐火车而不是开车前来。
senses.why: The participle carries the movement, and the phrase reads as a line climbing across a chart.
senses.whyCN: 分词承载了「动」的意思，整个短语读起来就是图上一条上升的线。

senses.title: The countable grammar
senses.definition: to be used only with plural countable nouns, never with mass nouns
senses.definitionCN: 指只能接可数名词复数，不能接不可数名词
senses.example: An increasing number of books are published in both print and digital form.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的书同时以纸质与电子形式出版。
senses.why: Number counts units, so a mass noun after it is a grammatical error rather than a stylistic choice.
senses.whyCN: number 数的是个体，所以后面接不可数名词是语法错误，而不是风格选择。

senses.title: The mass-noun contrast
senses.definition: to stand opposite an increasing amount of, which takes uncountable nouns
senses.definitionCN: 指与接不可数名词的「量」类说法相对
senses.example: An increasing number of jobs require coding skills, while an increasing amount of work is done by software.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的工作需要编程技能，同时越来越多的活儿由软件完成。
senses.why: The pair splits the world into units and masses, and mixing them is the commonest mistake.
senses.whyCN: 这一对说法把世界分成「个体」与「整体」，混用是最常见的错误。

senses.title: A trend used as evidence
senses.definition: to present a rising count as support for a claim about the future
senses.definitionCN: 指把上升的数量当作对未来的主张的支撑
senses.example: An increasing number of firms report that they cannot fill technical posts.
senses.exampleCN: 越来越多的公司报告说技术岗位招不满。
senses.why: A trend is evidence only if the count is defined, which is why careful writers name the group.
senses.whyCN: 趋势要成为证据，前提是数的是哪一群人说清楚，所以谨慎的作者会点名群体。

intro.en: Increase came from Latin increscere, to grow upon, from in- and crescere, to grow, through Old French encreistre. Number came from Latin numerus, whose own origin is uncertain. The quantity phrase an increasing number of is modern, shaped by statistical writing.
intro.cn: increase 出自拉丁语 increscere「在上面生长」，由 in- 与 crescere「生长」构成，经古法语进入英语。number 出自拉丁语 numerus「数」，而 numerus 本身的来源不确定。量词短语「an increasing number of」属现代用法，由统计写作塑成。

items.en: Crescere meant to grow, and it supplies increase, crescent and concrete.
items.cn: crescere 意为生长，increase、crescent、concrete 都出自它。

items.en: In- plus crescere gave increscere, to grow upon or grow into, the source of the verb.
items.cn: in- 与 crescere 合成 increscere「长上去」，是这个动词的来源。

items.en: French carried the verb to English in the fourteenth century, and the noun followed.
items.cn: 法语在十四世纪把这个动词带进英语，名词随后而来。

items.en: Numerus meant number, and its deeper origin is uncertain; numerous and numeral come from it.
items.cn: numerus 意为数，它更早的来源不确定；numerous 与 numeral 都出自它。

items.en: The phrase took its present shape with nineteenth-century statistics, which needed a way to report rising counts.
items.cn: 这个短语随十九世纪统计学而定型，因为统计学需要一种报告数量上升的方式。

note.en: The first group shares the growing or counting root; the second group names neighbouring quantity phrases.
note.cn: 第一组共享「生长」或「计数」词根；第二组是与它相邻的量词短语。

entries.definition: The verb or noun meaning to become larger.
entries.definitionCN: 指变大，可作动词或名词。

entries.definition: More and more, used with adjectives and verbs.
entries.definitionCN: 指越来越，常用于形容词与动词。

entries.definition: Made larger, describing a finished change.
entries.definitionCN: 指已经增加，描述完成的变化。

entries.definition: A count of separate units.
entries.definitionCN: 指个体单位的数目。

entries.definition: Many, from the same counting noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指众多的，同出「数」这一名词。

entries.definition: The close synonym, with a slightly softer tone.
entries.definitionCN: 指近义说法，语气略柔和。

entries.definition: The everyday phrasing, common in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指日常口语说法。

entries.definition: A journalistic variant stressing upward movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指新闻体的变体，强调向上。

entries.definition: The mass-noun counterpart, used with uncountable things.
entries.definitionCN: 指对应的不可数说法。

entries.definition: A rising share rather than a rising count.
entries.definitionCN: 指份额上升而非数量上升。

entries.definition: A larger part of a fixed whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指在固定整体中占更大的部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the growing root, the countable rule, and the amount contrast.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用「生长」词根、可数规则，以及和「不可数」说法的对照来记。

normal.en: Crescere is to grow, so an increasing number is a count that keeps growing.
normal.cn: crescere 是「生长」，所以 increasing number 是一个不断长大的数目。

normal.en: Number counts units; if you cannot say one, two, three, use amount instead.
normal.cn: number 数个体；说不出「一个、两个、三个」的东西，就改用 amount。

normal.en: The applicant list getting thicker each year is the picture behind the phrase.
normal.cn: 申请名单一年比一年厚，就是这个短语背后的画面。

normal.en: More and more is the spoken twin, an increasing number of is the written one.
normal.cn: more and more 是口语孪生，an increasing number of 是书面版本。

normal.en: Careful writers name the group being counted, or the trend proves nothing.
normal.cn: 谨慎的作者会说明数的是哪一群人，否则趋势证明不了什么。

abstract.en: A rising count is a shape in time, not a value judgement.
abstract.cn: 上升的数目是时间里的一个形状，不是价值判断。

abstract.en: Numbers grow quietly, and only the list on the desk shows it.
abstract.cn: 数目是悄悄长的，只有桌上那本名册看得见。

abstract.en: To count more of something is not yet to understand why there are more.
abstract.cn: 数出更多，还不等于明白为什么更多。

examples.en: An increasing number of families are moving to smaller towns.
examples.cn: 越来越多的家庭搬到小城镇。

examples.en: An increasing number of journals now require data to be shared.
examples.cn: 越来越多的期刊现在要求共享数据。

examples.en: An increasing number of workers report stress at the end of the week.
examples.cn: 越来越多的工人报告在周末感到压力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安 因克瑞辛 南伯 奥夫」——名册一年比一年厚：越来越多的

root: increase 出自拉丁语 increscere（in- + crescere「生长」），经古法语进入英语；number 出自拉丁语 numerus「数」，其更早来源不确定。短语为近代统计写作所塑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all follow a rising count: people, cases, participants, studies, a yearly trend, the countable rule, the mass contrast and a trend used as evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都跟着一个上升的数目：人、案例、参与者、研究、逐年趋势、可数规则、与不可数的对照，以及作为证据的趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the applicant register grows thicker every year and names spill into the corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：申请登记册一年比一年厚，名字多到溢到走廊。

branches.en: THE CROWD: more people join a stated group each year.
branches.cn: 人群：每年有更多人加入某一群体。

branches.en: THE RECORD: more instances are written down.
branches.cn: 记录：更多事件被写下。

branches.en: THE DOOR AND THE JOURNAL: volunteers sign in, and papers accumulate on a topic.
branches.cn: 门口与期刊：志愿者签到，论文在某一题目上堆积。

branches.en: THE LINE AND THE GRAMMAR: the chart climbs, and only plural count nouns may follow.
branches.cn: 曲线与语法：图表向上，后面只能接可数复数。

branches.en: THE MASS AND THE CLAIM: amount takes the uncountable, and a named group makes a trend into evidence.
branches.cn: 整体与主张：amount 接不可数，点明群体才让趋势成为证据。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb of growing to a Latin noun of counting, and the participle does the work of 'more and more'.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「生长」动词接到拉丁语「数」名词上，分词承担「越来越」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere and increscere supply the growth half; numerus supplies the count half.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere 与 increscere 提供「生长」的一半，numerus 提供「计数」的一半。

items.example: It is the root of increase and crescent.
items.exampleCN: 它是 increase 与 crescent 的根。

items.example: It adds direction to the growing.
items.exampleCN: 它给「生长」加上方向。

items.example: It is the direct source of increase.
items.exampleCN: 它是 increase 的直接来源。

items.example: It makes increasing an adjective of movement.
items.exampleCN: 它把 increasing 变成表示「正在动」的形容词。

items.example: It is the source of number and numerous.
items.exampleCN: 它是 number 与 numerous 的来源。

items.example: It supplies the countable half of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供短语中「可数」的一半。

items.example: It links the count to what is counted.
items.exampleCN: 它把数目与被数的东西连起来。

items.example: It forms numerous.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 numerous。

items.example: It forms increasingly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 increasingly。

由现在分词加副词尾构成，义为「越来越」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「不断增加的」
