同出「数」一词，义为「众多的」

definition_zh: 手势的；用手势表达的；笔触奔放的
definition_en: relating to or done with gestures
core_image: 一排手的轨迹留在空中，像写字一样留下看得见的笔画
scene: 画家不用细线勾边，而是大幅挥臂涂抹，评论家评价说： The painting is gestural rather than precise.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指「笔触奔放、以身体动作留下的痕迹为特征的」（第 3 个义项：绘画中强调挥洒动作的风格）；句意为这幅画是挥洒式的，而非精细描摹。

pos.zh: 手势的；用手势表达的；笔触奔放的

senses.title: Relating to gestures
senses.definition: concerning gestures or the use of bodily movement to express meaning
senses.definitionCN: 与手势或使用身体动作表达意义有关的
senses.example: Gestural meaning depends heavily on context.
senses.exampleCN: 手势意义在很大程度上取决于语境。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the noun to whatever it describes, so its broadest job is 'of gestures'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词连接到被描述之物，因此最宽的用法就是「与手势有关的」。

senses.title: Communicated by gestures
senses.definition: carried by bodily movement rather than by speech
senses.definitionCN: 由身体动作而不是言语承载的
senses.example: The children developed a rich gestural system of their own.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孩子发展出了自己丰富的手势系统。
senses.why: When a message is delivered by hands instead of words, the channel itself is named by this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 当信息由手而不是词语送达时，这个形容词命名的就是该渠道本身。

senses.title: Loose, action-based brushwork
senses.titleCN: 笔触奔放、以动作留下的画风
senses.definition: in painting, marked by visible sweeping movements of the hand or arm
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画中，以手或臂明显挥扫留下的痕迹为特征
senses.example: The portrait's gestural strokes suggest motion.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅肖像奔放的笔触暗示着运动。
senses.why: Modern painting made the painter's physical movement visible on the canvas, so the gesture became the style.
senses.whyCN: 现代绘画让画家的身体动作留在画布上可见，于是手势本身成了风格。

senses.title: Movement-based in dance
senses.definition: built from bodily movement as its main material
senses.definitionCN: 以身体动作为主要材料构建的
senses.example: The solo is purely gestural, with almost no music.
senses.exampleCN: 这段独舞纯粹以动作为本，几乎没有音乐。
senses.why: Dance strips expression down to movement, and this adjective marks that reduction.
senses.whyCN: 舞蹈把表达削减到动作本身，这个形容词标记的正是这种削减。

senses.title: Accompanying speech in linguistics
senses.definition: describing hand movements that run alongside speech and help organize it
senses.definitionCN: 描述与言语并行、帮助组织言语的手部动作
senses.example: Gestural cues help listeners resolve ambiguous sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 手势线索帮助听者消解歧义句。
senses.why: Speech is not alone; the hands add a parallel stream that researchers describe with this word.
senses.whyCN: 言语并不孤单；双手提供一条并行的流，研究者用这个词描述它。

senses.title: Controlled by hand movement
senses.definition: in computing, operated by movements of the hand or fingers instead of a mouse or keyboard
senses.definitionCN: 在计算中，用手或手指的动作而不是鼠标或键盘操作
senses.example: Gestural input replaced the mouse in the new interface.
senses.exampleCN: 在新界面里，手势输入取代了鼠标。
senses.why: Machines learned to read the hand, so the adjective moved from art and dance into interface design.
senses.whyCN: 机器学会了读手，这个形容词便从艺术与舞蹈进入界面设计。

senses.title: Physically shaping sound in music
senses.titleCN: 音乐中以身体动作塑造声音的
senses.definition: describing the conductor's or performer's use of bodily movement to shape sound
senses.definitionCN: 描述指挥或演奏者用身体动作塑造声音
senses.example: The conductor's gestural language was unusually clear.
senses.exampleCN: 这位指挥的手势语言格外清楚。
senses.why: A conductor shapes music through the air before a note is played, which is gesture used as instruction.
senses.whyCN: 指挥在音符响起之前就在空中塑造音乐，这是把动作当作指令。

senses.title: Signed rather than spoken
senses.titleCN: 以手语而非口语表达的
senses.definition: describing a language or utterance produced with the hands and body rather than the voice
senses.definitionCN: 描述用手与身体而不是嗓音产生的语言或话语
senses.example: Sign languages are fully gestural and fully grammatical.
senses.exampleCN: 手语完全是手势性的，也完全具备语法。
senses.why: A signed language is a complete language in the gestural channel, so the adjective can name its medium.
senses.whyCN: 手语是在手势渠道中完整运作的语言，因此这个形容词可以命名它的媒介。

intro.en: Gestural is an English adjective formed from gesture, which comes through Medieval Latin gestura from Latin gestus 'bearing'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gestural 是由 gesture 构成的英语形容词；gesture 经中世纪拉丁语 gestura 来自拉丁语 gestus「姿态」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gestus named the bearing or carriage of the body, from gerere 'to carry, perform'. The deeper origin of gerere is not established.
items.cn: gestus 指身体的姿态与举止，来自 gerere「携带、施行」。gerere 的更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Gestura carried the same meaning into Medieval Latin and then into French and English.
items.cn: gestura 把同一意义带入中世纪拉丁语，再进入法语与英语。

items.en: English gesture appears in the fifteenth century as a noun for a movement or bearing.
items.cn: 英语 gesture 在十五世纪出现，指动作或举止。

items.en: Gestural is recorded in the seventeenth century, formed with the English adjective suffix -al.
items.cn: gestural 在十七世纪见于记录，由英语关系形容词后缀构成。

items.en: The art sense describing loose, action-based brushwork belongs to modern criticism and the study of painting technique.
items.cn: 描述奔放、以动作为本的笔触这一艺术义属于现代批评与绘画技法研究。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of the adjective is not fixed, and the pre-Latin origin of gerere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个形容词确切的最早书证没有定论，gerere 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look alike or share the gesture root; group two holds near neighbours describing movement-based expression.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近或同出「手势」词根的词；第二组是描述「以动作为本的表现」的近义词。

entries.definition: The noun itself names the movement; the adjective describes whatever is made of or done with such movements.
entries.definitionCN: 名词本身命名动作；这个形容词则描述由这种动作构成或完成的事物。

entries.definition: It describes a style full of exaggerated gesture, not the general quality of being gestural.
entries.definitionCN: 形容充满夸张手势的风格，而不是一般意义上的「手势性的」。

entries.definition: It sounds close in art talk but comes from a word for weaving and refers to surface texture.
entries.definitionCN: 在艺术讨论中读音接近，但来自表示「编织」的词，指表面质地。

entries.definition: A German term for an organized whole; it shares a shape with this word but no Latin origin.
entries.definitionCN: 指有组织整体的德语术语；与这个词外形相似，但不同源。

entries.definition: It means done with the hands, often physical work; gestural stresses expression rather than labour.
entries.definitionCN: 意为用手完成的，常指体力工作；gestural 强调表达而不是劳动。

entries.definition: It covers every wordless channel; gestural is narrower and names the hand-and-body channel.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖所有无词渠道；gestural 更窄，命名手与身体的渠道。

entries.definition: It describes the strength of feeling shown; gestural describes the medium through which it is shown.
entries.definitionCN: 描述所显示情感的力量；gestural 描述显示它的媒介。

entries.definition: It relates to motion itself, especially in art; gestural adds the idea of meaningful bodily action.
entries.definitionCN: 与运动本身有关，尤其在艺术中；gestural 多出「有意义的身体动作」这一层。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the adjective suffix, the art sense and the modern interface sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：形容词后缀、艺术义与现代界面义。

normal.en: The noun names the movement; adding the adjective suffix makes a word for anything built from it.
normal.cn: 名词命名动作；加上形容词后缀，就得到描述由它构成之物的词。

normal.en: Art use: visible sweeping brushmarks are called gestural strokes.
normal.cn: 艺术用法：看得见的挥扫笔痕被称为挥洒式笔触。

normal.en: Dance use: a movement-only solo is a gestural piece.
normal.cn: 舞蹈用法：只靠动作的独舞是手势性作品。

normal.en: Technology use: a gestural interface reads the hand instead of a mouse.
normal.cn: 技术用法：手势界面读手，而不是读鼠标。

normal.en: Sign language is a fully gestural language, not a set of pantomime tricks.
normal.cn: 手语是完整的手势语言，不是一套哑剧把戏。

abstract.en: Picture a brush moving so fast that the movement itself stays on the canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象画笔快得让动作本身留在了画布上。

abstract.en: Picture hands shaping a sentence in the air for eyes instead of ears.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在空中为眼睛而不是耳朵塑出一句话。

abstract.en: Picture a conductor drawing a curve that becomes a phrase of music.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥画出的一道弧线变成了一段音乐。

examples.en: The museum labels the work as gestural abstraction.
examples.cn: 博物馆把这件作品标为手势性抽象画。

examples.en: Deaf communities use a fully gestural language with its own grammar.
examples.cn: 聋人群体使用一种有自身语法的完整手势语言。

examples.en: The new headset offers gestural control for simple commands.
examples.cn: 这款新头显为简单指令提供手势控制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 手势加「的」——凡是由手部动作构成的 → 手势的、挥洒式的

root: 英语 gesture 加关系形容词后缀；gesture 来自中世纪拉丁语 gestura，再上溯拉丁语 gestus「姿态」，源自动词 gerere「携带、施行」。gerere 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply the same adjective to different media: gesture in general, wordless messages, paint, dance, speech, interfaces, conducting and sign language.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用到不同媒介：一般手势、无词信息、绘画、舞蹈、言语、界面、指挥与手语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a visible trace of the hand left in air, paint or light.
core.cn: 核心意象：手在空中、颜料里或光线中留下的可见痕迹。

branches.en: GENERAL RELATION: the plain adjective for anything concerning gestures.
branches.cn: 一般关系：用于任何与手势有关之物的朴素形容词。

branches.en: WORDLESS LANGUAGE: a gesture system and a signed language both carry full meaning without speech.
branches.cn: 无词语言：手势系统与手语都能不用口语承载完整意义。

branches.en: PAINT: the painter's arm leaves its movement visible on the surface.
branches.cn: 绘画：画家的手臂把动作留在表面可见。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE: dance and conducting both shape expression through trained bodily movement.
branches.cn: 表演：舞蹈与指挥都通过训练有素的身体动作塑造表达。

branches.en: SPEECH AND MACHINE: hands run beside the voice and, in interfaces, replace the mouse.
branches.cn: 言语与机器：手与嗓音并行，在界面中还取代鼠标。

intro.en: Gestural is the adjective built on the gesture noun, and the family around it describes different kinds of bodily movement.
intro.cn: gestural 是在 gesture 这一名词上构成的形容词，它周围的词族描述不同类型的身体动作。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root gerere 'to carry, perform' produced gestus and gestura; English forms gesture, gestural and the verb gesticulate from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词根 gerere「携带、施行」产生 gestus 与 gestura；英语由同一词群构成 gesture、gestural 与动词 gesticulate。

items.example: A gesture carried the message.
items.exampleCN: 一个手势承载了信息。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 手势的或以手势完成的
items.example: The work is gestural from edge to edge.
items.exampleCN: 这幅作品从一边到另一边都是挥洒式的。

items.example: The scene was directed gesturally.
items.exampleCN: 这场戏是用手势语言指导的。

items.example: He gesticulated to make the point clear.
items.exampleCN: 他用力打手势把观点说明白。

items.example: Her gesticulation amused the class.
items.exampleCN: 她夸张的手势逗乐了全班。

items.example: The term is rare but follows the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这个术语罕见，但遵循同一构词模式。

items.meaning: a system controlled by hand movement
items.meaningCN: 用手部动作控制的系统
items.example: The game uses a gestural interface.
items.exampleCN: 这个游戏使用手势界面。

definition_zh: 家畜；牲畜（总称）
definition_en: farm animals kept for use or profit, considered together as a group
core_image: 围栏里牛、羊、马、骆驼挤在一起，耳朵上打着标记，栏外是草场
scene: 围栏门打开，牛群与羊群被赶向草场，耳标在阳光下反光，牧人骑着马在后面压阵。 Livestock must be counted before the winter feed is allocated.
sceneCN: 这里指「饲养的家畜整体」（第 1 个义项：牲畜总称）；句意为在分配冬季饲料前必须先清点家畜。

pos.zh: 家畜；牲畜（不可数集合名词）

derivatives.zh: livestock + farming（组合成分）→ 畜牧业（语义偏移：从动物群落到经营行业）
livestock + feed（组合成分）→ 家畜饲料
livestock + producer（组合成分）→ 畜牧生产者
livestock + unit（组合成分）→ 家畜单位（语义偏移：转为统计计量）
livestock + market（组合成分）→ 牲畜市场
livestock + guardian dog（组合成分）→ 护畜犬（语义偏移：指专门守护畜群的犬）

senses.title: Farm animals kept as a group
senses.definition: domesticated animals raised on a farm for food, work, fibre or profit, treated as one category
senses.definitionCN: 为食物、劳作、纤维或利润而在农场饲养的家养动物，作为一个类别看待
senses.example: The farm keeps livestock and grows fodder for them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场饲养家畜，并为其种植饲料。
senses.why: The compound joins live and stock, so the category is literally living property rather than animals seen one by one.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 live 与 stock 结合，因此该类别的字面义是「活着的财产」，而非逐只观看的动物。

senses.title: Cattle in a narrow regional use
senses.definition: cattle specifically, in regions where cattle are the dominant farm animal
senses.definitionCN: 在某些地区特指牛，因为牛是当地主要家畜
senses.example: In that county livestock means cattle, not sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个郡，这个词指牛，而非羊。
senses.why: A general category can be narrowed by local practice until the general word names the commonest member.
senses.whyCN: 泛指类别会被地方实践收窄，直到普通词指最常见的成员。

senses.title: Breeding stock
senses.definition: animals kept to produce young rather than to be sold or worked directly
senses.definitionCN: 为繁殖后代而饲养、而非直接出售或役使的动物
senses.example: Half the herd is breeding livestock kept for replacement heifers.
senses.exampleCN: 这群牛有一半是留作补充母牛的种畜。
senses.why: Stock also means a fund or supply, so animals kept to renew the herd are stock in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: stock 也有「储备、本钱」之义，因此用于更新畜群的动物正是严格意义上的「本钱」。

senses.title: Animals counted as capital
senses.definition: livestock viewed as a financial asset whose value is recorded and insured
senses.definitionCN: 被视为金融资产、需要记账与投保的家畜
senses.example: The bank valued the livestock before approving the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在批准贷款前对牲畜作了估值。
senses.why: The word's second element already means property, so the financial reading was present from the start.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的第二个成分本就意为财产，因此金融读法从一开始就存在。

senses.title: A herd on pasture
senses.definition: the animals while they are grazing or being moved across land
senses.definitionCN: 正在吃草或正被赶过土地的动物群
senses.example: Livestock graze the high pasture from June to September.
senses.exampleCN: 家畜从六月到九月在高地牧场吃草。
senses.why: The category becomes a moving collectivity when the animals are out on the land.
senses.whyCN: 当动物在土地上移动时，这个类别就变成一个移动的集体。

senses.title: Animals inside a mixed farm
senses.titleCN: 混合农场中的家畜环节
senses.definition: livestock as one component of a system that also grows crops
senses.definitionCN: 作为同时种植作物的系统中的家畜环节
senses.example: Mixed farming uses livestock to cycle nutrients back to the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 混合农业利用家畜把养分循环回田里。
senses.why: In a system, livestock is not only animals but a function: manure, traction and demand for fodder.
senses.whyCN: 在系统中，家畜不只是动物，还是一种功能：粪肥、畜力与对饲料的需求。

senses.title: A source of manure and traction
senses.definition: animals valued for dung, ploughing and transport rather than for meat or milk
senses.definitionCN: 因粪肥、耕地与运输而被重视，而非为肉或奶的动物
senses.example: On the small holding, livestock provide both manure and plough power.
senses.exampleCN: 在这块小地上，家畜同时提供粪肥与犁耕动力。
senses.why: Before engines, the living stock was the farm's energy system, and the word carries that memory.
senses.whyCN: 在发动机之前，活的家畜就是农场的能源系统，这个词带着那段记忆。

senses.title: Animals under herd-health control
senses.titleCN: 畜群健康管理中的家畜
senses.definition: the animals considered as a population to be monitored, vaccinated and quarantined
senses.definitionCN: 被视为需要监测、接种与隔离的动物群体
senses.example: Livestock movement is tracked to control disease.
senses.exampleCN: 为控制疫病，家畜的移动受到追踪。
senses.why: Veterinary medicine treats the herd as one unit, so the collective noun becomes a technical subject.
senses.whyCN: 兽医学把畜群当作一个单位，因此这个集合名词成为技术对象。

intro.en: Livestock is an English compound of live, living, and stock, a supply or fund. It names animals as living property and contrasts with dead stock, the tools and goods on a farm. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: livestock 是英语复合词，由 live「活着的」与 stock「储备、本钱」构成。它把动物命名为「活着的财产」，与 dead stock（农具与货物）相对。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stoc meant a tree trunk, a post or a fixed body, and from that came the sense of a stored supply or a fund.
items.cn: stoc 意为树干、柱子或固定主体，由此引申出「储备、本钱」之义。

items.en: Middle English stock covered goods, money and animals kept as a holding, so the word already implied property.
items.cn: 中古英语 stock 涵盖货物、钱与作为资产饲养的动物，因此这个词已含财产之意。

items.en: The compound live stock separated animals from dead stock, the implements and goods that do not breathe.
items.cn: 复合词 live stock 把动物与 dead stock（不会呼吸的器具与货物）区分开来。

items.en: The compound is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, first in estate accounts and farming manuals.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十六世纪的英语中已有记录，最早见于田产账目与农书。

items.en: Modern agriculture made livestock a sector word covering production, feed, units and health control.
items.cn: 现代农业使 livestock 成为部门词，涵盖生产、饲料、计量单位与健康管理。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact moment when live stock became one written word is not documented, and the deeper origin of stock is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：live stock 何时写成一个词没有确切记载，stock 的更早来源也属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on stock or live that are easily confused; group two holds collective words for farm animals.
note.cn: 第一组是由 stock 或 live 构成、易混淆的词；第二组是农场动物的集合名词。

entries.definition: A supply of goods, a fund, or shares in a company; livestock is specifically the living part of a farm's stock.
entries.definitionCN: 货物储备、资金或公司股份；livestock 特指农场储备中活的那部分。

entries.definition: Tools, machinery and unsold goods, the non-living property of a farm; it contrasts directly with livestock.
entries.definitionCN: 工具、机械与未售货物，即农场中非活的部分；与 livestock 直接相对。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning living or not yet dead; alone it does not name animals as property.
entries.definitionCN: 意为活着的、尚未死的形容词；单独使用并不指作为财产的动物。

entries.definition: The means by which someone earns a living; it looks like live plus stock but is built from a different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 某人谋生的手段；看起来像 live 加 stock，但第二个成分不同。

entries.definition: Domesticated bovines as a group; livestock is broader and includes sheep, goats, pigs and horses.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的家牛；livestock 范围更广，还包括羊、山羊、猪与马。

entries.definition: A group of animals of one kind kept together; livestock is a category, a herd is a particular gathering.
entries.definitionCN: 同类动物聚在一起的一群；livestock 是类别，herd 是具体的群。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for animals kept on a farm; livestock is its formal and commercial equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 农场饲养动物的日常说法；livestock 是其正式、商业化的对应词。

entries.definition: Animals used to pull ploughs or carts; they are one function of livestock, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 用于拉犁或拉车的动物；它们是家畜的一种功能，而非整个类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: live plus stock: living property, as opposed to dead stock.
normal.cn: live 加 stock：活着的财产，与 dead stock 相对。

normal.en: The family runs livestock, livestock farming, livestock feed, livestock unit, livestock market.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 livestock、livestock farming、livestock feed、livestock unit、livestock market。

normal.en: The word is uncountable: one says livestock, not livestocks.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数：说 livestock，不说 livestocks。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the sector: livestock production, livestock sector, livestock guardian dog.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示部门义：畜牧生产、畜牧部门、护畜犬。

normal.en: The old contrast with dead stock explains why live is inside the word.
normal.cn: 与 dead stock 的旧对照解释了 live 为何在其中。

abstract.en: Picture a farm ledger where animals and tools are written in two separate columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一本农场账簿，动物与工具分列两栏。

abstract.en: Picture a field that eats: the herd is a machine that turns grass into milk and manure.
abstract.cn: 想象一块会吃的田：畜群是一台把草变成奶与粪肥的机器。

abstract.en: Picture a moving warehouse of value, lowing as it crosses the road.
abstract.cn: 想象一座会移动的价值仓库，过马路时发出低鸣。

examples.en: Livestock accounted for half the family's income.
examples.cn: 家畜占了这个家庭收入的一半。

examples.en: The drought forced farmers to sell livestock early.
examples.cn: 干旱迫使农民提前出售家畜。

examples.en: Livestock health checks are required before any animal is moved.
examples.cn: 任何动物移动之前都必须做家畜健康检查。

dict_mnemonic.text: live（活的）+ stock（储备、本钱）→ 活着的本钱，即农场里能繁殖、产奶、干活、卖钱的牲畜总称。

root: live（古英语 libban「活着」）+ stock（古英语 stoc「树干、固定主体」，引申为储备、本钱）；与 dead stock（农具货物）相对，十六世纪起合为一词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one category: animals are first living property, then cattle by region, breeding stock, capital, a grazing herd, a farm function, a source of power and a monitored population.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个类别展开：动物先是活财产，再按地区指牛、种畜、资本、放牧畜群、农场功能、动力来源与被监测的群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a farmyard full of breathing property, each animal carrying a mark that says whose it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个装满会呼吸的财产的农家院落，每只动物都带着标记，说明它属于谁。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: all farm animals, or cattle alone where cattle dominate.
branches.cn: 类别：全部农场动物，或在牛占主导的地方单指牛。

branches.en: THE NEXT GENERATION: animals kept to renew the herd.
branches.cn: 下一代：为更新畜群而留的动物。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: animals with a price and an insurance entry.
branches.cn: 账簿：有价格、有保险条目的动物。

branches.en: THE LAND AND THE SYSTEM: grazing herds and the role animals play in mixed farming.
branches.cn: 土地与系统：放牧的畜群，以及动物在混合农业中的角色。

branches.en: POWER AND CONTROL: manure and traction, then vaccination and quarantine.
branches.cn: 动力与控制：粪肥与畜力，然后是接种与隔离。

intro.en: Livestock is a native English compound, not a Latin derivative; its parts are two old Germanic words, and its family is built by compounding.
intro.cn: livestock 是英语本族复合词，并非拉丁派生词；其组成部分是两个古老的日耳曼词，词族靠复合方式扩展。

latinIntro.en: Neither live nor stock has a reliable Latin relative, so the Latin side is left empty; the word's history is Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: live 与 stock 都没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；这个词的历史属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The first element separates animals from tools.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分把动物与工具分开。

items.example: The second element supplies the idea of property.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供财产之意。

items.example: Livestock wintered in the lower barn.
items.exampleCN: 家畜在低处的棚里过冬。

items.example: Livestock farming replaced the old wool trade.
items.exampleCN: 畜牧业取代了旧的羊毛贸易。

items.meaning: food grown or mixed for animals
items.meaningCN: 为家畜种植或混合的饲料
items.example: Livestock feed prices rose with the drought.
items.exampleCN: 家畜饲料价格随干旱上涨。

items.meaning: a standard measure of grazing demand
items.meaningCN: 衡量放牧需求的标准单位
items.example: One livestock unit equals one mature cow.
items.exampleCN: 一个家畜单位等于一头成年牛。

items.example: The livestock producer sold directly to the butcher.
items.exampleCN: 这位畜牧生产者直接把畜产品卖给屠户。

items.meaning: a place or trade for buying and selling animals
items.meaningCN: 买卖家畜的场所或交易
items.example: The livestock market opens before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 牲畜市场天亮前开市。

items.meaning: a dog bred to protect a herd
items.example: The livestock guardian dog slept among the sheep.
items.exampleCN: 护畜犬睡在羊群中间。

definition_zh: 放射性的；具放射性的；受放射性污染的
definition_en: emitting ionizing radiation because atomic nuclei are unstable, or relating to such emission
core_image: 一块泛着幽绿光的矿石旁边，盖革计数器的指针猛然跳起
scene: 这里指「放射性的」。 Uranium ore is radioactive, so it must be handled behind thick shielding.
sceneCN: 这里 radioactive 指「具放射性的」（第 1 个义项：原子核不稳定而自发发出电离辐射）；因此铀矿石必须在厚屏蔽后处理。图中可辨识物件：铀矿石、盖革计数器、辐射标志、铅手套。

pos.zh: 放射性的；具放射性的；与放射性有关的；受放射性污染的
放射性物质（多见于 radioactive(s) 的旧式说法）

senses.title: Emitting ionizing radiation
senses.titleCN: 具放射性的：原子核不稳定自发发出射线
senses.definition: giving off ionizing radiation because the atomic nuclei are unstable
senses.definitionCN: 因原子核不稳定而发出电离辐射
senses.example: Uranium ore is radioactive and sets off a Geiger counter.
senses.exampleCN: 铀矿石具有放射性，会让盖革计数器响起。
senses.why: The adjective joins radio- 'ray' to active 'doing': the material is actively giving out rays rather than merely reflecting them.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把表示「射线」的 radio- 与表示「起作用的」active 结合起来：材料在主动发出射线，而不只是反射射线。

senses.title: Relating to the phenomenon
senses.titleCN: 放射性现象的：用作技术修饰语
senses.definition: used in technical phrases to name the process or property of emitting rays
senses.definitionCN: 在技术短语中命名发射射线的过程或性质
senses.example: Radioactive decay follows a fixed half-life for each isotope.
senses.exampleCN: 每种同位素的放射性衰变都遵循固定的半衰期。
senses.why: Once the noun radioactivity was coined, the adjective became the general label for anything belonging to that phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: radioactivity 这一名词出现后，形容词便成为指属该现象的一般标签。

senses.title: Contaminated by radioactive material
senses.titleCN: 受放射性污染的：沾上了放射性物质
senses.definition: made dangerous by contact with radioactive material rather than by its own nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 因接触放射性物质而变得危险，而不是自身原子核不稳定
senses.example: The scrap yard was declared radioactive after the leak.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后，这家废料场被宣布受到放射性污染。
senses.why: Contamination spreads the label from the source to whatever the material touches, so objects can be radioactive without being radioactive substances.
senses.whyCN: 污染把这个标签从源头传播到材料接触过的一切，因此物品可以「受放射性污染」而本身并不是放射性物质。

senses.title: Of an unstable isotope
senses.titleCN: 放射性同位素的：指不稳定核素
senses.definition: describing an isotope whose nuclei decay spontaneously, often used before isotope or element names
senses.definitionCN: 形容原子核自发衰变的同位素，常用于 isotope 或元素名称之前
senses.example: Carbon-14 is the radioactive isotope used to date organic remains.
senses.exampleCN: 碳-14 是用来给有机遗存定年的放射性同位素。
senses.why: Chemistry distinguishes stable from unstable isotopes with this adjective, keeping the physical meaning close to the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 化学用这个形容词区分稳定与不稳定同位素，其物理含义紧贴第一义项。

senses.title: Used for dating
senses.titleCN: 用于定年：靠衰变速度推算年代
senses.definition: in geology and archaeology, describing a method that measures the decay of isotopes to estimate age
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学与考古学中，形容通过测量同位素衰变来估算年代的方法
senses.example: Radioactive dating placed the rock at about 2.5 billion years.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性定年把这层岩石测定在约 25 亿年前。
senses.why: Because decay runs at a steady rate, a radioactive clock can be read long after the event, and the adjective names that clock.
senses.whyCN: 由于衰变速率稳定，放射性时钟在事件发生很久之后仍可读数，形容词命名的正是这只钟。

senses.title: Associated with nuclear waste
senses.titleCN: 与核废料相关的：长期危险的工业产物
senses.definition: describing waste from reactors or weapons programmes that stays hazardous for a very long time
senses.definitionCN: 形容反应堆或核武器计划产生的、长期保持危险的废物
senses.example: Radioactive waste must be stored deep underground for thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性废物必须深埋地下，存放数千年。
senses.why: The nuclear industry extended the adjective to its by-products, where the danger lasts far longer than any human schedule.
senses.whyCN: 核工业把这个形容词扩展到其副产品，那里的危险远超任何人类时间表。

senses.title: Used as a tracer
senses.titleCN: 作示踪剂用的：让射线替人「看见」路径
senses.definition: describing a small amount of radioactive material used to follow movement through a body, pipe or plant
senses.definitionCN: 形容少量用于追踪物质在人体、管道或植物中运动的放射性材料
senses.example: A radioactive tracer showed where the fluid leaked from the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 放射性示踪剂显示出液体从管道何处泄漏。
senses.why: The emitted rays act as a signal, so a tiny amount of radioactive substance can reveal a path without being seen directly.
senses.whyCN: 发出的射线充当信号，因此极少量放射性物质无需直接可见也能暴露路径。

senses.title: Figuratively explosive
senses.titleCN: 比喻上「带辐射」的：碰不得的敏感议题
senses.definition: in informal speech, describing a topic or person so controversial that others avoid touching it
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容某话题或人物争议极大，别人都避而远之
senses.example: The old lawsuit became politically radioactive during the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 那桩旧诉讼在竞选期间变成了政治上碰不得的议题。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows the idea of invisible danger: as with real radioactivity, harm may follow mere contact, so people keep their distance.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻借用了「看不见的危险」：如同真实放射性，仅仅接触就可能受害，于是人们保持距离。

intro.en: Radioactive is a modern compound of radio- 'ray' and active, coined at the end of the nineteenth century when rays from uranium were first studied. Elements of the history remain uncertain.
intro.cn: radioactive 是 radio-「射线」与 active 的现代复合词，在 19 世纪末人们开始研究铀射线时被造出。其历史细节仍有存疑处。

items.en: The combining form radio- goes back to Latin radius 'spoke, ray'. It entered modern science through words for rays and radiant energy.
items.cn: 构词成分 radio- 可追溯到拉丁 radius「辐条、光线」，经由指射线与辐射能的科学词汇进入现代用语。

items.en: Active comes from Latin activus, built on agere 'to do, drive'. The pair radio- + active literally suggests 'actively ray-emitting'.
items.cn: active 出自拉丁 activus，基于 agere「做、驱动」。radio- 与 active 的组合字面上就是「主动发出射线的」。

items.en: The compound radio-active is generally attributed to Marie Curie's circle in 1898, in the period when polonium and radium were being isolated. The precise first printed use is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合词 radio-active 一般认为出自 1898 年前后居里夫妇的圈子，正值分离钋与镭的时期。最早的印刷使用确切出处存疑。

items.en: English quickly adopted radioactive for any substance giving off such rays, and radioactivity was formed as its noun.
items.cn: 英语很快用 radioactive 指任何发出这类射线的物质，并构成名词 radioactivity。

items.en: During the twentieth century the word spread from physics to medicine, industry, waste management and dating methods.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词从物理学扩展到医学、工业、废物管理与定年方法。

items.en: Attribution of the coinage is generally accepted rather than documented in every detail, and the exact first English citation remains uncertain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（创造归属与首见书证）：该词的创造归属属于「一般认为是」，并非每个细节都有文献可证；英语最早书证也仍存疑。

note.en: The first group separates adjectives and nouns of the same ray-family; the second gives near-synonyms for danger or instability.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「射线词族」中的形容词与名词；第二组给出表示危险或不稳定的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to radiation as a mode of energy transfer, especially heat. It says nothing about unstable nuclei or contamination.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为能量传递方式（尤指传热）的辐射，与原子核不稳定或污染无关。

entries.definition: The energy or rays themselves. Radioactive describes the source; radiation is what leaves it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能量或射线本身。radioactive 描述源头，radiation 指离开源头的东西。

entries.definition: The property or process of emitting rays. It cannot stand before a noun the way radioactive can.
entries.definitionCN: 指发出射线的性质或过程，不能像 radioactive 那样直接放在名词前。

entries.definition: The everyday word for broadcast communication or its equipment, shortened from radiotelegraphy; not a synonym for radioactive.
entries.definitionCN: 指广播通信或其设备的日常词，由 radiotelegraphy 缩略而来，并非 radioactive 的同义词。

entries.definition: In nuclear slang, 'hot' means radioactive or highly contaminated. It is informal and depends on context.
entries.definitionCN: 在核工业俚语中，hot 指具放射性或污染严重的；属口语用法，且依赖语境。

entries.definition: Describing a nucleus that may decay. Unstable states the cause; radioactive states the observable emission.
entries.definitionCN: 形容可能衰变的原子核。unstable 说的是原因，radioactive 说的是可观测的发射现象。

entries.definition: Made impure by contact with a harmful substance. It can be chemical or radioactive, so it is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 因接触有害物质而变得不纯；可以指化学污染，也可指放射性污染，范围更宽。

entries.definition: Relating to atomic nuclei or nuclear energy. A nuclear plant may handle radioactive material, but nuclear itself does not mean 'emitting rays'.
entries.definitionCN: 与原子核或核能有关。核电站会处理放射性物质，但 nuclear 本身不表示「发出射线」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: radio- 'ray' + active 'doing': the material is doing rays.
normal.cn: radio-「射线」+ active「起作用的」：材料在「做射线」。

normal.en: The family runs radioactivity, radiation, radioisotope, radionuclide, radiogenic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 radioactivity、radiation、radioisotope、radionuclide、radiogenic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: radioactive decay, radioactive waste, radioactive dating, radioactive tracer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：放射性衰变、放射性废物、放射性定年、放射性示踪剂。

normal.en: A Geiger counter clicks because the rays ionize gas inside it.
normal.cn: 盖革计数器会响，是因为射线电离了管内的气体。

normal.en: radiative is about heat transfer; radioactive is about unstable nuclei.
normal.cn: radiative 讲传热，radioactive 讲不稳定原子核。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that keeps warm by itself, never needing a fire, because the heat is made inside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块不用火也一直温热的石头，因为热从它内部产生。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible drizzle falling from a rock, which only a clicking meter can hear.
abstract.cn: 想象一场自岩石落下的无形细雨，只有会咔哒响的仪表听得见。

abstract.en: Picture a warning sign painted on a box that no one dares to open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被画上警示标志，没人敢打开。

examples.en: Naturally radioactive rocks release radon gas into basements.
examples.cn: 天然放射性岩石会向地下室释放氡气。

examples.en: The laboratory stores radioactive waste in lead-lined containers.
examples.cn: 实验室把放射性废物存放在衬铅容器里。

examples.en: Investigators used a radioactive tracer to locate the underground leak.
examples.cn: 调查人员用放射性示踪剂定位地下泄漏点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「射线（radio）一直在动（active）」——不停向外发出射线 → radioactive 放射性的

root: 拉丁 radius「光线、辐条」+ activus「活动的」（agere「做」）；1898 年前后由 radio- 与 active 合成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the physical property to its uses: unstable nuclei emit rays, and that emission becomes a hazard, a clock, a tracer, a metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从物理性质走向各种用途：不稳定核发出射线，而这一发射又变成危害、时钟、示踪剂与比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green-glowing ore making a meter needle jump.
core.cn: 核心意象：泛绿光的矿石让仪表指针猛跳。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: unstable nuclei emit ionizing rays, and the adjective names that process.
branches.cn: 性质本身：不稳定核发出电离射线，形容词命名这一过程。

branches.en: SPREAD BY CONTACT: the label moves from the source to whatever touches it.
branches.cn: 接触传播：标签从源头转移到它接触过的一切。

branches.en: THE ISOTOPE: chemistry uses the adjective to separate stable from unstable nuclear species.
branches.cn: 同位素：化学用该形容词区分稳定与不稳定的核素。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: steady decay becomes a clock, and emitted rays become a tracer signal.
branches.cn: 工具化：稳定衰变成为时钟，发出的射线成为示踪信号。

branches.en: LONG DANGER: industrial waste keeps the physical hazard, while politics turns it into a metaphor.
branches.cn: 长期危险：工业废物保留物理危害，政治则把它变成比喻。

intro.en: Radioactive is a modern scientific compound: a Latin-derived combining form for rays, plus an adjective of action, with -ity forming its noun.
intro.cn: radioactive 是现代科学复合词：拉丁来源的「射线」构词成分，加上表示动作的形容词，再由 -ity 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: The ray family includes radius, radiate, radiant, radiation, radiator and radio; the 'do' family includes act, action, agent, active and actor. Radioactive sits where the two families meet.
latinIntro.cn: 射线词族包括 radius、radiate、radiant、radiation、radiator、radio；「做」词族包括 act、action、agent、active、actor。radioactive 正处在这两个词族的交会处。

items.example: The isotope is radioactive for thousands of years.
items.exampleCN: 该同位素在数千年内保持放射性。

items.meaning: the property of emitting such rays
items.example: Radioactivity was discovered before its cause was understood.
items.exampleCN: 放射性的发现早于人们理解其成因。

items.meaning: the rays sent out, or the act of sending them
items.example: Radiation from the sample was measured hourly.
items.exampleCN: 每小时测量一次样品的辐射。

items.meaning: to send rays out from a centre
items.example: The metal radiated heat long after the fire died.
items.exampleCN: 火熄灭很久后，金属仍在散发热量。

items.example: The lab ordered a short-lived radioisotope.
items.exampleCN: 实验室订购了一种短寿命放射性同位素。

items.example: Radionuclides vary greatly in half-life.
items.exampleCN: 不同放射性核素的半衰期差别很大。

items.example: Radiogenic heat keeps the mantle slowly moving.
items.exampleCN: 放射性成因热使地幔缓慢流动。

items.example: The mail was irradiated as a precaution.
items.exampleCN: 邮件经过辐照作为预防措施。

definition_zh: 研究发现；调查结论；裁决；测得的数值；发现物
definition_en: a fact or piece of information discovered as the result of study or investigation
core_image: 一本摊开的记录册上，一行被红笔圈起，旁边贴着一枚小标签
scene: 研究室的桌上摊着一本记录册，负责人用红笔圈住其中一行，又在旁边贴上一枚标签，准备写进报告。 The main finding was that the drug lowered blood pressure without causing drowsiness.
sceneCN: 这里指研究或调查得出的一项发现（第 1 个义项：研究或调查中发现的事实）；句意为主要发现是这种药降低了血压，却没有引起嗜睡。图中可辨识物件：记录册、红笔、标签、报告草稿。

pos.zh: 发现；研究结论；裁决；发现物

derivatives.zh: 找到（过去式与过去分词）

senses.title: A fact discovered by study
senses.definition: a fact or conclusion reached through study or investigation
senses.definitionCN: 通过研究或调查得出的事实或结论
senses.example: The main finding was that the drug lowered blood pressure without causing drowsiness.
senses.exampleCN: 主要发现是这种药降低了血压，却没有引起嗜睡。
senses.why: Find meant to come upon something, and the ending names the thing come upon.
senses.whyCN: 动词词根意为碰到、找到，后缀命名被碰到的那件事。

senses.title: The conclusion of an inquiry
senses.definition: the formal conclusion of an official inquiry or review
senses.definitionCN: 官方调查或审查的正式结论
senses.example: The commission published a finding that the bridge had been poorly maintained.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会公布了一项认定，称这座桥维护不善。
senses.why: An inquiry is a search, and its end is the thing found, so the word moved into official reports.
senses.whyCN: 调查是一次寻找，终点是被找到的东西，这个词于是走进官方报告。

senses.title: A ruling in a court
senses.definition: a decision or determination made by a court or tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 法院或裁判机构作出的决定或认定
senses.example: The court's finding changed the terms of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭的认定改变了合同条款。
senses.why: Law borrowed the word for the fact a judge finds after hearing evidence.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词，指法官听取证据后认定的事实。

senses.title: A measured value
senses.definition: a value or observation obtained from an experiment or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 从实验或测量中得到的数值或观测
senses.example: One finding stood out: the treated group slept longer.
senses.exampleCN: 有一项发现很突出：处理组睡得更久。
senses.why: An experiment is a search for a number, and each number is something found.
senses.whyCN: 实验是在寻找一个数字，每个数字都是一样被找到的东西。

senses.title: An object uncovered
senses.definition: an object discovered during excavation or exploration
senses.definitionCN: 在发掘或勘探中发现的物件
senses.example: The excavation produced a finding that dated the site to an earlier period.
senses.exampleCN: 这次发掘出的一件发现物把遗址的年代推得更早。
senses.why: Archaeology finds things in the ground, and the word stays close to its oldest physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 考古学从地下找到东西，这个词贴近它最古老的实物义。

senses.title: Something seen on a scan
senses.definition: an observation made during a medical examination or scan
senses.definitionCN: 医学检查或扫描中观察到的情况
senses.example: A routine finding on the scan led to further tests.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描中的一项常规发现引出了进一步检查。
senses.why: Medicine reports what the eye or instrument finds inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 医学报告眼睛或仪器在体内找到的东西。

senses.title: A problem noted in an audit
senses.definition: a problem or weakness identified during an audit
senses.definitionCN: 审计过程中发现的问题或薄弱环节
senses.example: The audit reported a finding about missing receipts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计报告了一项关于收据缺失的发现。
senses.why: An audit searches records, and what it turns up is reported as a finding.
senses.whyCN: 审计是在翻查记录，翻出来的东西就作为发现报告。

senses.title: A lesson a learner takes away
senses.definition: a conclusion a student draws from an experiment or reading
senses.definitionCN: 学生从实验或阅读中得出的结论
senses.example: The students wrote one finding from the experiment in their journals.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把实验中的一项发现写进日志。
senses.why: When learners repeat a search, their conclusion is also something found.
senses.whyCN: 学习者重复一次寻找，他们的结论也是一样被找到的东西。

intro.en: Finding is the English noun from find, an inherited Germanic verb, with the native ending -ing. It is not a Latin word; the source is clear, while the date of the noun's first record is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词由英语动词 find 加本族名词化后缀构成，该动词是日耳曼语本族词，并非拉丁词；来源清楚，名词最早记录的年代不确定。

items.en: Findan meant to come upon or discover, and it is the direct ancestor of find.
items.cn: findan 意为碰到、发现，是「找到」这个动词的直接祖先。

items.en: The verb belongs to a Germanic family that also gives German finden and Dutch vinden.
items.cn: 该动词属于日耳曼词族，同族还有德语 finden 与荷兰语 vinden。

items.en: The native suffix -ing turns the verb into the name of the act or its result.
items.cn: 本族的名词化后缀把动词变成动作或其结果的名称。

items.en: The noun finding is recorded from the Middle English period; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词在中古英语时期已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Law gave the word a formal sense: the fact a court determines after hearing evidence.
items.cn: 法律给了它正式义：法庭听取证据后认定的事实。

items.en: Modern research made finding a standard countable unit of a paper, usually in the plural.
items.cn: 现代研究使这个名词成为论文里标准的可数单位，常用复数。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like finding; the second names neighbouring ideas of discovery and conclusion.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「本词」相近；第二组是「发现与结论」附近的其他说法。

entries.definition: The verb for coming upon something, and a noun for a discovery.
entries.definitionCN: 碰到某物的动词，也作名词指发现物。

entries.definition: A person who finds, or a device such as a viewfinder.
entries.definitionCN: 发现者，或取景器之类的装置。

entries.definition: The plural, used for a set of results in a report.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指报告中的一组结果。

entries.definition: The past tense of find; also a separate verb meaning to establish.
entries.definitionCN: find 的过去式；另有一个独立动词义为「建立」。

entries.definition: Affectionate; it looks close but belongs to another history.
entries.definitionCN: 喜爱的；形近却属于另一段词源。

entries.definition: The act or result of finding something previously unknown.
entries.definitionCN: 发现此前未知之物的行为或结果。

entries.definition: The judgement reached at the end of an inquiry.
entries.definitionCN: 调查结束时得出的判断。

entries.definition: The formal decision of a court or jury.
entries.definitionCN: 法院或陪审团的正式决定。

entries.definition: Something noticed and recorded during a study.
entries.definitionCN: 研究中注意到并记录下来的情况。

entries.definition: The broader word for any outcome, including one that is found.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何结果的更宽说法，包括被找到的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Germanic verb, the real legal sense and real research phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的日耳曼动词、真实的法律义与真实研究说法。

normal.en: Finding is find plus -ing: the thing you come upon after searching.
normal.cn: finding 是 find 加 -ing：寻找之后碰到的那件事。

normal.en: Find is a Germanic verb, not a Latin one, so the word feels native and short.
normal.cn: find 是日耳曼动词而非拉丁词，所以这个词短而本族。

normal.en: Law uses a finding for the fact a court determines, as in finding of fact.
normal.cn: 法律用 finding 指法院认定的事实，如事实认定。

normal.en: Research papers report findings in the plural because a study usually yields several.
normal.cn: 研究论文用复数 findings，因为一项研究通常产出好几条。

normal.en: An audit finding is a problem the auditor turned up.
normal.cn: 审计发现就是审计者翻出来的问题。

abstract.en: A finding is a piece of the world that has been made to speak.
abstract.cn: 一项发现是一小块被弄开口说话的世界。

abstract.en: The same fact can be a discovery in one field and a commonplace in another.
abstract.cn: 同一个事实在一个领域是发现，在另一个领域是老生常谈。

abstract.en: Findings are only as good as the search that produced them.
abstract.cn: 发现的好坏，取决于产生它的那次寻找。

examples.en: The finding was checked against a second data set.
examples.cn: 这项发现又用第二套数据作了核对。

examples.en: A single finding rarely settles a question on its own.
examples.cn: 单独一项发现很少能独自解决一个问题。

examples.en: The report lists each finding with the evidence behind it.
examples.cn: 报告列出每项发现及其背后的证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「翻顶」——翻找之后顶出来的一样东西：发现

root: 这个词由古英语动词 findan「找到、发现」加本族名词化后缀构成，该动词属日耳曼语本族词，不来自拉丁语；先指发现的动作，后指被发现的事实。法律认定与研究结论义为后起专门化；词源清楚，名词最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one thing found: a research fact, an inquiry conclusion, a court ruling, a measured value, an excavated object, a scan observation, an audit problem, and a lesson a learner keeps.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一件「被找到的东西」：研究发现、调查结论、法庭裁决、测得数值、出土物件、扫描所见、审计问题，以及学习者留下的体会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one line in a notebook circled in red, with a small label pasted beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录册里一行被红笔圈住，旁边贴着一枚小标签。

branches.en: THE STUDY AND THE NUMBER: a fact concluded from research, and a value read from an experiment.
branches.cn: 研究与数值：从研究得出的事实，以及从实验读出的数值。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL SEARCH: an inquiry and an audit both report what they turned up.
branches.cn: 官方查找：调查与审计都报告自己翻出来的东西。

branches.en: THE COURT: a judge's determination of fact becomes a finding.
branches.cn: 法庭：法官对事实的认定成为裁决。

branches.en: THE OBJECT AND THE BODY: something dug up and something seen on a scan.
branches.cn: 物件与身体：被挖出来的东西与被扫描看到的东西。

branches.en: THE LEARNER'S OWN: a student repeats the search and keeps one conclusion.
branches.cn: 学习者自己的一份：学生重复寻找，留下一条结论。

intro.en: Finding is a native English formation, so the Latin list is empty; the word is find plus -ing.
intro.cn: finding 是英语本族构词，因此拉丁词条留空；这个词是 find 加 -ing。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor in the immediate history of find; the relevant family is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: find 的直接词史里没有拉丁语祖先；相关词族是日耳曼语。

items.example: The Old English verb is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词是直接祖先。

items.example: The verb stayed short and native.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保持简短且为本族词。

items.example: The suffix builds finding, building and meeting.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示「发现」「建造」「会面」的三个名词。

items.example: The noun names the thing come upon.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名被碰到的那件事。

items.example: Reports usually use the plural.
items.exampleCN: 报告通常用复数。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀指人。

items.example: The old verb keeps an irregular past.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老动词保留不规则过去式。

items.example: Law fixes the phrase for a formal determination.
items.exampleCN: 法律把这个短语固定为正式认定。

definition_zh: n. 痛经；经期疼痛；原发性痛经；继发性痛经
definition_en: pain in the lower abdomen during menstruation, from mild cramps to pain severe enough to stop daily activity
core_image: 床头柜上热水袋与止痛药盒并排放着，日历上那几天被红笔圈出；诊室问卷的疼痛评分从 1 到 10 被圈到 8；超声屏上卵巢旁一个小囊肿横着测量线；女生蜷在沙发一角膝盖抵着小腹
scene: 床头柜上热水袋与止痛药盒并排放着，日历上那几天被红笔圈了出来，纸角已经卷起。 She was absent from work twice because of dysmenorrhoea.
sceneCN: 这里 dysmenorrhoea 指「经期出现的下腹疼痛」（第 1 个义项：痛经）；句意是她因为痛经两次没去上班。图中可辨识物件：热水袋、止痛药盒、被红笔圈出的日历。

pos.zh: 痛经；经期疼痛；原发性痛经；继发性痛经

senses.title: Pain during menstruation
senses.definition: pain in the lower abdomen during menstruation
senses.definitionCN: （名词）经期出现的下腹疼痛
senses.example: She was absent from work twice because of dysmenorrhoea.
senses.exampleCN: 她因为痛经两次没去上班。
senses.why: A hot water bag pressed against a lower belly while a calendar shows three days ringed in red.
senses.whyCN: 热水袋压在小腹上，日历上那三天被红笔圈了出来。

senses.title: The primary form
senses.definition: cramping pain with no underlying disease, common in the first years after periods begin
senses.definitionCN: （名词）没有器质性病变的痉挛性疼痛，多见于初潮后头几年
senses.example: Primary dysmenorrhoea usually begins within a year or two of the first period.
senses.exampleCN: 原发性痛经通常在初潮后一两年内开始。
senses.why: A school nurse log with the same three dates marked every month for one young student.
senses.whyCN: 校医记录本上，同一个年轻学生每个月都标着同样的那三天。

senses.title: The secondary form
senses.definition: pain caused by a condition such as endometriosis, often starting later in life
senses.definitionCN: （名词）由子宫内膜异位症等病症引起、往往较晚出现的疼痛
senses.example: Secondary dysmenorrhoea led the doctor to look for endometriosis.
senses.exampleCN: 继发性痛经促使医生去排查子宫内膜异位症。
senses.why: An ultrasound screen showing a small cyst beside the ovary with a measuring line across it.
senses.whyCN: 超声屏上卵巢旁有一个小囊肿，一条测量线横穿而过。

intro.en: Dysmenorrhoea is dys- meaning difficult, men- meaning month and -rrhoea meaning flow; put together the word names a monthly flow that comes with difficulty and pain.
intro.cn: dysmenorrhoea 由 dys-（困难）、men-（月）与 -rrhoea（流）组成；合起来这个词指称「来得艰难而疼痛的每月血流」。

items.en: The Greek prefix dys- means bad or difficult.
items.cn: 希腊语前缀 dys- 意为坏、困难。

items.en: Greek men means month, the same root behind menstrual.
items.cn: 希腊语 men 意为月，与 menstrual 同一词根。

items.en: Greek rhoia means a flow, giving the ending -rrhoea.
items.cn: 希腊语 rhoia 意为流，给出后缀 -rrhoea。

items.en: Medical Latin assembled the parts into a term for painful periods.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语把各部分拼成表示经期疼痛的术语。

items.en: Medicine split the term into a primary and a secondary form.
items.cn: 医学把这个术语分为原发性与继发性两型。

items.en: American writing drops one letter and spells it dysmenorrhea.
items.cn: 美式拼写省去一个字母，写作 dysmenorrhea。

note.en: Dysmenorrhoea shares dys- with dysentery and -rrhoea with diarrhoea, while amenorrhoea and menorrhagia change the prefix to name too little or too much flow.
note.cn: dysmenorrhoea 与 dysentery 共用 dys-，与 diarrhoea 共用 -rrhoea；而 amenorrhoea 与 menorrhagia 换了前缀，分别指经血过少与过多。

dict_mnemonic.text: dysmenorrhoea ＝ dys-（困难、坏）＋ men-（月，希腊语 men）＋ -rrhoea（流，希腊语 rhoia）＝「艰难的每月血流」＝痛经。记住 men- 就记住一串：menstrual 月经的、menstruation 月经、amenorrhoea 闭经（a- 无）、menorrhagia 经血过多。-rrhoea 家族还有 diarrhoea 腹泻（dia- 穿过）。临床分两型：primary 原发性（无器质病变，初潮后一两年起，痉挛样），secondary 继发性（由 endometriosis 子宫内膜异位症等引起，出现较晚）。美式拼写省一个 o：dysmenorrhea。

definition_zh: 肥力；生育力；繁殖力；想象力的丰富
definition_en: the quality of being fertile; ability to produce offspring or crops
core_image: 一张翻耕过的黑色农田在春雨里冒出嫩绿的苗芽
scene: 在春季农耕纪录片里，解说员说： This soil's fertility lets us grow three crops a year without chemical fertilizer.
sceneCN: 这里指「土壤中养分充足、能长出好庄稼的能力」（第1个义项：土壤让作物生长的性质）；句意为这片土壤的肥力让我们不用化肥也能一年三熟。

pos.zh: 肥力；生育力；繁殖力；想象力的丰富

derivatives.zh: 肥沃的；能生育的；想象力丰富的

senses.title: Soil or land that makes plants grow well
senses.definition: the quality of soil that allows it to support many strong crops
senses.definitionCN: 土壤能支撑大量茁壮作物生长的性质
senses.example: Farmers test the field every season to measure its fertility.
senses.exampleCN: 农民每个季节都检测田地以衡量其肥力。
senses.why: Fertility is the abstract noun of fertile, so it names the property that land has when crops grow easily on it.
senses.whyCN: fertility 是 fertile 的抽象名词，指的就是土地上作物容易生长的那种性质。

senses.title: Ability of animals or people to have children
senses.titleCN: 人类或动物的生育能力
senses.definition: the biological capacity to produce offspring
senses.definitionCN: 产生后代的生理能力
senses.example: Doctors measured his fertility before the marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在他结婚前检查了他的生育能力。
senses.why: The word carries the same root as fertile land because producing a child is, biologically, a kind of 'growth'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与 fertile land 共用词根，因为从生物角度看，生育也是一种「生长」。

senses.title: Rate of births in a population
senses.titleCN: 某一人口群体的生育率
senses.definition: the average number of children born to each woman or couple in a region
senses.definitionCN: 某地区每位女性或每对夫妇平均生育的孩子数量
senses.example: The fertility rate dropped sharply after the economic crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 经济危机后生育率急剧下降。
senses.why: Statistics uses fertility as the short form of 'fertility rate', the key number that demographers watch.
senses.whyCN: 统计学家把 fertility 作为 fertility rate 的简称，是人口学家最关注的数字。

senses.title: Medical treatment that helps conception
senses.definition: procedures or drugs used when a couple has trouble conceiving
senses.definitionCN: 夫妇难以受孕时使用的医疗手段或药物
senses.example: They tried fertility treatment for three years before a successful pregnancy.
senses.exampleCN: 他们尝试了三年生育治疗才成功怀孕。
senses.why: Fertility clinics and fertility treatment borrow the noun, focusing on the biological side.
senses.whyCN: 生育诊所与生育治疗借用了这个名词，聚焦在生理层面。

senses.title: Richness of imagination or ideas
senses.definition: the quality of producing many original ideas
senses.definitionCN: 能够产生大量原创想法的性质
senses.example: The fertility of his imagination made every lecture feel new.
senses.exampleCN: 他想象力的丰富让每一场讲座都别开生面。
senses.why: Just as fertile land yields many crops, a fertile mind yields many ideas; this is a common figurative extension.
senses.whyCN: 正如肥沃的土地长出很多庄稼，活跃的头脑产出很多想法，这是一个常见的比喻。

senses.title: Ability of eggs or sperm to function
senses.titleCN: 卵子或精子的存活能力
senses.definition: how effectively reproductive cells can unite to form a pregnancy
senses.definitionCN: 生殖细胞能够结合并形成怀孕的有效程度
senses.example: Freezing lowers egg fertility over time.
senses.exampleCN: 冷冻会慢慢降低卵子的受精能力。
senses.why: In biology, fertility is narrowed down to the viability of gametes, the smallest unit of reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 生物学里 fertility 被收窄到配子存活能力——这是生殖的最小单元。

senses.title: Season or place where growth peaks
senses.titleCN: 生长的高峰时段或地点
senses.definition: a period or region noted for abundant natural productivity
senses.definitionCN: 以自然生产力充足著称的时段或地区
senses.example: The annual flooding renews the fertility of the Nile delta.
senses.exampleCN: 一年一度的洪水恢复了尼罗河三角洲的肥沃。
senses.why: Rivers and flood plains are archetypes of fertility because they bring new soil every year.
senses.whyCN: 河流与冲积平原是 fertility 的原型，因为它们每年带来新的土壤。

senses.title: Figurative richness of a body of work
senses.definition: variety and abundance of themes or forms in an artist's output
senses.definitionCN: 艺术家产出中主题或形式的多样与充足
senses.example: Critics praised the fertility of the composer's late string quartets.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞了这位作曲家晚期弦乐四重奏的丰富主题。
senses.why: Critics borrow the agricultural metaphor: the artist's output is the 'crop' of their mental soil.
senses.whyCN: 评论家借用农业比喻：艺术家的产出就是他们精神土壤上的「庄稼」。

intro.en: Fertility enters English through French and Latin, keeping the root fert- that once meant 'to bear' and now means 'able to bear'.
intro.cn: fertility 经由法语和拉丁语进入英语，保留了词根 fert-——它原先的意思是「生」，现在是「能生」。

items.en: Latin fertilis meant 'bearing abundantly, fruitful', from the root ferre 'to bear, carry'. The suffix -itas turned it into fertilitas, the abstract noun for that quality.
items.cn: 拉丁语 fertilis 意为「产得多、果实多」，来自词根 ferre「生、携带」。后缀 -itas 把它变成 fertilitas——这个性质的抽象名词。

items.en: Old French fertileté borrowed Latin fertilitas, with the same meaning: the capacity to produce children or crops.
items.cn: 古法语 fertileté 借入拉丁语 fertilitas，含义相同：生育后代或作物的能力。

items.en: Middle English took fertileté directly from Old French, spelling it fertilitie by the 15th century.
items.cn: 中古英语直接从古法语借入 fertileté，到 15 世纪拼为 fertilitie。

items.en: Spelling settled to fertility in the 16th century, mirroring Latin fertilitas with its -ty abstract suffix.
items.cn: 16 世纪拼写固定为 fertility，用 -ty 抽象后缀呼应拉丁语 fertilitas。

items.en: By the 17th century, the word shifted from soil and bodies to minds, describing the 'bearing' of ideas and invention.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，词义从土壤与身体转移到头脑，描述想法与发明的「产出」。

items.en: From the 20th century, demographers shortened 'fertility rate' to fertility, giving it a precise numeric sense.
items.cn: 20 世纪起，人口学家把 fertility rate 简称为 fertility，赋予它一个精确的统计含义。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root fertile family members that share fert-; group two holds near-meaning abstract nouns for abundance.
note.cn: 第一组是同属 fert- 词根的 fertile 家族；第二组是语义相近的表示「丰富」的抽象名词。

entries.definition: Describes land, bodies or minds that produce much; fertility names the property itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容土地、身体或头脑产得多；fertility 命名的正是这个性质本身。

entries.definition: A substance added to soil to make it more fertile, not the quality itself.
entries.definitionCN: 加到土壤里让它更肥沃的物质，不是 fertility 这个性质本身。

entries.definition: The opposite of fertility: inability to produce offspring or crops.
entries.definitionCN: fertility 的反义词：无法产生后代或作物。

entries.definition: To make land or a body unable to produce; rare, opposed to fertilize.
entries.definitionCN: 让土地或身体失去生产能力的动词，罕见，与 fertilize 相反。

entries.definition: A formal synonym for fertility, used especially for reproductive or metaphorical productivity.
entries.definitionCN: fertility 的正式同义词，尤用于繁殖或比喻性的产出。

entries.definition: The state of producing many works, children or offspring; less biological than fertility.
entries.definitionCN: 产出很多作品、孩子或后代的状态；比 fertility 少生物学含义。

entries.definition: A large quantity; does not specifically imply the capacity to produce more, only that there is a lot.
entries.definitionCN: 大量存在；不特指生产能力，只说数量多。

entries.definition: The quality of growing thickly and richly; used for plants and hair, not people.
entries.definitionCN: 生长繁茂的性质；用于植物和头发，不用于人类。

normalIntro.en: fertility circles around the fert- root; link it to both growing plants and growing babies.
normalIntro.cn: fertility 围绕 fert- 词根；把它同时跟长庄稼和生孩子联系起来。

normal.en: fert- means 'to bear'; fertile land bears crops, fertile bodies bear children, fertility names the property.
normal.cn: fert- 意为「生」；肥沃的土地生庄稼，能生的身体生孩子，fertility 命名的就是这个性质。

normal.en: Think of Fertilizer, the substance you add to soil to boost fertility.
normal.cn: 想想 Fertilizer（肥料）——你加到土里提升 fertility 的东西。

normal.en: Fertility clinics treat people who cannot bear children.
normal.cn: Fertility 诊所治疗的是生不出孩子的人。

normal.en: The Nile's annual flood renews its famous fertility.
normal.cn: 尼罗河每年的洪水重新给它那著名的 fertility。

normal.en: A fertility of ideas comes from a fertile imagination.
normal.cn: idea 的 fertility 来自 fertile 的想象力。

abstract.en: Imagine a river delta where fresh mud arrives each year, always growing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每年都有新泥冲刷进来的河流三角洲，永远在生长。

abstract.en: Fertility is a quiet invisible force under soil and under skin.
abstract.cn: fertility 是土壤下和皮肤下一股安静看不见的力。

abstract.en: Numbers on a census page tracking something that declines slowly.
abstract.cn: 人口普查表上慢慢下滑的一串数字。

examples.en: The fertility of the floodplain keeps feeding a million families downstream.
examples.cn: 冲积平原的肥力持续养活下游一百万户家庭。

examples.en: Herbalists in the village claim the tea improves fertility.
examples.cn: 村里的草药师说这种茶能提高生育能力。

examples.en: Demographers expect fertility to rebound after the recession ends.
examples.cn: 人口学家预期衰退结束后生育率会回升。

dict_mnemonic.text: fer- = 生 → fertility = 生的性质

root: ferre（拉丁语，生、携带）→ fertilis（肥沃的）→ fertilitas → fertility。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one core image: something that 'bears' — soil bears crops, bodies bear children, minds bear ideas, and statistics bears numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个核心意象：某种「产出」之物——土壤产出庄稼、身体产出孩子、头脑产出想法、统计产出数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fertile field with dark soil and green sprouts pushing through after rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场雨后，黑土上冒出嫩绿芽尖的肥沃田野。

branches.en: AGRICULTURE: soil that grows crops well, and the season or ground where growth peaks.
branches.cn: 农业：能让庄稼长好的土壤，以及生长达到高峰的季节或地块。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: the ability to conceive, and the viability of eggs or sperm.
branches.cn: 生物学：受孕的能力，以及卵子或精子的存活能力。

branches.en: STATISTICS: the birth rate measured across a population.
branches.cn: 统计：在一个人口中测得的出生率。

branches.en: MEDICINE: the treatment given to help conception.
branches.cn: 医学：为帮助受孕而进行的治疗。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE RICHNESS: an abundant imagination, and the richness of a whole body of work.
branches.cn: 比喻性的丰富：丰沛的想象力，以及整部作品的丰厚。

intro.en: Fertility is formed on the Latin root fert- with an abstract noun suffix -ity; the fertile family also adds -ize, -izer, and -ile.
intro.cn: fertility 在拉丁词根 fert- 上加抽象名词后缀 -ity 构成；fertile 家族还能加 -ize, -izer, -ile。

latinIntro.en: fert- comes from Latin ferre 'to bear, carry', a root that also appears in confer, defer, transfer.
latinIntro.cn: fert- 来自拉丁语 ferre「生、携带」，这个词根也出现在 confer, defer, transfer 里。
