definition_zh: 出现；显现；（新事物的）产生、兴起；（生物）羽化、出土；（哲学）涌现；（从麻醉等状态）苏醒；古义：意外事件
definition_en: the act of coming into view or into existence; the rise of a new phenomenon, group, or idea; (biology) the appearance of an adult insect or a shoot above the surface; (philosophy and complexity science) the arising of properties not predictable from components; recovery from anaesthesia or a similar state; (archaic) an unforeseen event
core_image: 水面下浮起一个形状，先是一团模糊的暗影，然后破出水面，被光看见
scene: 池塘边，孩子指着水面：一只蜻蜓正从水下的幼虫壳里钻出来。 By the pond a child points at a dragonfly climbing out of its underwater shell: its emergence.
sceneCN: 这里 emergence 是「羽化、出水」（第 3 个义项：昆虫成虫从蛹壳或水中出来）；句意：池塘边，孩子指着一只正从水下幼虫壳里钻出的蜻蜓：这是它的羽化。图中可辨识物件：池塘、蜻蜓、蜕下的空壳、孩子的手。

pos.zh: 出现；产生；兴起（不可数，指过程；可数时指一次具体的出现）
（生物）羽化、出土；（哲学）涌现；（医学）苏醒（专业义）

forms.label: 复数（多次出现或多种涌现）

senses.title: Coming into view
senses.definition: the act of appearing or becoming visible after being hidden
senses.definitionCN: 原本隐藏的事物显现、变得可见的动作
senses.example: The emergence of a fin above the water told us a whale was close.
senses.exampleCN: 水面上露出一个鳍，说明鲸就在附近。
senses.why: Emergence is emerge + -ence, and emerge is Latin emergere, from ex- 'out' + mergere 'to sink, dip'. The word pictures something that was under a surface pushing its way out until it can be seen.
senses.whyCN: emergence 是 emerge + -ence，而 emerge 源自拉丁语 emergere，由 ex-“出”+ mergere“下沉、浸没”构成。这个词描绘的是原本在水面下的东西顶出来、直到被看见。

senses.title: Coming into existence
senses.definition: the process by which a new thing, idea, industry, or social form begins to exist
senses.definitionCN: 新事物、观念、产业或社会形态开始存在的过程
senses.example: The emergence of cheap solar power changed the economics of electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价太阳能的出现改变了电力的经济格局。
senses.why: Here the surface is historical rather than physical: a new phenomenon rises above the threshold of notice and becomes a fact in the world. English uses 'the emergence of' as a standard frame for tracing origins.
senses.whyCN: 这里的水面是历史性的而非物理的：新现象升到“可被注意”的阈限之上，成为世界中的事实。英语用 the emergence of 作为追溯起源的标准框架。

senses.title: Insect or plant breaking out
senses.definition: the appearance of an adult insect from its pupa or nymph case, or of a shoot above the soil
senses.definitionCN: 成虫从蛹或若虫壳中出现，或幼苗顶出土面
senses.example: The emergence of mayflies happens within a few warm evenings each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 蜉蝣的羽化每年春天集中在几个温暖的傍晚发生。
senses.why: Biology restores the literal image: the insect was enclosed, then it comes out. The technical noun for this is 'emergence', often paired with 'emergence trap' and 'post-emergence' in ecology and agriculture.
senses.whyCN: 生物学恢复了字面意象：昆虫本被包在里面，然后出来。这个专业名词就是 emergence，在生态学与农业中常与 emergence trap、post-emergence 搭配。

senses.title: Recovery from anaesthesia or coma
senses.definition: the return of consciousness after anaesthesia, sedation, or a coma
senses.definitionCN: 麻醉、镇静或昏迷之后意识的恢复
senses.example: The nurse watched for signs of emergence in the recovery room.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在恢复室观察患者苏醒的迹象。
senses.why: Medical usage treats unconsciousness as a medium: the patient is submerged in it and then emerges. The phrase 'emergence from anaesthesia' is fixed in clinical writing and keeps the same ex- + mergere structure.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把无意识视为一种介质：病人浸在其中，然后浮出。emergence from anaesthesia 是临床写作中的固定说法，保留同样的 ex- + mergere 结构。

senses.title: Emergent properties in complex systems
senses.definition: the appearance of collective properties in a system that cannot be predicted from its individual components alone
senses.definitionCN: 系统整体出现无法仅由单个组成部分预测的集体性质
senses.example: Philosophers debate the emergence of consciousness from complex neural networks.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家争论意识如何从复杂神经网络中涌现。
senses.why: Philosophy extends the 'coming out' image to levels of description: nothing in a single neuron predicts thought, yet thought emerges from the whole. The noun names the level-jump, not any one component.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把“出来”的意象扩展到描述层级：单个神经元里没有任何东西能预测思想，思想却从整体中涌现。这个名词命名的是层级跃迁，而非某个组件。

senses.title: Rise of a group or nation
senses.definition: the rise to prominence or power of a group, class, or country
senses.definitionCN: 某群体、阶层或国家走向显要或掌权
senses.example: The emergence of a middle class reshaped the country's politics.
senses.exampleCN: 中产阶级的崛起重塑了该国的政治。
senses.why: Social history uses emergence for collective actors entering the visible stage of politics. The word avoids saying they were created; it says they came into view and began to count.
senses.whyCN: 社会史用 emergence 描述集体行动者进入政治可见舞台。这个词不说他们被创造出来，而说他们进入视野并开始有分量。

senses.title: A fact becoming public
senses.definition: the point at which previously hidden information becomes known or public
senses.definitionCN: 此前隐藏的信息变得为人所知或公开的时点
senses.example: The emergence of the memo forced the minister to resign.
senses.exampleCN: 备忘录的曝光迫使部长辞职。
senses.why: Journalism borrows the water image for information: facts rise from concealment into the open. The noun marks the moment of visibility, which is why headlines say 'the emergence of new evidence' rather than 'the discovery'.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业把水的意象借给信息：事实从隐藏处浮到明处。这个名词标记可见性的时刻，所以标题说 the emergence of new evidence，而不说 the discovery。

senses.title: An unforeseen event (archaic)
senses.definition: an unexpected happening that requires immediate attention; the older sense from which 'emergency' developed
senses.definitionCN: 需要立即处理的意外事件；emergency 由此旧义发展而来
senses.example: In seventeenth-century prose, an emergence could mean a sudden crisis, not a slow appearance.
senses.exampleCN: 在 17 世纪的文本中，an emergence 可指突发的危机，而非缓慢的显现。
senses.why: This sense is historical. The same verb produced two nouns: emergence for the process of coming out, emergency for the urgent event itself. Modern English keeps them apart, and using emergence for a crisis now sounds archaic.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项属于历史用法。同一个动词产生两个名词：emergence 指“出来的过程”，emergency 指紧急事件本身。现代英语把它们分开，如今用 emergence 指危机显得古旧。

intro.en: Emergence is emerge + -ence, from Latin emergere 'to rise out, come forth', built on ex- 'out' and mergere 'to dip, sink'. The same mergere gives merge, submerge and immersion, so the family is really about surfaces and what lies beneath them.
intro.cn: emergence 是 emerge + -ence，源自拉丁语 emergere“升出、显露”，由 ex-“出”和 mergere“浸、沉”构成。同一个 mergere 还给出 merge、submerge、immersion，因此这个词族真正讲的是“表面”与“表面之下”。

items.en: Latin mergere meant 'to dip, plunge, sink'. With ex- 'out' it formed emergere 'to come up out of, rise out of'. The image is physical: something below a liquid surface pushes upward.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mergere 意为“浸入、下沉”。加 ex-“出”构成 emergere“从……中升出”。意象是物理的：液体表面之下有东西向上顶。

items.en: The noun emergentia is attested in Late Latin philosophical writing for 'a rising out'. The word reached English through French, with the -ence suffix marking a state or process.
items.cn: 名词 emergentia 见于晚期拉丁语哲学文本，义为“升出”。该词经法语进入英语，-ence 后缀标记状态或过程。

items.en: English emergence is recorded in the 1640s. Early examples often mean an unexpected occurrence, a sense soon taken over by emergency, which was coined from the same verb with -ency.
items.cn: 英语 emergence 记录于 17 世纪 40 年代。早期例子多指意外事件，这一义项很快被同一动词加 -ency 构成的 emergency 接管。

items.en: Entomology and botany fixed emergence for the adult insect leaving its case and the shoot leaving the soil. The date of this technical specialization is approximate but clearly nineteenth-century.
items.cn: 昆虫学与植物学把 emergence 固定为成虫离壳、幼芽出土。这一专业化的确切年代为大致估计，但明确属于 19 世纪。

items.en: In the twentieth century, emergence became a key term in philosophy and complexity science for properties of a whole that its parts do not individually possess. The usage extends the Latin 'rising out' to levels of organization.
items.cn: 20 世纪，emergence 成为哲学与复杂性科学的关键术语，指整体具有而部分单独不具备的性质。这一用法把拉丁语“升出”延伸到组织层级。

items.en: Today the word covers insects, industries, evidence and consciousness. The unifying test is always the same: something was below a surface or below notice, and now it is above it.
items.cn: 今天这个词覆盖昆虫、产业、证据与意识。统一的检验始终相同：某物原在表面之下或注意阈限之下，现在到了上面。

note.en: The first group separates words built on the same verb but with different prefixes or suffixes; the second group separates ways of describing something new.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一动词但前缀或后缀不同的词；第二组区分描述“新出现”的不同说法。

entries.definition: an urgent, dangerous situation requiring immediate action. It shares emergere with emergence but names the crisis, not the process of appearing.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立即行动的危险紧急情况。它与 emergence 共享 emergere，但命名危机本身，而非显现过程。

entries.definition: to combine into one. Latin mergere alone means 'to dip, sink'; without ex- there is no coming out, only going in.
entries.definitionCN: 合并为一。单用拉丁语 mergere 意为“浸入、下沉”；没有 ex- 就没有“出来”，只有“进去”。

entries.definition: to put or go under water. Sub- 'under' + mergere is the exact opposite direction from emergence.
entries.definitionCN: 使沉入水中或潜入水下。sub-“在下”+ mergere 与 emergence 方向正好相反。

entries.definition: the fact of being seen or present. It is neutral and static; emergence stresses the process of coming out from hiding.
entries.definitionCN: 被看见或存在的事实。它中性而静态；emergence 强调从隐藏中出来的过程。

entries.definition: movement to a higher position or status. It matches the upward half of emergence but lacks the idea of a concealing surface.
entries.definitionCN: 向更高位置或地位的移动。它对应 emergence 向上的那一半，但缺少“遮蔽表面”的意思。

entries.definition: the arrival of something important, from Latin advenire 'come to'. It is more formal and more final than emergence, which can describe a still-unfolding process.
entries.definitionCN: 重要事物的到来，源自拉丁语 advenire“来到”。它比 emergence 更正式、更带终结感，而 emergence 可描述仍在展开的过程。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the Latin pair ex- + mergere, the sibling nouns emergence and emergency, and everyday frames such as the emergence of new industries and emergence from anaesthesia.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：拉丁语 ex- + mergere 这一对成分、同源姊妹名词 emergence 与 emergency，以及 the emergence of new industries、emergence from anaesthesia 等日常框架。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + mergere 'sink': emergence is something sinking upward until it breaks the surface.
normal.cn: ex-“出”+ mergere“沉”：emergence 是某物一路向上、破出水面。

normal.en: Think of a diver coming up: the same verb gives emerge, emerge + -ence, and the opposite submerge.
normal.cn: 想一个潜水员上浮：同一个动词给出 emerge、emerge + -ence，以及反方向的 submerge。

normal.en: The emergence of an industry is a new thing crossing the line of notice, not being manufactured.
normal.cn: 产业的 emergence 是新事物越过“被注意”这条线，而不是被制造出来。

normal.en: A mayfly's emergence is literal: the adult leaves the nymph case and is suddenly visible.
normal.cn: 蜉蝣的 emergence 是字面意义上的：成虫离开若虫壳，突然可见。

normal.en: Emergence and emergency are siblings: one names the coming out, the other the sudden event that demands action.
normal.cn: emergence 与 emergency 是姊妹词：一个命名“出来”，一个命名需要行动的突发事件。

abstract.en: A surface is a promise: whatever is below it can become visible without being created.
abstract.cn: 表面是一种承诺：其下的东西不必被创造也能变得可见。

abstract.en: Emergence is a level-jump, not a sum: the whole shows something the parts never contained.
abstract.cn: 涌现是层级跃迁，不是求和：整体显露出部分从未包含的东西。

abstract.en: What rises into view also rises into consequence — visibility and power often arrive in the same moment.
abstract.cn: 升入视野的东西也升入影响——可见性与权力常常同时到来。

examples.en: The emergence of online learning changed how universities reach students.
examples.cn: 在线学习的出现改变了大学触达学生的方式。

examples.en: Biologists camp by the river to record the annual emergence of mayflies.
examples.cn: 生物学家在河边扎营，记录蜉蝣每年的羽化。

examples.en: The emergence of the secret report triggered a public inquiry.
examples.cn: 这份秘密报告的曝光引发了公开调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一摸紧，死”——一摸水面，紧跟着死寂的暗处冒出东西 → emergence 浮现、出现

root: e-/ex-（出）+ 拉丁语 mergere“浸、沉”+ -ence（状态名词后缀）；字面义“从水下升出”，核心是“原本在表面之下，现到表面之上”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of emergence all describe a crossing from below to above: from under water, under the soil, under anaesthesia, under notice, or under the level of individual parts. The word measures visibility and existence with the same surface metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: emergence 的八个义项都描述一次“由下到上”的越界：从水下、土下、麻醉之下、注意阈限之下，或从个体部分的层级之下。这个词用同一个表面隐喻同时度量“可见”与“存在”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shape rising from below a surface until it breaks through and can be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个形状从表面之下升起，直到破面而出、可以被看见。

branches.en: VISIBILITY: a hidden thing or fact crosses the line of notice and becomes seen or public.
branches.cn: 可见性：隐藏的事物或事实越过注意线，变得可见或公开。

branches.en: EXISTENCE AND POWER: a new industry, class, or nation rises into historical consequence.
branches.cn: 存在与权力：新产业、阶层或国家升入历史影响。

branches.en: LIVING SURFACES: an insect leaves its case, a shoot leaves the soil, a patient leaves anaesthesia.
branches.cn: 生命表面：昆虫离壳、幼芽出土、病人脱离麻醉。

branches.en: LEVEL JUMP: collective properties appear that no single component contains.
branches.cn: 层级跃迁：出现任何单个组件都不包含的集体性质。

branches.en: HISTORICAL SENSE: the same verb once named a sudden event, now carried by its sibling emergency.
branches.cn: 历史义：同一动词曾指突发事件，现由姊妹词 emergency 承担。

intro.en: Emergence is a suffix-rich word: emerge + -ence, with the verb itself made of a Latin prefix and root. The set shows how one verb spawns process nouns, adjectives, and a look-alike sibling noun.
intro.cn: emergence 是后缀丰富的词：emerge + -ence，而动词本身由拉丁前缀与词根构成。这组词展示同一个动词如何产生过程名词、形容词，以及一个形近的姊妹名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin core is mergere 'to sink'. With ex- it yields emergere 'rise out'; with sub- it yields submergere 'sink under'. The noun suffixes -ence and -ency later split into emergence and emergency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁核心是 mergere“下沉”。加 ex- 得 emergere“升出”；加 sub- 得 submergere“沉入”。名词后缀 -ence 与 -ency 后来分化出 emergence 与 emergency。

items.meaning: the process of coming out or into existence
items.meaningCN: 出现；涌现（-ence 构成过程名词）
items.example: The emergence of the market took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这个市场的形成用了十年。

items.meaning: to come out from below a surface
items.meaningCN: 出现；浮现（字面“从下沉中出来”）
items.example: The sun emerged from behind the clouds.
items.exampleCN: 太阳从云后露出来。

items.meaning: newly appearing; arising as a whole
items.meaningCN: 新出现的；涌现的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.example: Emergent behavior appears only when many agents interact.
items.exampleCN: 涌现行为只在多个主体互动时才出现。

items.meaningCN: 新兴的；正在形成的（-ing 分词形容词）
items.example: Emerging economies grew faster than mature ones.
items.exampleCN: 新兴经济体的增长快于成熟经济体。

items.meaning: an urgent situation that suddenly arises
items.meaningCN: 紧急情况（-ency 构成状态名词）
items.example: The hospital declared a public emergency.
items.exampleCN: 医院宣布进入公共紧急状态。

items.meaningCN: 合并（单用 mergere，无“出”前缀）
items.example: The two firms merged last year.
items.exampleCN: 两家公司去年合并。

items.meaning: to put or go under a surface
items.example: The flood submerged the lower fields.
items.exampleCN: 洪水淹没了低处的田地。

items.meaning: the act of coming out of a liquid; rare, chiefly astronomy
items.meaningCN: 出液；复现（罕用，多用于天文）
items.example: The emersion of the star was timed precisely.
items.exampleCN: 这颗星的复现时间被精确记录。

definition_zh: 注册入学；登记加入；注册人数；名册
definition_en: the act of putting a name on an official list, especially of students, members or patients, and the number or record so produced
core_image: 注册处的长桌：一本摊开的名册，笔尖一行行落下名字，桌角摞着填好的表格
scene: 开学前的走廊里，几张长桌并排摆开，工作人员把摊开的名册压住纸角，学生们排着队等候，走廊尽头的钟还没到点。 Enrollment for the summer session closed two days early.
sceneCN: 这里指「注册入学」这一动作（第 1 个义项：把名字正式列入学生名册）；句意为夏季学期的注册提前两天截止。图中可辨识物件：摊开的名册、签字笔、表格摞、排队的学生。

pos.zh: 注册；登记加入；注册人数（可数指具体人数或名册）
（美式拼写）入学注册；英式写法只单写一个字母

senses.title: The act of registering as a student
senses.titleCN: 注册入学（学生登记动作）
senses.definition: the act of entering a student's name on a school's official list
senses.definitionCN: 把学生姓名正式列入学校名册的行为
senses.example: Enrollment for the summer session closed two days early.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季学期的注册提前两天截止。
senses.why: the noun of action built from the verb, so it names the doing before it names any result.
senses.whyCN: 由动词派生的动作名词，因此先指「做」这件事，再指结果。

senses.title: The number registered
senses.definition: the count of people recorded on the list at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时点记在名册上的人数
senses.example: Total enrollment passed twenty thousand this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年总注册人数超过了两万。
senses.why: counting offices turned the action noun into a tally, which is the commonest everyday use today.
senses.whyCN: 统计部门把动作名词改成数字，这是今天最常见的日常用法。

senses.title: Joining a program or trial
senses.titleCN: 登记加入项目、试验或计划
senses.definition: the act of signing up for a program, study or benefit scheme rather than for a school
senses.definitionCN: 为项目、研究或福利计划报名，而非为学校注册的行为
senses.example: Enrollment in the drug trial requires a doctor's referral.
senses.exampleCN: 参加药物试验的登记需要医生转介。
senses.why: the school sense was generalized: any official list has an act of joining it.
senses.whyCN: 学校义被推广：任何正式名册都有「加入」这一动作。

senses.title: The sign-up window
senses.definition: the fixed period during which names may be added to the list
senses.definitionCN: 允许把名字加入名册的固定时段
senses.example: The enrollment window lasts three weeks each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 每年秋天的注册窗口持续三周。
senses.why: a period reading grew out of the action: if joining takes time, the time itself gets the name.
senses.whyCN: 由动作义长出时段义：既然加入需要时间，时间本身就得了这个名字。

senses.title: The register itself
senses.definition: the list or record on which the names are kept
senses.definitionCN: 保存这些姓名的名单或记录
senses.example: Officials checked the enrollment against the tax records.
senses.exampleCN: 官员把注册名册与税务记录核对。
senses.why: metonymy did the work: the act, then the paper that records the act.
senses.whyCN: 转喻在起作用：先是动作，再是记录动作的那张纸。

senses.title: The act of taking people in
senses.titleCN: 招收；把学生收入名册（机构视角）
senses.definition: an institution's act of admitting and recording new students
senses.definitionCN: 机构录取并把新生记入名册的行为
senses.example: The district limits enrollment to residents of the county.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区把招收范围限制在本县居民。
senses.why: the same noun is read from the institution's side, where the action is admission rather than application.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从机构一侧读，动作就成了录取而非申请。

senses.title: Recording a category in a scheme
senses.titleCN: 把某类人纳入统计口径
senses.definition: the inclusion of a group in an official count or scheme
senses.definitionCN: 把某一群体纳入正式统计或制度安排
senses.example: Enrollment of part-time students changed the funding formula.
senses.exampleCN: 把兼读学生纳入统计改变了拨款公式。
senses.why: statistical writing extended the word from people joining to categories being counted.
senses.whyCN: 统计文本把词从「人加入」扩展到「类别被计入」。

senses.title: A state of being inside a system
senses.titleCN: 抽象：被正式纳入某个体系的状态
senses.definition: the condition of being formally included in an organization or scheme
senses.definitionCN: 被正式纳入某个组织或制度安排的状态
senses.example: Union enrollment gave the workers a shared voice.
senses.exampleCN: 加入工会使工人们有了共同的声音。
senses.why: the result reading is pushed further: what is gained is not a place on a list but standing inside a body.
senses.whyCN: 结果义再推一步：得到的不是名册上的一行，而是身处某个团体之中的资格。

intro.en: Enrollment is enroll plus the noun ending -ment; enroll goes back through Old French to Latin rotulus 'little roll', the scroll on which names were written.
intro.cn: 这个词由动词 enroll 加名词词尾 -ment 构成；enroll 经古法语上溯到拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，即写名字用的那卷纸。

items.en: Rotulus, a diminutive of rota 'wheel', meant a little roll of parchment; officials kept names on such rolls.
items.cn: rotulus 是 rota「轮子」的指小形式，指一小卷羊皮纸；官员把名字记在这种卷上。

items.en: Old French took the word as rolle, the scroll or list on which a name was entered.
items.cn: 古法语把它写作 rolle，指名册所用的卷轴或清单。

items.en: English roll still means a list of names, as in the class roll or the voters' roll.
items.cn: 英语 roll 至今仍指名单，如班级名册、选民册。

items.en: The verb, with a prefix meaning 'in', entered English in the fourteenth century and meant to write a name onto the roll.
items.cn: 这个动词带着表示「进入」的前缀在十四世纪进入英语，意为把名字写进名册。

items.en: The noun of action added a suffix meaning 'the act or result of' and soon also named the number recorded.
items.cn: 加表示「动作或结果」的词尾构成动作名词，随后也指记录下来的数量。

items.en: Dating note: the earliest noun citations are approximate, and the step from 'roll' to 'count of students' is generally accepted but not dated precisely.
items.cn: 年代说明：该名词的最早书证只是约数；从「卷轴」到「学生人数」的演变一般认为是自然引申，但确切年代无定论。

note.en: Group one holds spelling variants and relatives of the same word; group two holds other nouns for entering an institution.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的拼写变体与同族词；第二组是其他表示进入机构的名称。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun, with one l; American usage doubles the l.
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式拼写，只保留一个重复的辅音字母；美式则写两遍。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun; the noun names the act, the verb names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词；名词指动作，动词指「做」。

entries.definition: A person who has enrolled; the noun shifts from the act to the individual.
entries.definitionCN: 已注册的人；名词从动作转到个人。

entries.definition: The old word for the parchment list, still used for registers of names.
entries.definitionCN: 指羊皮纸名单的旧词，至今仍用于各种名册。

entries.definition: A broader word for official recording, used of cars, voters and patients as well as students.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的正式登记说法，除学生外也用于车辆、选民与病人。

entries.definition: The institution's act of letting someone in; enrollment adds the step of writing the name down.
entries.definitionCN: 机构允许进入的行为；注册则补上「把名字写下」这一步。

entries.definition: The number or group admitted in one period, viewed as a batch rather than a process.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时期录取的人数或群体，被当作一批而非一个过程。

entries.definition: The formal ceremony or act of entering a university register; narrower and more ceremonial.
entries.definitionCN: 正式进入大学名册的行为或仪式，范围更窄、更具仪式性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphology, real phrases and real school office scenes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实构词、真实搭配与真实的注册处场景。

normal.en: A prefix meaning 'in' plus roll, the old word for a list: to write a name into the list.
normal.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀加「名册」的旧说法：把名字写进名单。

normal.en: The noun of action also became the count, so the same word answers 'what happened' and 'how many'.
normal.cn: 动作名词也兼指数量，因此同一个词既回答「发生了什么」，也回答「有多少」。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: total enrollment, enrollment rate, enrollment period.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：总注册人数、注册率、注册期。

normal.en: The British spelling uses a single l, the American doubles it.
normal.cn: 英式拼写只保留一个重复的辅音字母，美式则把这个字母写两遍。

normal.en: Picture the registrar's desk, where the act and the number are the same page.
normal.cn: 想象注册处那张桌子，动作与数字就写在同一页上。

abstract.en: Picture a rope being rolled up with names caught between its layers.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷绳子被卷起，名字夹在层与层之间。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only while a clerk holds a pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门只在职员握笔时才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a tide line on the sand: what is written stays after the water leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象沙滩上的潮线：水退去后，写下的痕迹还在。

examples.en: Enrollment for the summer session closed two days early.
examples.cn: 夏季学期的注册提前两天截止。

examples.en: Total enrollment passed twenty thousand, the highest in the college's history.
examples.cn: 总注册人数超过两万，创下该学院历史新高。

examples.en: The clinic reported steady enrollment in its vaccination program.
examples.cn: 诊所报告其疫苗接种项目的登记人数保持稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「入」加「名册」再加「名词尾」：把名字写进名册这件事 → 注册入学

root: 由动词 enroll 加名词词尾 -ment 构成；enroll 经古法语 rolle 上溯拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」，而 rotulus 是 rota「轮子」的指小形式，指卷起的羊皮纸名单。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses follow one pen stroke: a name goes onto a list, and that single act yields a count, a window, a register, an admissions decision, a statistical category and finally a place inside a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一笔下去：名字落进名册，这一个动作又生出人数、时段、名册、录取决定、统计类别，最后生出「身处某个团体」的资格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long desk with an open roll of names, a pen resting on the line just filled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，摊开的名册上刚写满一行，笔还停在那一行。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE CATEGORY: one name written down, then a whole group counted in.
branches.cn: 动作与类别：先是一个名字被写下，再是一整类人被计入。

branches.en: NUMBER AND WINDOW: the tally read off the page, and the period the page stays open.
branches.cn: 数字与时段：从纸面读出的人数，以及名册开放的时段。

branches.en: JOINING AND RECORD: signing up for a program, and the paper that keeps the sign-up.
branches.cn: 加入与记录：为项目报名，以及保存这份报名的纸页。

branches.en: THE OTHER SIDE: the institution doing the admitting rather than the person applying.
branches.cn: 另一侧：做录取动作的是机构，而非申请人。

branches.en: INSIDE A BODY: what is gained is not a line on paper but standing within an organization.
branches.cn: 身在团体：得到的不是纸上的一行，而是组织之中的资格。

intro.en: Enrollment is a prefix, a base and a noun ending; the same pieces build the verb, the British spelling and the name of the person enrolled.
intro.cn: 这个词由前缀、词干与名词词尾构成；同样的部件还构成动词、英式拼写与注册者的名称。

latinIntro.en: Latin rotulus 'little roll' gives roll, enroll and enrollment; rota 'wheel' is its parent word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rotulus「小卷轴」衍生出 roll、enroll 与 enrollment；其母词 rota 意为「轮子」。

items.example: The prefix marks putting a name into the list.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示把名字放进名册。

items.structure: roll (base word, from Latin rotulus 'little roll')
items.meaning: a list or scroll of names
items.example: A roll of names was kept at the town office.
items.exampleCN: 镇公所保存着一卷名单。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of the deed.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成行为的名词。

items.meaning: to write a name onto a list
items.example: Students enroll at the start of term.
items.exampleCN: 学生在学期开始时注册。

items.meaning: the act or the count of registering
items.example: Enrollment closes before classes begin.
items.exampleCN: 注册在开课之前截止。

items.meaning: the same noun in British usage
items.meaningCN: 英式拼写下的同一名词
items.example: British forms ask for enrolment by post.
items.exampleCN: 英式表格要求邮寄办理注册。

items.example: Each enrollee receives a card.
items.exampleCN: 每位注册者会领到一张卡。

items.meaning: to remove a name from the list
items.example: The family chose to disenroll after the move.
items.exampleCN: 这家人搬家后选择了注销注册。

definition_zh: 过度详述；反复抨击；毒打
definition_en: to explain or argue something at excessive length; to attack or beat hard
core_image: 同一根钉子被锤了一遍又一遍
scene: 会议已超时，经理仍对那一点念念不忘。 The manager belabored the same minor point for half an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 belabored 是「过度详述」（第 1 个义项：对某点纠缠过久）；句意是经理把同一个小问题翻来覆去讲了半小时。

pos.zh: 过度详述；抨击；殴打

collocations.zh: 把显而易见的事翻来覆去讲

derivatives.zh: 基础词（英式拼写 labor 为美式），义为「劳动；辛劳」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「被过度渲染的；冗长乏味的」

senses.title: To dwell on at excessive length
senses.definition: to explain or argue something longer than necessary
senses.definitionCN: 对某事讲解或争辩得超过必要限度
senses.example: The manager belabored the same minor point for half an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 经理把同一个小问题翻来覆去讲了半小时。
senses.why: Beating a subject with words copies the older sense of beating with blows.
senses.whyCN: 用言语「捶打」话题，正是旧义「以拳脚击打」的转喻。

senses.title: To attack or beat
senses.definition: to strike someone physically, or to attack with words
senses.definitionCN: 以拳脚击打某人，或以言辞抨击
senses.example: The critics belabored the play from every angle.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家们从各个角度猛烈抨击这出戏。
senses.why: The root labor as a verb meant to work over, that is, to pound.
senses.whyCN: 词根 labor 作动词本义「反复捶打、加工」。

intro.en: Belabor puts be- before labor, to work a thing over.
intro.cn: belabor 在 labor 前加 be-，意为「对某物反复加工」。

items.en: laborare meant to toil or struggle.
items.cn: 拉丁语 laborare 意为「劳作、挣扎」。

items.en: labour passed into English through Old French.
items.cn: labor 经古法语进入英语。

items.en: belaboren meant to beat or pound upon.
items.cn: 中古英语 belaboren 意为「击打、捶打」。

items.en: the verbal sense of overworking an argument emerged.
items.cn: 十六至十七世纪出现「就论点反复纠缠」的引申义。

items.en: belabor a point is now the dominant use.
items.cn: 如今 belabor a point 成为主导用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the be- prefix or the labor root; the near-meaning group gathers dwelling-on and attacking words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 be- 前缀或 labor 词根；近义组汇集纠缠与抨击类词。

entries.definition: past form in British spelling
entries.definitionCN: 英式拼写的过去式（belaboured）

entries.definition: worked out in detail
entries.definitionCN: 详尽的——同含 labor 词根，义为「加工出」

entries.definition: to work together
entries.definitionCN: 合作——同含 labor 词根

entries.definition: to keep thinking or talking about
entries.definitionCN: 老是想着/谈着；强调停留不去

entries.definition: to repeat forcefully
entries.definitionCN: 反复敲打；强调持续施力

entries.definition: to attack strongly
entries.definitionCN: 抨击；对应「攻击」一义

normalIntro.en: Belabor is be- plus labor: keep working a point over.
normalIntro.cn: belabor 是 be- 加 labor：对同一个点反复加工。

normal.en: Belabor a point means to over-explain it.
normal.cn: belabor a point 指对某点过度纠缠。

normal.en: The root labor means work or toil.
normal.cn: 词根 labor 意为「劳作」。

normal.en: Elaborate and collaborate share the root.
normal.cn: elaborate 与 collaborate 共享此词根。

senses.title: The earth's great circle
senses.titleCN: 地球赤道：与两极等距的大圆
senses.definition: the great circle around the earth that lies halfway between the north and south poles and marks zero latitude
senses.definitionCN: 绕地球一圈、位于南北两极正中并标出零度纬线的大圆
senses.example: The river crosses the equator twice on its long course.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河在漫长的流程中两次越过赤道。
senses.why: Latin aequator meant 'equalizer'; the circle is named for making day and night equal, and it is the zero line from which latitude is counted.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 aequator 意为「使相等者」；这条圈因使昼夜等长而得名，也是计算纬度的零度线。

senses.title: The equatorial region
senses.titleCN: 赤道地区：赤道两侧的湿热地带
senses.definition: the hot, humid belt of the earth near the equator
senses.definitionCN: 赤道附近炎热潮湿的地带
senses.example: Rubber plantations thrive in the equator's rain belt.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶园在赤道雨带里生长旺盛。
senses.why: The line marks a climate as well as a coordinate, so the region around it is called the equator in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 这条线既标坐标也标气候，因此它周围的地区在日常说法里也叫 the equator。

senses.title: The celestial equator
senses.titleCN: 天赤道：天球上与地球赤道对应的大圆
senses.definition: the great circle on the celestial sphere lying in the plane of the earth's equator
senses.definitionCN: 天球上位于地球赤道平面内的大圆
senses.example: The sun crosses the celestial equator at the equinoxes.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳在二分点时穿过天赤道。
senses.why: Astronomers projected the earth's equator onto the sky, where it serves as the zero line for declination.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家把地球赤道投影到天空，用作赤纬的零度线。

senses.title: The magnetic equator
senses.titleCN: 磁赤道：地磁场的零倾角线
senses.definition: the line around the earth where a magnetic needle stays horizontal and magnetic dip is zero
senses.definitionCN: 地球表面磁针保持水平、磁倾角为零的连线
senses.example: Compasses behave differently near the magnetic equator.
senses.exampleCN: 在磁赤道附近，指南针的表现不同。
senses.why: The magnetic field has its own symmetry plane, so it produces an 'equator' that does not match the geographic one.
senses.whyCN: 磁场有自己的对称面，因此产生一条与地理赤道不重合的「赤道」。

senses.title: The thermal equator
senses.titleCN: 热赤道：地表年均最高温的连线
senses.definition: the line of highest mean annual temperature, which shifts with the seasons and with land distribution
senses.definitionCN: 年平均气温最高的连线，随季节与海陆分布而移动
senses.example: The thermal equator lies north of the geographic equator in July.
senses.exampleCN: 七月时热赤道位于地理赤道以北。
senses.why: Heat, not geometry, defines this belt, yet its central line is still pictured as an equator.
senses.whyCN: 定义这条带的是热量而非几何，但它的中心线仍被想象成一条赤道。

senses.title: The cell equator
senses.titleCN: 细胞赤道：有丝分裂中期染色体排列的平面
senses.definition: the plane midway between the two poles of a dividing cell, where chromosomes line up
senses.definitionCN: 分裂细胞两极之间的中间平面，染色体在此排列
senses.example: Chromosomes align at the cell equator before separating.
senses.exampleCN: 染色体在分离前排列在细胞赤道面上。
senses.why: A dividing cell has two poles like a small sphere, so the plane halfway between them borrows the name equator.
senses.whyCN: 分裂的细胞像一个小球有两极，因此两极之间的平面借用了赤道之名。

senses.title: A great circle of any sphere
senses.titleCN: 任意球体的大圆：与自转轴垂直的等分圈
senses.definition: any great circle perpendicular to the axis of a sphere or spheroid
senses.definitionCN: 与球体或椭球体自转轴垂直的任一大圆
senses.example: Surveyors computed the equator of the model dome.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员计算了模型穹顶的赤道圈。
senses.why: The earth's equator is only one instance of a general geometric relation, which can be applied to any rounded body.
senses.whyCN: 地球赤道只是一般几何关系的一个实例，可套用到任何近球体。

senses.title: A dividing line between halves
senses.titleCN: 平分线：把事物分成相等两半的界线
senses.definition: a line imagined as dividing something into two equal parts
senses.definitionCN: 被想象为把某物分成相等两半的界线
senses.example: The negotiators drew an equator through the disputed budget.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判者把有争议的预算划出一条对半分的界线。
senses.why: The word's core image, a line that makes two sides equal, can be moved from geography to any divided whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心意象——一条使两边相等的线——可以从地理移到任何被分割的整体。

intro.en: Equator is from Medieval Latin aequator 'equalizer', from aequare 'to make equal', built on aequus 'level, equal'. The geographical name began as a phrase about the circle that equalizes day and night. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: equator 来自中世纪拉丁 aequator「使相等者」，源于 aequare「使相等」，其词根为 aequus「平的、相等的」；地理名称最初是一个关于「使昼夜相等之圈」的短语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal'. Its deeper origin is not settled; the connection sometimes suggested to a root meaning 'even' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、均匀的、相等的」；其更深来源没有定论，有时提出的与「平」有关的词根联系属重构形式。

items.en: Aequare meant 'to make level or equal', a verb formed from aequus.
items.cn: aequare 意为「使平、使相等」，是由 aequus 构成的动词。

items.en: Aequator, 'one who equalizes', was used for the circle that makes day and night equal.
items.cn: aequator 意为「使相等者」，被用来指使昼夜等长的那条圈。

items.en: The older phrase circulus aequator diei et noctis, 'the circle equalizing day and night', explains why the line received this name.
items.cn: 更早的短语 circulus aequator diei et noctis 意为「使昼夜相等之圈」，说明了这条线得名的原因。

items.en: English geography adopted equator for the zero-latitude circle in the seventeenth century, dropping the rest of the phrase.
items.cn: 英语地理学在 17 世纪采用 equator 指零度纬线圈，省去了短语的其余部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first dates): the pre-Latin origin of aequus is unresolved, and the earliest English uses of the magnetic and thermal senses are not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：aequus 在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，磁赤道与热赤道在英语中的最早用法亦无确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin 'equal' stock; group two holds the geographic lines and belts it is paired with.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「相等」词干的词；第二组是常与赤道配对的地理线与地带。

entries.definition: From aequatio 'a making equal': a statement that two quantities are equal, with no geographical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 aequatio「使相等」：表示两个量相等的式子，不含地理意义。

entries.definition: Aequus 'equal' plus latus 'side': a figure whose sides are all equal.
entries.definitionCN: aequus「相等」加 latus「边」：各边相等的图形。

entries.definition: Aequus plus valere 'be worth': equal in value or effect, not equal in shape.
entries.definitionCN: aequus 加 valere「有价值」：价值或效果相等，而非形状相等。

entries.definition: Built on aequus directly: the same in amount, degree, or value.
entries.definitionCN: 直接建在 aequus 之上：数量、程度或价值相同。

entries.definition: The region between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn, which contains the equator but is wider.
entries.definitionCN: 南北回归线之间的地带，包含赤道但范围更宽。

entries.definition: A circle parallel to the equator; the equator is the zero-degree parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 与赤道平行的圈；赤道就是零度纬线。

entries.definition: The angular distance from the equator, not the line itself.
entries.definitionCN: 相对赤道的角距离，不是那条线本身。

entries.definition: A great circle through the poles; meridians cross the equator at right angles.
entries.definitionCN: 过两极的大圆；经线与赤道正交。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin 'equalizer', real geographic lines and real cell biology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「使相等者」、真实的地理线与真实的细胞生物学，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Aequus 'equal' + -ator 'one who makes': the circle that makes day and night equal.
normal.cn: aequus「相等」+ -ator「使……者」：使昼夜相等的那条圈。

normal.en: The equator is the zero-degree parallel; latitude is counted up and down from it.
normal.cn: 赤道是零度纬线；纬度从它向南北计数。

normal.en: The celestial equator is the earth's equator projected onto the sky.
normal.cn: 天赤道是地球赤道投影到天空的结果。

normal.en: The magnetic equator is where a compass needle lies flat.
normal.cn: 磁赤道是磁针保持水平的地方。

normal.en: In cell division, chromosomes line up on the cell equator, also called the metaphase plate.
normal.cn: 细胞分裂时染色体排在细胞赤道上，也叫中期板。

abstract.cn: 想象一条带子正好系在球的正中间。

abstract.en: Picture a knife cutting an orange into two equal cups.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀把橙子切成两只相等的杯状半。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn through a budget so that both sides get the same amount.
abstract.cn: 想象在预算中间划一条线，让两边得到相同的数额。

examples.en: The equator passes through several countries in Africa and South America.
examples.cn: 赤道穿过非洲和南美洲的若干国家。

examples.en: Temperatures stay high near the equator all year.
examples.cn: 赤道附近全年气温都很高。

examples.en: The celestial equator is the zero line for declination.
examples.cn: 天赤道是赤纬的零度线。

root: 中世纪拉丁 aequator「使相等者」= aequare「使相等」（aequus「平的、相等的」）+ -ator；原指使昼夜相等之圈，后在英语中指零度纬线。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all use one image, a line that divides a round body into two equal halves: the earth's zero latitude, its hot belt, the sky's projection, the magnetic and thermal lines, the cell's mid-plane, any sphere's great circle, and a figurative dividing line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共用一个意象：把圆体分成相等两半的线——地球的零度纬线、湿热地带、天空中的投影、磁与热的对应线、细胞的中间平面、任意球体的大圆，以及比喻性的平分线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a belt drawn around the middle of a sphere, making the two halves equal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绕球体中部的带子，使两半相等。

branches.en: THE LINE: the earth's zero circle is one case of a general great circle perpendicular to an axis.
branches.cn: 这条线：地球的零度圈是与轴垂直的一般大圆的一个实例。

branches.en: THE BELT: climate turns a geometric line into a hot region, and heat draws its own central line.
branches.cn: 地带：气候把几何线变成炎热区域，热量又画出自己的中心线。

branches.en: THE SKY: the earth's equator is projected outward as the celestial equator.
branches.cn: 天空：地球赤道向外投影为天赤道。

branches.en: THE FIELD: magnetism produces a second equator that does not match the geographic one.
branches.cn: 场：磁性产生第二条与地理赤道不重合的赤道。

branches.en: DIVISION: a cell's mid-plane and a figurative halfway line both repeat the equal-halves gesture.
branches.cn: 分割：细胞的中间平面与比喻的对半线都重复了「等分」动作。

intro.en: Equator belongs to a Latin family built on aequus 'equal'; the same root yields equality, equation and adequate.
intro.cn: equator 属于以拉丁 aequus「相等」为根的词族；同一词根还衍生 equality、equation 与 adequate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus 'level, equal' yields aequare 'to make equal', aequator 'equalizer' and aequatio 'equation'; English keeps the family in equal, equity and equator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aequus「平的、相等」衍生 aequare「使相等」、aequator「使相等者」与 aequatio「等式」；英语以 equal、equity 与 equator 保留这个词族。

items.example: The verb supplies the action of equalizing.

items.example: The noun first named the circle that equalizes day and night.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指使昼夜相等的圈。

items.example: The equator divides the globe into two halves.
items.exampleCN: 赤道把地球分成两半。

items.example: Equatorial heat drives strong storms.
items.exampleCN: 赤道的热量催生强风暴。

items.example: The trade winds move equatorward.

items.example: The law aims at equality before the courts.

items.exampleCN: 昼夜平分点每年出现两次。

items.example: The supply was adequate for the winter.
items.exampleCN: 供给足够过冬。

intro.en: Degrade comes from Latin degradare, from de- plus gradus, a step.
intro.cn: degrade 源自拉丁语 degradare，由 de- 加 gradus（台阶）构成。

items.en: Gradus meant a step or a rank.
items.cn: gradus 意为台阶或等级。

items.en: Degradare meant to put down a step.
items.cn: degradare 意为降下一级。

items.en: Degrade entered English for removing from office.
items.cn: 十四世纪 degrade 以免职义进入英语。

items.en: Degrade widened to lowering dignity.
items.cn: 十六世纪 degrade 扩展到贬损尊严。

items.en: Degrade was used for worn land and soil.
items.cn: 十九世纪 degrade 用于耗损的土地与土壤。

items.en: Degrade gained the chemical breakdown sense.
items.cn: 二十世纪 degrade 带上化学分解的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the grad- step family; the near-meaning group names lowering or breaking down.
note.cn: 形近组共享 grad-（台阶）家族；近义组都是「降低或分解」的说法。

entries.definition: To raise something to a higher level.
entries.definitionCN: 升级。

entries.definition: Happening slowly in small stages.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐的。

entries.definition: The process of becoming worse or breaking down.
entries.definitionCN: 降级；降解。

entries.definition: To make someone feel less respected.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低身份。

entries.definition: To become progressively worse.
entries.definitionCN: 恶化。

entries.definition: To rot or split into simpler parts.
entries.definitionCN: 分解；腐烂。

entries.definition: To make someone feel ashamed in public.
entries.definitionCN: 羞辱。

normalIntro.en: Degrade is de- plus gradus, a step: take it down a step.
normalIntro.cn: degrade 就是 de- 加 gradus（台阶）：把它往下挪一级。

normal.en: Gradus means a step.
normal.cn: gradus 意为台阶。

normal.en: De- means down.
normal.cn: de- 表示向下。

normal.cn: degrade 把它往下移。

definition_zh: 职业的；由工作引起的；与占用有关的
definition_en: relating to a job or profession, or to the conditions and effects of work
core_image: 工厂医务室里，医生对照一张岗位暴露表给工人量血压，窗外是高炉的白烟
scene: 医生翻看工人的岗位记录，判断长期吸入粉尘是否损害了他们的肺。 The doctor reviewed the job records to see whether dust exposure had caused occupational lung disease.
sceneCN: 这里 occupational 指「由工作环境引起的」（第 2 个义项：因职业条件导致的疾病或伤害）；句意为医生查阅岗位记录，判断粉尘接触是否造成了职业性肺病。图中可辨识物件：体检表、口罩、听诊器、粉尘采样器。

pos.zh: 职业的；工作引起的；占用相关的

derivatives.zh: 职业；占领；占用（去掉形容词后缀 -al）
在职业方面（-al 加 -ly 构成副词）
作业疗法，用日常活动帮助康复
职业危害，工作本身带来的风险

senses.title: Relating to a person's job
senses.definition: connected with the job or profession a person has
senses.definitionCN: 与某人所从事的职业或工作相关
senses.example: The form asks for occupational history over the past ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 表格要求填写过去十年的职业经历。
senses.why: occupational is simply occupation plus the adjective suffix -al, so it means 'of a job' before anything else.
senses.whyCN: occupational 就是「职业」这一名词加形容词后缀 -al，因此首要意思是「属于职业的」。

senses.title: Caused by conditions at work
senses.definition: caused by the physical or mental conditions of a job
senses.definitionCN: 由工作的身体或心理条件所导致
senses.example: Noise-induced hearing loss is a common occupational injury.
senses.exampleCN: 噪声性听力损失是一种常见的职业伤害。
senses.why: once the adjective was attached to disease and injury, it came to mean 'caused by work' rather than merely 'about work'.
senses.whyCN: 当这个形容词与疾病、伤害搭配后，意思就从「关于工作」变成「由工作引起」。

senses.title: Relating to the use of premises
senses.definition: connected with the legal or practical holding of a building or land
senses.definitionCN: 与对建筑或土地的法律或实际占用相关
senses.example: The lease sets out the occupational rights of the tenant.
senses.exampleCN: 租约列明了租客的占用权利。
senses.why: the adjective follows the older branch of occupation, where the word means holding premises rather than holding a job.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也跟随这一名词的旧分支，那里的意思是持有房屋而非持有工作。

senses.title: Of therapy based on daily activities
senses.definition: relating to therapy that uses everyday activities to restore function
senses.definitionCN: 与借助日常活动恢复功能的疗法相关
senses.example: After the stroke he began occupational therapy twice a week.
senses.exampleCN: 中风后他每周接受两次作业疗法。
senses.why: the therapy is named for the occupations, meaning activities, that patients practise, not for their paid jobs.
senses.whyCN: 这种疗法因患者练习的「日常活动」而得名，并非因他们的有薪工作。

senses.title: Of a surname taken from a trade
senses.titleCN: 以职业为来源的姓氏的
senses.definition: describing a family name derived from an ancestor's trade
senses.definitionCN: 描述由祖先行业演变来的姓氏
senses.example: Smith is the most familiar occupational surname in English.
senses.exampleCN: 史密斯是英语中最常见的职业姓氏。
senses.why: historians of names call surnames occupational when they record what an ancestor did for a living.
senses.whyCN: 姓名学研究把记录祖先谋生行当的姓氏称作职业姓氏。

senses.title: Of job categories in statistics
senses.definition: relating to the grouping of workers by the type of work they do
senses.definitionCN: 与按工作类型对劳动者进行分组相关
senses.example: The survey uses a standard occupational classification.
senses.exampleCN: 该调查采用标准的职业分类。
senses.why: labour statistics needed a neutral adjective for categories of work, and this one filled the gap.
senses.whyCN: 劳动统计需要为工作类别找一个中性的形容词，这个词填补了这一空缺。

senses.title: Of a pension tied to an employer
senses.titleCN: 与雇主挂钩的养老金的
senses.definition: describing a pension provided through a particular job or employer
senses.definitionCN: 描述通过特定工作或雇主提供的养老金
senses.example: She transferred her occupational pension when she changed jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 她换工作时转移了自己的职业养老金。
senses.why: pension law distinguishes schemes tied to an employment from personal ones, and the adjective marks the former.
senses.whyCN: 养老金法规区分与雇佣挂钩的计划与个人计划，这个形容词标出前者。

senses.title: Relating to military occupation
senses.definition: relating to the administration or forces of a territory held by an army
senses.definitionCN: 与军队控制下的地区的管理或部队相关
senses.example: The tribunal examined the occupational authorities' orders.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭审查了占领当局的命令。
senses.why: the adjective also serves the military branch, where occupation means control imposed by force.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词同样服务于军事分支，那里的「占用、职业」指以武力强加的控制。

intro.en: Occupational is an English formation: occupation, from Latin occupatio, plus the adjective suffix -al. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: occupational 是英语构词：occupation 来自拉丁 occupatio，再加形容词后缀 -al。年代均为约数。

items.en: The root capere 'to take, seize' underlies the whole family; its pre-Latin shape is reconstructed, not directly attested.
items.cn: 词根 capere「拿、夺取」支撑整个词族；其拉丁语前形态属于重构形式，并非直接有据。

items.en: Occupatio, from occupare 'seize, hold', named the act of taking possession and later the work that takes up one's time.
items.cn: occupatio 来自 occupare「夺取、持有」，指占有行为，后来也指占去时间的工作。

items.en: English borrowed occupation through Old French in the fourteenth century, and the job sense grew from the idea of time taken up.
items.cn: 英语经古法语在十四世纪借入 occupation，职业义由「时间被占去」这一想法发展而来。

items.en: The Latin adjective suffix -alis, through French -al, was added to make an adjective of 'belonging to occupation'.
items.cn: 拉丁形容词后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 加入，构成表示「属于职业」的形容词。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the adjective was attached to disease, health, therapy and classification, fixing its modern range.
items.cn: 十九至二十世纪，这个形容词与疾病、卫生、疗法和分类搭配，固定了它的现代用法范围。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of the adjective is not recorded, and the pre-Latin base of capere remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：该形容词最早的英语用例没有确切记录，capere 的拉丁语前词基仍属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Latin verb and one deceptive look-alike with a different root; group two holds adjectives about work with different scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁动词的词形，外加一个词根不同却形近的词；第二组是范围不同的「工作」形容词。

entries.definition: The noun meaning a job, a seizure of territory or the use of premises; the adjective adds -al to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指职业、占领领土或占用房屋的名词；形容词是在其后加 -al。

entries.definition: The past participle and adjective meaning in use, taken by an army, or busy; it describes a state, not a category.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词兼形容词，意为被占用、被军队占据或忙碌；描述状态而非类别。

entries.definition: The person who occupies a building; it names a person rather than a relation to work.
entries.definitionCN: 指占用某栋建筑的人；指人，而非与工作的关系。

entries.definition: From Latin vocare 'to call', via vocation 'a calling': it means training for a trade, and shares only the ending with occupational.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vocare「召唤」，经 vocation「天职」而来，指职业培训；与 occupational 只共享词尾。

entries.definition: Describing education or training that prepares someone for a specific trade, rather than anything about their current job.
entries.definitionCN: 描述为特定行业做准备的教育或培训，而非关于其现有工作的一切。

entries.definition: Relating to a profession with formal qualifications, and often implying high standards or paid status.
entries.definitionCN: 与具有正式资格的专门职业相关，常暗示高标准或有薪身份。

entries.definition: A plain everyday compound meaning connected with work, without the formal or legal tone of occupational.
entries.definitionCN: 日常朴素的复合词，意为与工作有关，没有 occupational 的正式或法律色彩。

entries.definition: The common spoken equivalent of occupational in phrases such as job-related stress.
entries.definitionCN: 在 job-related stress 一类短语中，是 occupational 的日常口语对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定短语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: occupation + -al: the suffix turns the noun into 'relating to'.
normal.cn: occupation 加 -al：后缀把名词变成「与……相关的」。

normal.en: Fixed medical phrases carry the sense: occupational disease, occupational health, occupational therapy.
normal.cn: 固定医学短语承载词义：职业病、职业卫生、作业疗法。

normal.en: The same family gives occupation, occupy, occupant, occupancy, occupier.
normal.cn: 同一词族给出 occupation、occupy、occupant、occupancy、occupier。

normal.en: Therapy is occupational because patients practise daily activities, not because they are at work.
normal.cn: 作业疗法之所以叫 occupational，是因为患者练习日常活动，而非因为在上班。

normal.en: Statistics says occupational classification when it groups workers by the type of job.
normal.cn: 统计说 occupational classification 时，是按工作类型给劳动者分类。

abstract.en: Picture a badge that follows a worker from the factory gate to the clinic door.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚徽章跟着工人从厂门一直走到诊所门口。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow cast by a job onto a person's health, long after the shift ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一份工作投在健康上的影子，在下班很久后仍未散去。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a drawer that sorts a whole life by the work written on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉贴着标签，按上面写的工作把一整段人生归类。

examples.en: The clinic specialises in occupational injuries of the hand.
examples.cn: 这家诊所专门治疗手部职业损伤。

examples.en: Occupational mobility is lower in regions with a single large employer.
examples.cn: 在只有一家大型雇主的地区，职业流动性较低。

examples.en: The report compared occupational earnings across five sectors.
examples.cn: 报告比较了五个行业的职业收入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「occupation（职业）+ al（的）」——与职业有关的 → 职业的

root: 拉丁 capere「抓取」→ occupare「夺取、占有」→ occupatio「职业；占据」→ 英语 occupation 加形容词后缀 -al。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all say 'belonging to occupation': to a job, to illness caused by work, to the holding of premises, to therapy by daily activity, to trade surnames, to statistical classes, to employer pensions, and to military rule.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都表示「属于职业」：属于工作、属于工作引发的疾病、属于房屋的持有、属于日常活动疗法、属于行业姓氏、属于统计类别、属于雇主养老金、属于军事管制。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a job casting a long shadow over health, home and paperwork.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份工作把长长的影子投在健康、住所与文书之上。

branches.en: JOB AND CATEGORY: the adjective describes both one person's work and the statistical box it falls into.
branches.cn: 工作与类别：这个形容词既描述某人的工作，也描述它落入的统计格子。

branches.en: WORK AS CAUSE: disease and injury turn 'about work' into 'caused by work'.
branches.cn: 工作作为原因：疾病与伤害把「关于工作」变成「由工作引起」。

branches.en: HOLDING A PLACE: premises held by a tenant and territory held by an army both keep the old sense of occupation.
branches.cn: 占住一处：租客持有的房屋与军队控制的领土，都保留这一名词的旧义。

branches.en: ACTIVITY AS THERAPY: here occupation means the everyday activities a patient practises.
branches.cn: 活动即疗法：这里的「占用、职业」指患者练习的日常活动。

branches.en: INHERITED AND EARNED: a surname records an ancestor's trade, a pension records an employer's scheme.
branches.cn: 承袭与累积：姓氏记录祖先的行业，养老金记录雇主的计划。

intro.en: Occupational is a layered English word: Latin root and prefix, a Latin noun ending, then an English adjective ending.
intro.cn: occupational 是层叠构成的英语词：拉丁词根与前缀、拉丁名词词尾，最后是英语形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere 'seize' gives occupare and occupatio; the adjective ending -alis, through French -al, is added in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 capere「抓取」派生 occupare 与 occupatio；形容词词尾 -alis 经法语 -al 在英语中加入。
