definition_zh: 遗传的；世袭的；继承的
definition_en: passed from parents to offspring through genes, or transmitted by legal succession from one generation to the next
core_image: 家族相册里，几代人的手形几乎一模一样，连指节的弯度都对得上
scene: 家族相册里，几代人的手形几乎一模一样。 A hereditary trait ran through every generation of the family.
sceneCN: 这里 hereditary 指「由上一代经遗传传下来的」（第 1 个义项：经基因传递的）；句意为一种遗传性状贯穿了这个家族的每一代。可辨识物件：相册、放大的手部照片、家谱线、铅笔标记。

pos.zh: 遗传的；经基因传递的
世袭的；依法继承的

derivatives.zh: 可继承的财产（法律用语）

senses.title: Passed through genes
senses.definition: transmitted from parents to offspring through genetic material
senses.definitionCN: 通过遗传物质由亲代传给子代
senses.example: Hereditary deafness runs in that family.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传性耳聋在那个家族中代代出现。
senses.why: The adjective describes a trait whose cause travels in the genes, so it names the route rather than the illness itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词描述病因随基因传递的性状，因此命名的是传递路径，而非疾病本身。

senses.title: Inherited from ancestors
senses.definition: received from an ancestor rather than acquired in one's own lifetime
senses.definitionCN: 从祖先处承接，而非在本人一生中获得
senses.example: The tendency is partly hereditary.
senses.exampleCN: 这种倾向有一部分是遗传的。
senses.why: The word can soften a claim: partly hereditary means ancestry contributes without settling the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以缓和断言：部分遗传意味着祖先有贡献，但并不决定结果。

senses.title: Transmitted by succession
senses.definition: passed down by legal or customary succession rather than election
senses.definitionCN: 按法律或习俗世袭传递，而非经选举
senses.example: The duke held a hereditary seat in the old assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 公爵在旧议会中拥有一个世袭席位。
senses.why: Law uses the same adjective for offices because a seat can pass to an heir just as an estate can.
senses.whyCN: 法律用同一个形容词描述职位，因为席位也能像产业一样传给继承人。

senses.title: Of hereditary monarchy
senses.definition: describing a system in which the head of state succeeds by birth
senses.definitionCN: 描述国家元首按出生顺序继位的制度
senses.example: The country replaced hereditary rule with elections.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家用选举取代了世袭统治。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to institutions, not only to bodies, when rule itself is handed down.
senses.whyCN: 当统治权本身被传下时，这个形容词也附着于制度，而不只是身体。

senses.title: Of hereditary material
senses.definition: relating to the material that carries genes from one cell to the next
senses.definitionCN: 与把基因从一代细胞带到下一代细胞的物质相关
senses.example: Hereditary material is copied into every cell.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传物质被复制进每一个细胞。
senses.why: In biology the adjective can modify the carrier as well as the trait, which is why hereditary material is a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学中，这个形容词既能修饰性状，也能修饰载体，因此「遗传物质」成为固定搭配。

senses.title: Of a hereditary predisposition
senses.definition: describing an inherited tendency that raises risk without causing the condition alone
senses.definitionCN: 描述提高风险但并不单独致病的遗传倾向
senses.example: A hereditary predisposition does not guarantee illness.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传易感性并不保证一定患病。
senses.why: The word separates inheritance from inevitability: a predisposition is a loaded starting point, not a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「遗传」与「必然」分开：易感性是一个有负载的起点，而不是判决。

senses.title: Legally inheritable
senses.definition: able to pass to an heir under the law
senses.definitionCN: 依法可以传给继承人
senses.example: The estate was hereditary and could not be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业属于可继承财产，不能出售。
senses.why: Property law uses the adjective for land and rights that must descend rather than be traded freely.
senses.whyCN: 财产法用这个形容词描述必须下传、不能自由买卖的土地与权利。

senses.title: Carried down from the past
senses.definition: describing an attitude or conflict handed down so long that it seems inborn
senses.definitionCN: 描述传得太久、仿佛天生的态度或冲突
senses.example: The two villages were hereditary enemies.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个村子是世代相传的仇敌。
senses.why: The metaphor treats hostility as an estate: children receive a quarrel they never chose.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻把敌意当作产业：孩子们接收了一场他们从未选择的争吵。

intro.en: Hereditary comes from Latin hereditarius 'of an inheritance', from hereditas 'inheritance', from heres (hered-) 'heir'.
intro.cn: hereditary 来自拉丁 hereditarius「继承的」，再上溯 hereditas「继承」与 heres（hered-）「继承人」。

items.en: Heres (genitive heredis) meant 'heir'. Its deeper origin is not established; links to other Indo-European words are hypotheses, and any PIE form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: heres（属格 heredis）意为「继承人」。其更深来源未得到确证；与其他印欧语词的联系只是假说，任何原始印欧语形式均属重构。

items.en: Hereditarius 'of an inheritance' was formed from hereditas; the adjective suffix -arius marks belonging or relation.
items.cn: hereditarius「继承的」由 hereditas 构成；形容词后缀 -arius 表示归属或关系。

items.en: English took hereditary from Latin or French in the fifteenth or sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在 15 或 16 世纪从拉丁语或法语借入 hereditary；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The legal sense survives in hereditary titles and hereditary peers, where office passes by birth rather than election.
items.cn: 法律义残存于世袭头衔与世袭贵族，其职位按出生而非选举传递。

items.en: The biological sense developed in the nineteenth century, when heredity became a research subject and traits were traced through families.
items.cn: 生物学义在 19 世纪发展起来，当时遗传成为研究课题，性状被沿家族追踪。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): heres has no established pre-Latin etymology, and the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：heres 没有已确立的拉丁语之前词源，英语首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same hered- family that differ in grammar or nuance; group two holds adjectives that also describe what is present from birth or runs in families.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hered- 词族、但语法角色或侧重不同的词；第二组是同样描述「出生即有」或「家族中常见」的形容词。

entries.definition: The process or system of transmission; hereditary is the adjective describing what is transmitted.
entries.definitionCN: 指传递过程或系统；hereditary 是描述被传递之物的形容词。

entries.definition: Able to be inherited, often used of traits or property; hereditary describes the actual transmission or legal status.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够被继承，常用于性状或财产；hereditary 描述实际的传递或法律地位。

entries.definition: A legal term for inheritable property; it is a noun of things, not a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 指可继承财产的法律术语；它是事物名词，不是性状。

entries.definition: The adverb form; it describes how something is transmitted rather than what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式；描述传递方式，而非事物本身。

entries.definition: The ordinary participle from inherit; hereditary is the fixed adjective, especially in biology and law.
entries.definitionCN: inherit 的普通分词；hereditary 是固定形容词，尤用于生物学与法律。

entries.tag: present at birth not always geneti
entries.definition: Present at birth; a congenital condition may arise during development and need not be hereditary.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生时即存在；先天状况可能在发育中形成，未必是遗传的。

entries.definition: Occurring in a family more often than chance; familial does not prove a genetic cause.
entries.definitionCN: 指在家族中发生率高于偶然；familial 并不证明存在遗传原因。

entries.definition: The broad modern adjective; hereditary emphasises transmission from ancestors, genetic emphasises the genes themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 宽泛的现代形容词；hereditary 强调从祖先传递，genetic 强调基因本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: heres 'heir' + -ary: belonging to an inheritance.
normal.cn: heres「继承人」+ -ary：属于继承的。

normal.en: The family runs hereditary, heredity, hereditarily and hereditament.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 hereditary、heredity、hereditarily 与 hereditament。

normal.en: Law fixes hereditary peer and hereditary title; biology fixes hereditary disease.
normal.cn: 法律固定搭配世袭贵族、世袭头衔；生物学固定搭配遗传性疾病。

normal.en: Hereditary peer describes a seat, not a gene.
normal.cn: 世袭贵族描述的是席位，不是基因。

normal.en: A hereditary predisposition raises risk without deciding the outcome.
normal.cn: 遗传易感性提高风险，却不决定结果。

abstract.en: Picture a seal stamped on every generation of a document.
abstract.cn: 想象每一代文件上都盖着同一枚印章。

abstract.en: Picture a tune learned before birth and never questioned.
abstract.cn: 想象一支在出生前就学会、从不被质疑的曲子。

abstract.en: Picture a title that comes with the furniture, not with a vote.
abstract.cn: 想象一个头衔随家具而来，而不是随选票而来。

examples.en: The condition is hereditary, though not everyone who carries the gene falls ill.
examples.cn: 这种病是遗传的，但并非每个携带该基因的人都会发病。

examples.en: Hereditary peers lost their voting rights in the reform.
examples.cn: 世袭贵族在改革中失去了投票权。

examples.en: The museum refused to sell the hereditary collection.
examples.cn: 博物馆拒绝出售这批世袭收藏。

dict_mnemonic.text: hered（继承人）+ itary（形容词尾）——与继承人相关的 → 世袭的、遗传的。

root: 拉丁 hereditarius「继承的」← hereditas「继承」← heres（hered-）「继承人」；heres 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a stamp that keeps reappearing: in genes, in ancestry, in offices, in monarchy, in cellular material, in risk, in property law and finally in inherited hostility.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一枚反复出现的印章展开：出现在基因、祖先、职位、君主制、细胞物质、风险、财产法，最后出现在沿袭的敌意中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same hand shape appearing in photograph after photograph.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一手形在一张又一张照片中反复出现。

branches.en: GENETIC AND ANCESTRAL: a trait travels through genes and is received from ancestors.
branches.cn: 遗传与祖先：性状经基因传递，并从祖先处承接。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND RISK: the carrier itself, and an inherited tendency that only raises risk.
branches.cn: 物质与风险：载体本身，以及只提高风险的遗传倾向。

branches.en: OFFICE AND RULE: seats and crowns pass by birth rather than election.
branches.cn: 职位与统治：席位与王冠按出生而非选举传递。

branches.en: PROPERTY LAW: land and rights that must descend to heirs.
branches.cn: 财产法：必须下传给继承人的土地与权利。

branches.en: INHERITED HOSTILITY: an old quarrel arrives like an estate.
branches.cn: 沿袭的敌意：旧日争吵像产业一样被接收。

intro.en: Hereditary is an adjective built on the Latin hered- stem plus a suffix, and the same stem builds a legal and biological family.
intro.cn: hereditary 是由拉丁 hered- 词干加后缀构成的形容词，同一词干还构成法律与生物词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin heres (hered-) gives hereditas, hereditarius, hereditary, heredity and inherit; -arius marks belonging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 heres（hered-）衍生 hereditas、hereditarius、hereditary、heredity 与 inherit；-arius 标记归属关系。

items.example: The stem names the person who receives.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名接收者。

items.example: Hereditas named the estate and the relation together.
items.exampleCN: hereditas 同时命名产业与关系。

items.example: The adjective added -arius to the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在词干后加 -arius。

items.example: The suffix turns the stem into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成描述词。

items.example: The title was hereditary.
items.exampleCN: 这个爵位是世袭的。

items.example: Heredity and environment interact.
items.exampleCN: 遗传与环境相互作用。

items.example: The trait is hereditarily transmitted.
items.exampleCN: 这一性状以遗传方式传递。

items.example: She inherited the house.
items.exampleCN: 她继承了这所房子。

items.example: The inheritance was divided.
items.exampleCN: 遗产被分配。

items.example: The right is inheritable.
items.exampleCN: 这项权利可继承。

items.example: The deed lists every hereditament.
items.exampleCN: 契据列明了每一项可继承财产。

items.example: The debate drew both hereditarians and environmentalists.
items.exampleCN: 这场争论吸引了遗传论者与环境论者。

definition_zh: 蒸发；蒸发量；蒸干浓缩
definition_en: the process by which a liquid changes into vapor at its surface, or the loss of moisture caused by this process
core_image: 一只浅盘里的水在阳光下越来越薄，盘底慢慢露出一圈白色的盐痕
scene: 雨后的水洼在午后阳光下缩小，傍晚只剩一圈浅浅的湿痕。 A shallow puddle shrinks under the afternoon sun, and by evening only a damp ring remains: that steady loss of water is evaporation.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「液体在表面缓慢变成水汽而减少」（第 1 个义项：液面汽化）；句意为水洼在阳光下缩小，到傍晚只剩湿痕，这种持续失水就是蒸发。

pos.zh: 蒸发（作用）；汽化
蒸发量；水分损失量
蒸干；通过蒸发使溶液浓缩
（比喻）逐渐消失；消散

forms.label: 复数（多种蒸发过程或多次测定）

senses.title: Liquid turning into vapor
senses.definition: the process in which molecules at the surface of a liquid escape into the air as vapor
senses.definitionCN: 液体表面分子逸入空气、变成水汽的过程
senses.example: Evaporation from the open tank continues even when the water is cool.
senses.exampleCN: 即使水是凉的，敞口罐里的水仍在持续蒸发。
senses.why: Only surface molecules can leave; the liquid does not need to boil. This is the physical core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 只有表面分子能逃出去，液体不必沸腾。这是这个词的物理核心。

senses.title: Loss of moisture from a surface
senses.definition: the drying of soil, skin, laundry or pavement as moisture leaves it
senses.definitionCN: 土壤、皮肤、衣物或路面因水分离开而变干
senses.example: Covering the seedbed slows evaporation and keeps the soil moist.
senses.exampleCN: 覆盖苗床能减缓蒸发，让土壤保持湿润。
senses.why: The same physical process seen from the side of the material: what matters is how much water it loses.
senses.whyCN: 同一个物理过程从材料一侧看：重点是它失去了多少水。

senses.title: Concentration by boiling off water
senses.definition: the removal of water by heating so that a solution becomes more concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 加热除去水分，使溶液变得更浓
senses.example: Salt is obtained from seawater by evaporation in shallow pans.
senses.exampleCN: 盐是通过在浅盘中蒸发海水得到的。
senses.why: Here evaporation is used as a tool: the water is unwanted, and what stays behind is the product.
senses.whyCN: 这里蒸发是工具：水是不要的部分，留下来的才是产物。

senses.title: Water-cycle flux
senses.definition: the movement of water from land and water bodies into the atmosphere, treated as a measurable part of the water cycle
senses.definitionCN: 水从陆地和有水表面进入大气，作为水循环中可测量的一环
senses.example: Satellites estimate evaporation over the ocean by tracking water vapor.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星通过追踪水汽来估算海面上的蒸发量。
senses.why: In earth science the process is treated as a flux: water leaves a surface at a measurable rate.
senses.whyCN: 在地球科学里，这一过程被当作通量：水以可测的速度离开某个表面。

senses.title: Amount evaporated
senses.definition: the quantity of water lost by evaporation, usually measured over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内因蒸发失去的水量
senses.example: The pan recorded an evaporation of four millimeters overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸发皿记录到一夜之间蒸发了四毫米。
senses.why: The process name is transferred to its measured result, a common pattern in scientific vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 过程名称被转用到测量结果上，这是科学词汇常见的转义方式。

senses.title: Vaporization below boiling
senses.definition: vaporization that occurs below the boiling point, especially in physics and engineering
senses.definitionCN: 在沸点以下发生的汽化，尤用于物理与工程
senses.example: Evaporation differs from boiling because it needs no bubbles.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸发与沸腾不同，因为它不需要气泡。
senses.why: Physics separates evaporation from boiling by mechanism, not by speed.
senses.whyCN: 物理学按机制而非速度把蒸发与沸腾区分开。

senses.title: Figurative disappearance
senses.definition: the gradual disappearance of money, support, confidence or another abstract quantity
senses.definitionCN: 钱、支持、信心等抽象之物的逐渐消失
senses.example: The evaporation of public trust followed the repeated delays.
senses.exampleCN: 反复拖延之后，公众信任逐渐消失。
senses.why: The metaphor treats an abstract quantity as a liquid that silently thins out.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把抽象之物当成一种无声变薄的液体。

senses.title: Evaporative cooling
senses.definition: cooling produced when a liquid evaporates and takes heat away with it
senses.definitionCN: 液体蒸发带走热量而产生的降温
senses.example: Sweating relies on evaporation to lower body temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 出汗依靠蒸发来降低体温。
senses.why: The word names the process that removes heat, so it also names the cooling effect used by organisms and machines.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是带走热量的过程，因此也指生物与机器利用的降温效果。

intro.en: The Latin elements are clear, but the deeper origin of vapor is disputed, and the dates of the technical senses are approximate.
intro.cn: 拉丁成分清楚，但 vapor 更深来源存在争议；技术义的出现年代为大致估计。

items.en: The base is vapor 'steam, vapor' with the verb vaporare 'to steam, to be hot'. The prefix e- (before a consonant, from ex-) means 'out of'.
items.cn: 基础词是 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」与动词 vaporare「冒汽、发热」。前缀 e-（辅音前由 ex- 变来）意为「向外」。

items.en: Late Latin evaporatio, evaporationis (f., third declension) meant 'a steaming away'. The noun is built from evaporare plus the action suffix -atio.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 evaporatio（属格 evaporationis，阴性第三变格）意为「蒸散」。该名词由 evaporare 加动作后缀 -atio 构成。

items.en: English adopted evaporation in the seventeenth century through scientific French and Latin. Early examples describe the drying of liquids.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪经科学法语与拉丁语吸收 evaporation，早期例子描述液体的变干。

items.en: With the growth of chemistry and meteorology, the noun acquired measured and technical uses such as evaporation rate and evaporation residue.
items.cn: 随着化学与气象学的发展，该名词获得「蒸发速率」「蒸发残渣」等测量与技术用法。

items.en: The figurative sense for money, trust or hope is a nineteenth- and twentieth-century extension. The underlying image is a liquid thinning until nothing is left.
items.cn: 用于金钱、信任或希望的比喻义是十九至二十世纪的延伸。底层意象是一种液体不断变薄，直到什么都不剩。

note.en: The first group is close in sound but not in root; the second group shares the physical process or its opposite.
note.cn: 第一组读音相近但不同源；第二组共享同一物理过程或其反面。

entries.definition: the act of moving people out of a dangerous place. It comes from Latin vacuus 'empty', not from vapor.
entries.definitionCN: 撤离；疏散。来自拉丁语 vacuus「空的」，与 vapor 无关。

entries.definition: the act of judging the value or quality of something, from Latin valere 'to be worth'.
entries.definitionCN: 评估；评价。来自拉丁语 valere「有价值」，与蒸发无关。

entries.definition: the combined loss of water by evaporation from the soil and transpiration from plants; it contains evaporation but adds the plant pathway.
entries.definitionCN: 蒸散。土壤蒸发与植物蒸腾之和；词里含 evaporation，但增加了植物这条路径。

entries.definition: the general change from liquid to vapor, including boiling; evaporation is the surface-only case.
entries.definitionCN: 汽化。液变气的一般过程，包括沸腾；蒸发只是仅发生在表面的那一种。

entries.definition: the change from vapor back to liquid; it is the reverse arrow of the water cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 凝结。水汽变回液体，是水循环里方向相反的一支。

entries.definition: the loss of water vapor through plant surfaces; it is evaporation routed through a living organism.
entries.definitionCN: 蒸腾。水汽经植物表面散失；可以理解为经过活体生物的蒸发。

entries.definition: the everyday word for becoming dry; it names the result rather than the physical mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 变干；干燥。日常词，说的是结果，而不是物理机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'out' and the base means 'steam': steam going out of a liquid.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「向外」，基础词意为「蒸汽」：蒸汽从液体里出去。

normal.en: The family runs evaporate, evaporative, evaporator and evapotranspiration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evaporate、evaporative、evaporator 与 evapotranspiration。

normal.en: Science fixes the collocations: evaporation rate, evaporation residue, evaporation pan.
normal.cn: 科学语境固定搭配：蒸发速率、蒸发残渣、蒸发皿。

normal.en: Evaporation is the surface process; boiling is the bulk process with bubbles.
normal.cn: 蒸发是表面过程；沸腾是整体过程并产生气泡。

normal.en: The water cycle pairs evaporation with condensation and precipitation.
normal.cn: 水循环把蒸发与凝结、降水配成一组。

abstract.en: Picture a shallow plate of water slowly turning into a white ring of salt.
abstract.cn: 想象一盘浅水慢慢变成一圈白色的盐痕。

abstract.en: Picture a bank balance shrinking without any withdrawal being recorded.
abstract.cn: 想象一笔存款没有任何取款记录却不断变少。

abstract.en: Picture a puddle that leaves only a dark outline on the pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象一洼水最后只在路面上留下一个深色轮廓。

examples.en: Evaporation from the lake leaves a crust of salt along the shore.
examples.cn: 湖水的蒸发在岸边留下一层盐壳。

examples.en: Mulch reduces evaporation and helps seedlings survive a dry spell.
examples.cn: 覆盖物减少蒸发，帮助幼苗熬过干旱期。

examples.en: The evaporation of the reserve fund was never explained to members.
examples.cn: 储备金的逐渐消失从未向成员解释过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一娃泼水」——泼出去的水在太阳下慢慢变少 → 蒸发

root: 拉丁语 e-「向外」+ vaporare「冒汽」，源自 vapor「蒸汽、水汽」；经晚期拉丁语 evaporatio 与科学法语进入英语。vapor 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one physical event and fan out into measurement, technique and metaphor. The event is surface escape; measurement turns it into a number, technique turns it into a tool, and metaphor turns it into silent loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个物理事件出发，再分向测量、技术与比喻。事件本身是表面逸出；测量把它变成数字，技术把它变成工具，比喻把它变成无声的流失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin layer of liquid losing itself into the air, leaving a mark behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层薄液不断进入空气，最后留下痕迹。

branches.en: ESCAPE AND DRYING: the same event seen from the air side and from the material side.
branches.cn: 逸出与变干：同一事件从空气一侧和材料一侧分别看。

branches.en: CONCENTRATION: removing water is a tool, and physics names its mechanism.
branches.cn: 浓缩：除去水分是一种工具，物理学为其机制命名。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the water cycle turns the event into a flux and then into a number.
branches.cn: 测量：水循环把事件变成通量，再变成数字。

branches.en: COOLING: the escaping molecules carry heat, so evaporation becomes a service.
branches.cn: 降温：逃出的分子带走热量，蒸发于是成为一种功能。

branches.en: METAPHOR: an abstract quantity is treated as a liquid that thins away.
branches.cn: 比喻：抽象之物被当作一种会变薄的液体。

intro.en: Evaporation is built from Latin pieces that also build a compact English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: evaporation 由拉丁成分构成，这些成分还构成一组紧凑的英语词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor gives vapor, vaporous and evaporate; the prefix e- marks movement out, and -atio marks an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 衍生 vapor、vaporous 与 evaporate；前缀 e- 标记「向外」，后缀 -atio 标记动作或其结果。

latinEntries.meaning: to steam away, to pass off as vapor

items.example: The prefix marks water leaving the liquid.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记水离开液体。

items.example: The base names the thing that the liquid becomes.
items.exampleCN: 基础词命名液体变成的东西。

items.meaning: the action or result of steaming away
items.example: Evaporation cools the remaining liquid.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发使剩余的液体降温。

items.example: The puddle will evaporate by noon.
items.exampleCN: 水洼到中午就会蒸发。

items.example: Evaporative cooling works in dry air.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发降温在干燥空气中有效。

items.meaning: a device that evaporates a liquid
items.example: The evaporator removes water from the juice.
items.exampleCN: 蒸发器除去果汁中的水。

items.meaning: combined water loss from soil and plants
items.example: Evapotranspiration is measured over whole catchments.
items.exampleCN: 蒸散在整个流域尺度上测量。

items.example: A vaporous haze hung over the warm marsh.
items.exampleCN: 温暖沼泽上方悬着一层雾状水汽。

items.example: The laser can vaporize a thin metal film.
items.exampleCN: 激光能使薄金属膜汽化。

definition_zh: 妊娠期的；按孕期长短来衡量的
definition_en: relating to the period in which a young mammal develops inside its mother before birth
core_image: 一张按周编号的产检表格，每一格代表胎儿在母体内长成的一段路
scene: 产检室里，医生摊开一张按周编号的表格，逐格核对胎儿的发育进度。 The clinic keeps a chart of gestational age so that every scan can be compared with the expected range.
sceneCN: 这里 gestational 指「按怀孕时长来衡量的」（第 1 个义项：以孕周为尺度来描述孕期）；句意为诊所保留一张孕龄记录表，以便每次检查都能与预期范围对照。

pos.zh: 妊娠（期）的；孕期的；按孕周计算的

senses.title: Measured by length of pregnancy
senses.definition: relating to the length of time an unborn mammal has been developing
senses.definitionCN: 与未出生幼体已经发育的时长有关
senses.example: The clinic records gestational age in weeks at every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所每次就诊都以周为单位记录孕龄。
senses.why: gestational is the adjective of gestation, which in Latin means 'a carrying'; the suffix -al turns that carrying period into a defining attribute.
senses.whyCN: gestational 是 gestation 的形容词，后者在拉丁语中意为「背负、运送」；后缀 -al 把这段「怀着的时期」变成事物的限定属性。

senses.title: Belonging to the unborn stage
senses.definition: belonging to the stage of development of the unborn young rather than to the mother
senses.definitionCN: 属于未出生幼体自身的发育阶段，而非母亲的状态
senses.example: Gestational development in the first trimester is mostly organ formation.
senses.exampleCN: 孕早期的胎儿发育主要是器官形成。
senses.why: the word shifts attention from the carrier to what is being carried, because gestation names both the carrying and the thing carried.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把注意力从承载者移向被承载者，因为 gestation 同时指「怀着」这件事与被怀着的对象。

senses.title: Of disorders that start with pregnancy
senses.titleCN: 孕期才出现的病症（如妊娠糖尿病）
senses.definition: used of medical conditions that arise because of pregnancy rather than before it
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述因怀孕而出现、怀孕前并不存在的疾病
senses.example: Gestational diabetes usually disappears after delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 妊娠糖尿病通常在分娩后消失。
senses.why: such conditions exist only during the carrying period, so the adjective marks pregnancy as their cause and their time limit.
senses.whyCN: 这类疾病只存在于怀孕期内，形容词因此既标明孕期的起因，也标明它的时限。

senses.title: Counted from the last menstrual period
senses.titleCN: 以末次月经为起点计算的
senses.definition: counted from the last menstrual period rather than from conception
senses.definitionCN: 从末次月经起算，而不是从受孕起算
senses.example: By gestational dating, the pregnancy is two weeks older than the embryo.
senses.exampleCN: 按孕龄推算，孕期比胚胎本身的实际周数多两周。
senses.why: clinical counting starts before conception because the exact moment of fertilisation is unknown, so the adjective follows the calendar doctors actually use.
senses.whyCN: 临床计算从受孕之前开始，因为受精的确切时刻无法确定，形容词于是跟随医生实际使用的日历。

senses.title: Of a person carrying another's pregnancy
senses.definition: describing a person who carries a pregnancy for someone else
senses.definitionCN: 描述替他人怀胎的人
senses.example: The gestational carrier has no genetic link to the child.
senses.exampleCN: 代孕母体与孩子没有基因联系。
senses.why: the emphasis falls on the carrying work alone, which is exactly what distinguishes a carrier from a genetic parent.
senses.whyCN: 重点只落在「怀胎」这件工作上，而这正是代孕母体与基因父母的分界。

senses.title: Of structures visible in early scans
senses.titleCN: 早期超声可见结构的（如孕囊）
senses.definition: used of the early structures that mark where the pregnancy is implanted
senses.definitionCN: 用于描述标示胚胎着床位置的早期结构
senses.example: The sonographer located a gestational sac inside the uterus.
senses.exampleCN: 超声医师在子宫内找到了孕囊。
senses.why: these structures belong to the pregnancy as a whole, not to the embryo alone, so the adjective attaches them to the gestational period.
senses.whyCN: 这些结构属于整个妊娠而非单独的胚胎，形容词因此把它们系在孕期的整体上。

senses.title: Of pregnancy length in other mammals
senses.definition: used of the carrying period in mammals other than humans
senses.definitionCN: 用于人类以外哺乳动物的怀胎时长
senses.example: Gestational length in elephants approaches two years.
senses.exampleCN: 大象的孕期接近两年。
senses.why: the Latin root describes any animal carrying young, so the adjective extends naturally to zoology.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根本来就指任何动物怀胎，形容词因此自然延伸到动物学。

senses.title: Of a slow period before something emerges
senses.titleCN: 比喻：事物成形前的酝酿期
senses.definition: figurative, of the slow period during which an idea or project takes shape before it appears
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指想法或项目成形、露面之前的缓慢酝酿期
senses.example: The policy had a long gestational phase before anyone saw a draft.
senses.exampleCN: 这项政策在任何人看到草案之前经过了漫长的酝酿期。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the shape of the literal one: something invisible grows at its own pace until it can be shown.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了字面义的形状：看不见的东西按自己的节奏成长，直到可以示人。

intro.en: Gestational is the adjective of gestation, from Latin gestatio 'a carrying', built on gestare 'to carry, carry in the womb', a frequentative of gerere 'to carry, bear'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gestational 是 gestation 的形容词，后者来自拉丁 gestatio「背负」，由 gestare「背负、怀胎」构成，而 gestare 是 gerere「携带、承担」的反复动词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gerere meant 'to carry, bear, conduct', and it also underlies gesture and digest; its deeper ancestry is not settled.
items.cn: gerere 意为「携带、承担、进行」，gesture 与 digest 也由它而来；它更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Gestare is a frequentative of gerere, adding repeated or sustained carrying; the frequentative reading is generally accepted rather than proven by attestation.
items.cn: gestare 是 gerere 的反复动词，加上「反复、持续地背负」的意思；这一反复体解释一般认为是正确的，但并非由书证直接证明。

items.en: Gestatio named the act of carrying, and medical Latin narrowed it to carrying young in the womb.
items.cn: gestatio 指「背负」这一动作，医学拉丁语把它收窄为「在子宫中怀胎」。

items.en: English gestation is recorded from the seventeenth century; the adjective gestational followed much later with the growth of obstetric measurement.
items.cn: 英语 gestation 自 17 世纪有记录；形容词 gestational 则晚得多，随产科测量方法的兴起才出现。

items.en: The suffix -al, from Latin -alis, means 'pertaining to', so gestational simply means 'pertaining to gestation'.
items.cn: 后缀 -al 来自拉丁 -alis，意为「与……有关的」，因此 gestational 就是「与 gestation 有关的」。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date of the adjective): no firm first citation for gestational is available, and the pre-Latin origin of gerere is a reconstruction rather than a documented form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（形容词的首见年代）：gestational 没有可靠的最早书证；gerere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，而非有文献记录的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like gestational but do not share its root; group two holds the medical time words that overlap with it in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近但词根不同的词；第二组是在含义上与之重叠的医学时间词。

entries.definition: A German noun for an organised whole whose parts cannot be understood separately; it has no Latin root and no link to gestation.
entries.definitionCN: 德语名词，指各部分不能分开理解的整体；没有拉丁词根，与 gestation 无关。

entries.definition: From Latin gestura, built on gestus, the past participle of gerere; it shares the root with gestation but means a bodily movement used to express meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 gestura，建立在 gerere 的过去分词 gestus 之上；与 gestation 同根，但指表达意思的身体动作。

entries.definition: Di- 'apart' plus gerere 'carry': to carry food apart inside the body, hence to break it down; the root is shared but the sense is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: di-「分开」加 gerere「携带」：在体内把食物分开搬运，因此指消化；词根相同而词义无关。

entries.definition: Con- 'together' plus gerere: to carry things into one place until they pile up, as blood congests a tissue.
entries.definitionCN: con-「一起」加 gerere：把东西搬进一处直到堆积，如血液使组织充血。

entries.definition: Relating to the period before birth, usually from conception onward; broader than gestational, which measures the carrying period itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生之前的时期，通常自受孕算起；比 gestational 宽，后者只量怀胎这段时长。

entries.definition: The British medical term for care given before birth; it describes services rather than a measurement of age.
entries.definitionCN: 英式医学用语，指产前照护；描述的是服务，而不是孕龄的计量。

entries.definition: Relating to the weeks just before and just after birth; it brackets the delivery rather than covering the whole pregnancy.
entries.definitionCN: 指出生前后数周；框住分娩这一刻，而不覆盖整个孕期。

entries.definition: Relating to the mother; gestational describes the time dimension, while maternal describes the person.
entries.definitionCN: 与母亲有关；gestational 描述时间维度，maternal 描述人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real clinical phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的临床搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: gest- 'carry' + -ation + -al: the carrying period turned into an adjective.
normal.cn: gest-「背负」+ -ation + -al：把「怀着的时期」变成形容词。

normal.en: The same root shows in gesture and digest, both built on Latin gerere 'carry'.
normal.cn: 同一词根见于 gesture 与 digest，二者都建立在拉丁 gerere「携带」之上。

normal.en: Clinical phrases fix the sense: gestational age, gestational diabetes, gestational week.
normal.cn: 临床搭配固定了词义：孕龄、妊娠糖尿病、孕周。

normal.en: The counting starts before conception, which is why gestational age exceeds embryo age.
normal.cn: 计算起点在受孕之前，所以孕龄大于胚胎的实际周数。

normal.en: The family runs gestation, gestate, gestating, gestational.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 gestation、gestate、gestating、gestational。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with one square per week, each square holding a stage of a hidden life.
abstract.cn: 想象一本每周一格的日历，每一格里装着一段看不见的生命阶段。

abstract.en: Picture a pot kept warm on a stove for months before anyone lifts the lid.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在炉上温了几个月的锅，没有人掀开盖子。

abstract.en: Picture a manuscript sealed in a drawer until its author decides it is ready.
abstract.cn: 想象一份手稿被锁在抽屉里，直到作者认为它可以见人。

examples.en: Gestational age is estimated from the last menstrual period.
examples.cn: 孕龄由末次月经推算。

examples.en: She was treated for gestational diabetes in the third trimester.
examples.cn: 她在孕晚期接受了妊娠糖尿病的治疗。

examples.en: The study compared gestational length across mammal species.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了不同哺乳动物的孕期时长。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gest（带）+ ational」——把胎儿一路带着走的时期 → 妊娠期的

root: 拉丁 gestare「背负、怀胎」（gerere「携带」的反复动词）+ -ation + -al；gerere 更早来源属重构形式，gestare 的反复体关系一般认为是正确的。英语 gestational。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of gestational circle one idea: a span of time defined by carrying the young, measured in weeks, split into stages, and finally stretched to cover any slow incubation.
sensesIntro.cn: gestational 的八个义项围绕一个观念：由「怀着幼体」定义的时段，按周计量、按阶段划分，最后延伸去指任何缓慢的酝酿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a week-by-week chart of a hidden life being carried.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张按周记录、承载着看不见生命的表格。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the carrying span is turned into a number of weeks.
branches.cn: 计量：把怀胎时长换算成周数。

branches.en: DEVELOPING YOUNG: the focus moves from carrier to carried, in humans and in other mammals.
branches.cn: 发育中的幼体：焦点从承载者移向被承载者，人也包括其他哺乳动物。

branches.en: CLINICAL MARKS: conditions and structures exist only because the pregnancy exists.
branches.cn: 临床标记：疾病与结构只因妊娠而存在。

branches.en: CARRYING ONLY: a carrier contributes the period, not the genes.
branches.cn: 只承担怀胎：代孕者提供的是时段，而非基因。

branches.en: SLOW EMERGENCE: anything hidden can be said to have a gestational phase.
branches.cn: 缓慢浮现：任何隐藏之物都可以说有酝酿期。

intro.en: Gestational can be read as three pieces: a Latin root for carrying, a noun suffix, and an adjective suffix.
intro.cn: gestational 可以拆成三段读：表「背负」的拉丁词根、名词后缀与形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin gerere 'to carry' yields gestare, gestatio and gestus; English draws gesture, digest, congest and gestation from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gerere「携带」衍生 gestare、gestatio 与 gestus；英语的 gesture、digest、congest 与 gestation 都取自这一词族。

items.structure: gestare (Latin verb, first conjugation, frequentative of gerere)
items.meaning: to carry, to carry in the womb
items.example: The root supplies the idea of sustained carrying.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「持续背负」的意思。

items.meaning: the act or state of doing something
items.example: Gestation names the act of carrying.
items.exampleCN: gestation 指「背负」这一动作。

items.example: Gestational means pertaining to gestation.
items.exampleCN: gestational 意为与 gestation 有关的。

items.meaning: the carrying of young in the womb
items.example: Gestation lasts about nine months in humans.
items.exampleCN: 人类的妊娠约持续九个月。

items.meaning: to carry young, or to develop slowly
items.example: The plan gestated for years before it was announced.
items.exampleCN: 这项计划在公布前酝酿了多年。

items.example: The gestating embryo was visible on the scan.
items.exampleCN: 正在发育的胚胎在扫描图像上可见。

items.example: The infants were grouped gestationally rather than by birth weight.
items.exampleCN: 这些婴儿按孕龄而非出生体重分组。

items.meaning: the standard clinical measure of pregnancy length
items.example: Gestational age is reported in completed weeks.
items.exampleCN: 孕龄以整周数报告。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry, carry in the womb

definition_zh: 在经济上；从经济角度；节约地；以低成本方式；在资源使用效率上；在经济上处于某种状况（如贫困、活跃）；有利可图地；经济上依赖地
definition_en: with respect to the economy or to cost, or in a manner that avoids waste of money, time, or resources
core_image: 一个人左手提着满袋的特价菜，右手拿着账本，两条路都走向同一个收银台
scene: 这里指「在经济上」。 With a bag of discounted vegetables in one hand and a ledger in the other, he walks to the same checkout. He shops economically, buying discounted vegetables and entering every price in the ledger.
sceneCN: 这里 economically 是「在经济上、从花费角度」（第 3 个义项：在成本上）；句意：他一手提打折蔬菜，一手记账，按经济划算的方式采购。图中可辨识物件：特价蔬菜袋、账本、收银台、价签、计算器。

pos.zh: 在经济上；节约地；以低成本方式

collocations.zh: 经济活动人口中的（有工作或求职的）

senses.title: Thriftily: with little waste of money
senses.definition: in a way that spends money carefully and avoids waste
senses.definitionCN: 以谨慎花钱、避免浪费的方式
senses.example: They lived economically and saved for the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 他们节俭度日，为修屋顶攒钱。
senses.why: Economically is economic plus -ally. Because economic and economical both descend from Greek oikonomia 'household management', the adverb can carry either 'of the economy' or 'without waste'.
senses.whyCN: economically 是 economic 加 -ally。由于 economic 与 economical 都出自希腊语 oikonomia“家务管理”，这个副词既能带“经济上的”义，也能带“不浪费地”义。

senses.title: In economic terms: as measured by the economy
senses.titleCN: 在经济上：按经济指标衡量
senses.definition: with reference to economic activity, output, or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 参照经济活动、产出或状况而言
senses.example: The two regions are economically very different.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个地区在经济上差别很大。
senses.why: Here -ally marks a point of view rather than a manner: the sentence looks at the region through an economic lens. This is the adverb's most common academic use.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 -ally 标记的是视角而非方式：句子透过经济这只镜头看这个地区。这是该副词最常见的学术用法。

senses.title: Cost-wise: in terms of price or outlay
senses.titleCN: 在成本上：就价格或开支而言
senses.definition: with respect to the cost of producing or obtaining something
senses.definitionCN: 就生产或获取某物的花费而言
senses.example: The plan is economically attractive but technically risky.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案在成本上有吸引力，技术上却有风险。
senses.why: Cost is the individual's version of the economy's budget. The adverb moves easily between a household ledger and a national accounts table.
senses.whyCN: 成本是个人版的“经济预算”。这个副词可以自如地在家用账本与国民账户之间移动。

senses.title: Resource-efficiently: using less to do more
senses.titleCN: 资源高效地：用更少做更多
senses.definition: in a manner that obtains a result with minimal material or energy input
senses.definitionCN: 以最少的材料或能量投入取得结果的方式
senses.example: The engine runs more economically at a steady speed.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机在稳定速度下运行更省。
senses.why: The adverb can modify a process rather than a person: running economically means the machine's input-output ratio is good, which is thrift expressed as engineering.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词可以修饰过程而非人：运行得 economically，就是机器的投入产出比好，也就是以工程语言表达的节俭。

senses.title: Profitably: so that the numbers work
senses.titleCN: 有利可图地：账算得过来
senses.definition: in a way that can be sustained financially or is worth the investment
senses.definitionCN: 在财务上可持续、或值得投入的方式
senses.example: The mine can operate economically only at high ore prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这座矿只有在矿石价格高时才能在经济上维持运营。
senses.why: Viability is thrift at the scale of a firm: what cannot cover its costs is not economical to run. The adverb here means 'so that costs are covered'.
senses.whyCN: 可行性是“企业尺度上的节俭”：覆盖不了成本的事，就不值得做。这个副词在此意为“在成本能被覆盖的前提下”。

senses.title: Economically disadvantaged: short of money
senses.definition: having low income or few material resources, as a social category
senses.definitionCN: 作为社会类别，指收入低或物质资源少
senses.example: The programme targets economically disadvantaged students.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目面向经济上处于弱势的学生。
senses.why: In policy language the adverb avoids naming poverty directly: it describes the dimension in which the disadvantage lies. The euphemism is precise about the axis, vague about the level.
senses.whyCN: 在政策语言中，这个副词避免直接说“贫穷”，而描述弱势所在的维度。这种委婉对“轴”很精确，对“程度”则含糊。

senses.title: Economically active: in the labour force
senses.titleCN: 经济活动人口：在劳动力中
senses.definition: engaged in or seeking paid work, as defined by labour statistics
senses.definitionCN: 按劳动统计定义，正在从事或寻找有偿工作
senses.example: Only half the adult population is economically active.
senses.exampleCN: 成年人口中只有一半属于经济活动人口。
senses.why: Statistics narrows 'economic' to paid work: caring for a household counts biologically and socially, but not in this measure. The adverb marks the boundary of the definition.
senses.whyCN: 统计把“经济的”窄化为有偿工作：家务在生物与社会意义上都算劳动，却不在此项统计内。这个副词标记了定义的边界。

senses.title: Economically dependent: relying on another's income
senses.titleCN: 经济依赖：依靠他人的收入
senses.definition: relying on another person or institution for the means of living
senses.definitionCN: 依靠他人或机构提供生活来源
senses.example: She remained economically dependent on her parents until thirty.
senses.exampleCN: 她三十岁前在经济上一直依赖父母。
senses.why: Dependence is the mirror of household management: someone else holds the purse. The adverb again marks the axis of reliance rather than describing behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 依赖是家务管理的镜像：钱袋握在别人手里。这个副词再次标记依赖的“轴”，而不是描述行为。

intro.en: Economically is economic plus -ally, the adverb ending from Latin -alis plus -e. Economic comes from Greek oikonomikos 'skilled in household management', through Latin oeconomicus. The adverb inherits both the 'of the economy' and the 'thrifty' branches of the family.
intro.cn: economically 是 economic 加 -ally，后者是拉丁语 -alis 加 -e 形成的副词词尾。economic 一般认为出自希腊语 oikonomikos“善于持家的”，经拉丁语 oeconomicus。这个副词同时继承了这一词族的“经济的”与“节俭的”两条分支。

items.en: Policy phrases such as economically disadvantaged and economically active become standard categories in official statistics.
items.cn: economically disadvantaged、economically active 等政策短语成为官方统计的标准类别。

items.en: Economic and economical settle into their modern division, and the adverb follows both: 'in economic terms' and 'without waste'.
items.cn: economic 与 economical 稳定为现代分工，副词也随之两用：既可表“在经济上”，也可表“不浪费地”。

items.en: Economic and economy enter English from Latin and Greek sources; the adverb ending -ally is added later in the usual way.
items.cn: economic 与 economy 自拉丁与希腊来源进入英语；副词词尾 -ally 随后按常规加上。

items.en: oikonomikos 'skilled in managing a household' is built on oikos 'house' plus nomos 'managing'. The adverb's two senses both descend from this one skill.
items.cn: oikonomikos“善于持家”由 oikos“房屋”加 nomos“管理”构成。副词的两个义项都源自这一种本领。

items.en: The -ally in economically is -al plus -ly, not a separate suffix '-ally'. The same pattern gives basically and systematically.
items.cn: economically 里的 -ally 是 -al 加 -ly，并不是独立的 -ally 后缀。basically、systematically 也是同样结构。

note.en: The first group separates a same-root twin and a same-root adverb from one different-root neighbour; the second compares words that share only part of the meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分一个同根同族词、一个同根副词和一个不同词根的撞形词；第二组比较只共享部分含义的词。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning 'thrifty'. The adverb economically can express both this sense and the 'of the economy' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 意为“节约的”的形容词。副词 economically 既可表此义，也可表“经济上的”。

entries.definition: in name only, or by nominal value. nomen 'name' is the root, not nomos 'law, managing'.
entries.definitionCN: 名义上地；按名目值地。词根是 nomen“名字”，不是 nomos“法则、管理”。

entries.definition: in a way that unites churches or the inhabited world. It is built on oikoumene, from oikos, with no nomos element.
entries.definitionCN: 以联合各教会或普世的方式。它以 oikos 为基的 oikoumene 构成，没有 nomos 成分。

entries.definition: at low cost. It states the price level, while economically often adds the idea of good management.
entries.definitionCN: 以低价。它陈述价格水平，而 economically 常另含“管得好”的意思。

entries.definition: sparingly, with deliberate simplicity. It sounds more moral and more austere than economically.
entries.definitionCN: 节省地、有意简朴地。它比 economically 更带道德与清苦色彩。

entries.definition: in a way that gives good value for money. It is an evaluated comparison, while economically may simply describe the axis.
entries.definitionCN: 以合算的方式。它是经过评估的比较，而 economically 可能只是说明维度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: economically is economic plus -ally, i.e. -al plus -ly, the ordinary adverb pattern.
normal.cn: economically 是 economic 加 -ally，也就是 -al 加 -ly，普通副词构词法。

normal.en: It has two jobs because the family has two adjectives: economic 'of the economy', economical 'thrifty'.
normal.cn: 它有两份工作，因为这一族有两个形容词：economic“经济的”、economical“节约的”。

normal.en: oikos 'house' plus nomos 'manage' means 'in household-management terms', whether the household is a family or a nation.
normal.cn: oikos“房屋”加 nomos“管理”，意为“按家务管理的说法”，无论这户人家是家庭还是国家。

normal.en: Economically active counts paid work only; housework is outside the statistic.
normal.cn: economically active 只计有偿工作；家务在这一统计之外。

normal.en: nominally is not related: nomen is 'name', nomos is 'law, managing'.
normal.cn: nominally 与它无关：nomen 是“名字”，nomos 是“法则、管理”。

abstract.en: Picture a shopper holding a discount bag and a ledger: two ways of watching the same money.
abstract.cn: 想象一位顾客一手提着打折菜、一手拿着账本：两种盯住同一笔钱的方式。

abstract.en: The same adverb measures a household, a region, an engine, a mine, a student, a worker, and a dependent adult.
abstract.cn: 同一个副词可以衡量一个家庭、一个地区、一台发动机、一座矿、一名学生、一位劳动者、一个受赡养的成年人。

abstract.en: Every sense asks which ledger is open: spending, output, price, resources, or dependence.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在问：翻开的是哪一本账——支出、产出、价格、资源，还是依赖关系。

examples.en: The factory now runs more economically than it did last year.
examples.cn: 这家工厂现在比去年运行得更省。

examples.en: The province is economically dependent on one crop.
examples.cn: 该省在经济上依赖单一作物。

examples.en: Economically, the proposal makes sense; politically, it does not.
examples.cn: 从经济上看，这个提案说得通；从政治上看则不然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一口弄米扣利」——一口锅弄米还扣着利，处处算得省 → economically 在经济上、节约地

root: 希腊语 oikonomikos“善于持家”＝oikos“房屋”＋nomos“管理”；经拉丁语 oeconomicus 入英语作 economic，加 -ally（-al＋-ly）成 economically。核心是“按一本账来衡量或行事”。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses point at a ledger. What changes is which ledger — the household's spending, the region's output, a project's cost, a machine's resources, a firm's viability, a student's income, the labour force, or a dependent's support.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指向一本账。变化的只是哪一本账——家庭支出、地区产出、项目成本、机器资源、企业可行性、学生收入、劳动力、被赡养者的生活来源。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shopper with a discount bag in one hand and a ledger in the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位顾客一手提着特价菜，一手拿着账本。

branches.en: MANNER: the adverb describes how money or energy is spent — carefully, with little waste.
branches.cn: 方式：这个副词描述钱或能量如何被花——谨慎地、少浪费地。

branches.en: VIEWPOINT: the adverb names the lens or axis — economic terms, cost terms — rather than a manner.
branches.cn: 视角：这个副词命名镜头或维度——经济口径、成本口径——而不是方式。

branches.en: VIABILITY: at firm scale, 'economically' means costs can be covered.
branches.cn: 可行性：在企业尺度上，economically 意为成本能被覆盖。

branches.en: SOCIAL AXES: disadvantage and dependence are located on the economic axis, not described as behaviour.
branches.cn: 社会维度：弱势与依赖被定位在经济这一轴上，而不是被描述为行为。

branches.en: STATISTICAL BOUNDARY: 'economically active' marks paid work as the edge of the measure.
branches.cn: 统计边界：economically active 把有偿工作标为该测量的边界。

intro.en: Economically is economic plus -ally. The ending is -al (adjective, Latin -alis) plus -ly (adverb, Old English -līce); it is not a single suffix '-ally'.
intro.cn: economically 是 economic 加 -ally。词尾是 -al（形容词后缀，拉丁语 -alis）加 -ly（副词后缀，古英语 -līce），并非单一的 -ally 后缀。

latinIntro.en: The base is Greek oikonomia through oikonomikos and Latin oeconomicus: oikos 'house' plus nomos 'managing'. The adverb inherits both the economic-science and thrift branches.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是经 oikonomikos 与拉丁语 oeconomicus 而来的希腊语 oikonomia：oikos“房屋”加 nomos“管理”。副词继承“经济科学”与“节俭”两条分支。

items.meaning: in economic terms, or without waste
items.meaningCN: 在经济上；节约地（-al＋-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The mill is economically marginal.
items.exampleCN: 这家磨坊在经济上处于边缘。

items.example: Economic policy shapes household budgets.
items.exampleCN: 经济政策塑造家庭预算。

items.example: An economical lamp uses less power.
items.exampleCN: 省电的灯耗电更少。

items.meaning: the system of production and consumption; thrift
items.example: The economy grew by two percent.
items.exampleCN: 经济增长了百分之二。

items.example: We must economize on water this summer.
items.exampleCN: 今年夏天我们必须节约用水。

items.example: The economist warned of inflation.
items.exampleCN: 这位经济学家警告通胀风险。

items.meaningCN: 在生态上（同 oikos 词基的平行副词）
items.example: The marsh is ecologically valuable.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽在生态上很有价值。

items.meaningCN: 自主地；自治地（nomos 指法则）
items.example: The unit operates autonomously.
items.exampleCN: 该单位自主运作。

items.meaning: in name only, by stated value
items.meaningCN: 名义上地（词根为 nomen“名字”，与本词无关）
items.example: He is nominally in charge.
items.exampleCN: 他名义上负责。

items.meaningCN: 基本上（同样是 -al＋-ly 结构）
items.example: The two plans are basically the same.
items.exampleCN: 这两个方案基本相同。

latinEntries.meaningCN: economic 所本的拉丁语形容词
